Position Summary: The Tsagaratou Laboratory, in the Department of Genetics and the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, studies how epigenetic regulators – in particular the TET family of DNA dioxygenases – control the development, lineage identity and effector function of conventional T cells and of innate-like T cells such as iNKT cells. The laboratory uses conditional knockout mouse models, multiparameter flow cytometry, primary cell culture and genomic/epigenomic profiling to determine how the loss of these regulators reshapes immune cell identity and the response to pathogens and to cancer, and extends these findings to engineered cell ( CAR ) immunotherapy. The Research Technician will provide day-to-day experimental support for these projects and will take ownership of experiments from the bench through data analysis. Primary duties include assisting in mouse colony management, genotyping, dissection of mice and isolation of primary lymphocytes from various organs; antibody staining, sample acquisition on multicolor flow cytometers and FACS sorting; primary cell culture, retroviral transduction and adoptive transfer into recipient mice; DNA and RNA isolation and preparation of samples for downstream molecular and sequencing analysis; and analysis, quality control and presentation of the resulting data. After training, the incumbent is expected to execute experiments independently, to troubleshoot protocols, to maintain detailed and reproducible records, and to present their own results at lab meetings and journal clubs. The position also includes reagent ordering and inventory, routine equipment upkeep, compliance with IACUC and Environment, Health and Safety requirements, and training other laboratory members in techniques the incumbent has mastered. This is a mentored position well suited to a candidate preparing to apply to graduate or medical school. The incumbent will be trained directly by the Principal Investigator, will be supported in developing independent technical and analytical skills, and is expected to contribute to peer-reviewed publications.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Management Preferences: Demonstrated hands-on experience working with laboratory mice, colony management, breeding set-up, ear tagging, PCR genotyping, dissection or isolation of primary cells Demonstrated experience with multicolor flow cytometry or FACS sorting, including antibody panel set-up, compensation controls, instrument operation or data acquisition Demonstrated experience with primary cell culture or viral transduction, including retroviral or lentiviral production Demonstrated experience with standard molecular biology techniques, including DNA or RNA isolation Demonstrated ability to analyze and present one’s own experimental data together with accurate, reproducible record keeping
Special Physical/Mental Requirements: -Ability to work safely with biological materials -The work requires fine motor control, manual dexterity, and sustained visual concentration at a microscope -Requires standing or sitting for extended periods. The incumbent must be able to move up to 25 pounds. -Duties to be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Assistant Study Coordinator
description: The Assistant Study Coordinator will work in tandem with the Cellular Therapeutics POD's study coordinators to carry out basic elements of the conduct of the POD's clinical trials, including subject and data management. The Assistant Study Coordinator will work to ensure the delivery of quality research and patient safety by adhering to regulatory compliance standards, as dictated by federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and local and institutional policies related to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Protocol Office; safeguarding institutional integrity. This position may require holidays, weekend and evening coverage as needed based upon clinic schedules and business need.

title: Open Rank - Neuroengineering Cluster- Assistant/Associate/Full Professor
description: The Division of Data Science and Society (DSS) at UNC-Chapel Hill's School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) is excited to announce an open-rank tenure-track faculty position as part of the University's neuroengineering cluster hire initiative. This cluster unites the Lampe Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering, the Department of Computer Science, the Department of Neurosurgery, and DSS to build a collaborative, interdisciplinary hub in neuroengineering, focused on brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), brain function imaging and interpretation, closed-loop neuromodulation, and the translation of neuroengineering innovations into improved human health. Within this cluster, the DSS position will provide leadership in machine learning, statistical, and AI frameworks that transform complex large-scale, multi-modal neuroscience and behavioral data into clinically relevant insights, addressing core challenges of heterogeneity, dimensionality, harmonization, and data governance. This position complements cluster strengths in neuroengineering devices, real-time computing systems, and clinical translation, serving as a link between data acquisition, scientific discovery, and application. The successful candidate will work with cluster faculty to develop and sustain an externally funded research program focused on understanding, predicting, and translating brain function into large-scale neural and behavioral data. Research areas of interest include machine learning and statistical inference for neural data, multimodal neural data integration and harmonization, computational modeling of cognition and behavior, neuroimaging analytics, adaptive neuromodulation, foundation models for neural and behavioral data, and related approaches that advance understanding of brain function and support neurotechnology development. A translational emphasis (such as clinical decision support or neurotechnology deployment) that can position this work to deliver direct, measurable benefits to human health is also desirable. Faculty in this cluster will be recruited with a strong commitment to team science, including joint appointments where appropriate, and coordinated research programs spanning devices, systems, computing, modeling, and translation. Through collaboration among faculty, students, external partners, and the clinical community, the Division of Data Science and Society in SDIS aims to translate research discoveries into tangible societal benefits. We invite you to join the DSS faculty and be part of this mission.

title: Professor of the Practice
description: The Division of Data Science and Society (DSS) at UNC-Chapel Hill's School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) is excited to announce a full-time Professor of the Practice position in data science. This position provides academic leadership for the culminating capstone experience in the school's graduate data science programs - the online Master of Applied Data Science (MADS) and the residential Master of Science in Data Science (MS) - and serves as the faculty lead for MADS. The successful candidate will orchestrate the delivery of the graduate capstone course, serve as instructor of record for the MADS capstone, and teach additional DATA courses in the MADS program as program needs require. Primary responsibilities include: * Orchestrate the delivery of the graduate capstone course by vetting projects in conjunction with the school's Office of Cross-Sector Partnership, overseeing and grading student work, and communicating with the external clients of capstone projects. * Teach a wide range of the DATA courses offered in the MADS program, including the culminating capstone experience, in coordination with other teaching faculty. * Serve on the Admissions Committee for MADS, reviewing candidates who meet program qualifications and making admission decisions. * Collaborate with school staff on curricular improvements to ensure the online program management vendor delivers services that meet university academic standards. * Oversee continuous quality improvement of the curriculum by reviewing instructor and student feedback and implementing changes. * Take an active role in planning and carrying out the optional on-campus immersion held during the summer. * Participate in virtual student recruitment sessions four times a year. Professors of the practice at SDIS bring deep professional and pedagogical expertise into the classroom and play a central role in connecting students with real-world practice. Working closely with teaching faculty, program staff, the Office of Cross-Sector Partnership, and the school's external partners, the Professor of the Practice will ensure that data science master's students complete a rigorous, client-facing capstone experience that translates classroom learning into professional practice. We invite you to join the DSS faculty and be part of this mission.

title: Open Rank - Assistant/Associate/Full Professor
description: The Division of Data Science and Society (DSS) at UNC-Chapel Hill's School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) is excited to announce the fifth year of a strategic open-rank tenure-track faculty hiring initiative. This initiative aims to enhance research and innovation in the rapidly evolving field of data science. We are looking for strong contributors to the areas of data science foundations, the societal impact of data science, and applications in the medical, social, physical, biological, and environmental sciences. This initiative seeks to attract exceptional researchers working within or across the following DSS research pillars: * Data: Techniques for collecting, storing, disseminating, and translating data into actionable insights. * Algorithms and Models: Mathematical, computational and statistical tools that empower researchers and stakeholders to discover, create, analyze, present, synthesize, and utilize data. * Applications: Innovative and effective uses of data and models to advance interdisciplinary knowledge and address pressing social issues. * Social Impact: Examination of unintended consequences and ethical questions arising from using data to tackle society's most pressing challenges. UNC-Chapel Hill's interdisciplinary approach to data science research will foster the development of innovative foundational research and applications across various fields. Through collaboration among faculty, students, and external partners, the Division of Data Science and Society in SDIS aims to bridge the gap between academia, industry, and community groups, translating research discoveries into tangible societal benefits. We invite you to join the DSS faculty and be part of this mission.

title: Clinical Instructor
description: The Division of Radiologic Science is recruiting for a faculty member to join our new Ultrasound Program. The faculty member will be responsible for participating and providing support for the development, implementation and evaluation of the philosophy, outcomes, policies, and curricular components of the Sonography program: o Responsible for supervision and evaluation in the clinical setting o Program content and student learning experiences within the curriculum. o Revisions in all course materials and experiences based on curricular changes and refinements and course evaluations. o Effectiveness assessment of curriculum design. o Compliance with accreditation standards and requirements affecting Sonography education. o Active role in accreditation activities. o Teaches and Designs Courses in area(s) where qualified.

title: Study Coordinator
description: This position plays a pivotal role in advancing cancer research and improving patient outcomes by facilitating the conduct of oncology clinical trials in compliance with federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and institutional policies. This position independently manages multiple complex trials throughout their life cycle, including activation, implementation, and closure, under the direction of a Clinical Operations Manager. Key responsibilities include: Recruitment, consent, and enrollment of study participants Coordination of study visits across various clinic settings Documentation of procedures and visits, facilitation of sample collection, and data entry Collaboration with research teams to ensure regulatory compliance and patient safety This position is integral to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Clinical Trials Office, maintaining research quality and safeguarding institutional integrity, and driving discoveries that shape the future of cancer care.

title: Public Service Program Associate
description: The Public Service Program Associate provides direct programmatic support and guidance for public service and community engagement at UNC-Chapel Hill. As part of the Carolina Center for Public Service (CCPS) team, the associate works independently with community organizations, faculty, staff, and students to facilitate meaningful, mutually beneficial service-learning and other service and community engagement experiences. This individual ensures that programming aligns with community partner priorities and academic needs and provides guidance in making referrals and connections. The associate provides guidance and information to faculty teaching service-learning courses and to students involved with service-learning and other community experiences, while also supporting CCPS in advancing strategic goals and program outcomes. Acting as a connector across academic, administrative, and community settings, the associate independently ensures effective communication, problem-solving, and coordination for all stakeholders. The role includes interpreting policies and providing logistical and planning support for programming and events. The associate uses a variety of technology and systems to evaluate, support, and monitor service-learning and engagement, track program outcomes, and provide information that supports decision-making, evaluation, and continuous improvement efforts. The program associate also supports personnel and financial administration, coordinating student hiring and HR processes and tracking and monitoring and analyzing program expenses in relation to available funds. Through a combination of relationship management, systems expertise, data oversight, organization, and fiscal support, the Public Service Program Associate builds and sustains high-quality community engagement initiatives that support Carolina's engaged teaching, research, and service. Requires a valid North Carolina driver's license and the ability to meet University requirements to operate University-owned vehicles, including a 12-passenger van, for transportation of students and program-related travel.

description: The position(s) duties include tutoring student-athletes for the Academic Support Program for Student-Athletes in various subject areas. Tutoring will occur in one-on-one and group situations.

description: MPH residential alumni practicum advisors provide concentration-specific practicum support throughout the practicum search, selection, planning, implementation, and evaluation process. Their responsibilities include: - Reviewing SPHG 703 pre-course survey data to understand students' practicum interests, needs, and questions. - Conducting at least one ~30-minute meeting with each student to review their practicum planning document and direct them to resources, opportunities, and connections as appropriate. - Attending SPHG 703 class sessions (select Fridays from 1:25-2:25 p.m.) during the spring term via Zoom. - Responding to student and teaching team emails within 2 business days, excluding holidays and out of office dates. - Hosting office hours to support students as they apply for, interview for, and select practicum opportunities. - Reviewing and providing feedback on the appropriateness and feasibility of learning agreements. - Assisting with practicum tracking and documentation for students in their section. - Reviewing and responding to students' mid-practicum surveys. - Troubleshooting and providing technical assistance during practicum as needed. - Assessing students' practicum products for competency demonstration. - Participating in teaching team meetings. - Participating in practicum quality improvement processes. - In the event a student requests an Incomplete grade in a practicum course, the practicum advisor is responsible for resolving the Incomplete with the student in consultation with the MPH Practicum Director.

title: Center for Women's Mood Disorders Psychologist - Open Rank
description: The Department of Psychiatry at the University of North Carolina (UNC) School of Medicine at Chapel Hill is seeking a fixed term faculty to join the Center for Women's Mood Disorders (CWMD). This position is primarily clinical in nature and will focus on providing evidence-based assessment and psychotherapy services to individuals experiencing mental health concerns during the perinatal period, including pregnancy, the postpartum year, and following pregnancy or infant loss. Clinical services will be delivered primarily through outpatient care settings using both in-person and telehealth modalities. Faculty rank will be commensurate with experience. Primary responsibilities include providing psychotherapy within the Perinatal Behavioral Health Psychotherapy Program and collaborating closely with psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, advanced practice providers, trainees, and other members of a multidisciplinary team. The faculty member will provide assessment and treatment for a broad range of perinatal mental health concerns, including mood and anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive and related disorders, trauma-related conditions, adjustment concerns, and other reproductive mental health conditions. Experience working with individuals undergoing fertility treatment and those experiencing reproductive mental health challenges such as premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) and perimenopausal mental health concerns is highly desirable. This position may include teaching and supervision responsibilities within the department's training programs. The faculty member may provide clinical supervision to psychology interns, psychology fellows, practicum students, psychiatry residents, social work trainees, and other interprofessional learners. Additional teaching activities may include participation in seminars, case conferences, and didactic programming related to perinatal and reproductive mental health. Faculty are expected to contribute to the academic mission of the department through excellence in clinical care, education, service, and scholarly activity. Participation in program development, quality improvement initiatives, clinical research collaborations, and other scholarly endeavors is encouraged. The ideal candidate will demonstrate expertise in evidence-based psychotherapies for individuals in the perinatal period, including behavioral interventions such as Behavioral Activation and Exposure and Response Prevention, as well as third-wave behavioral approaches such as Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT). Candidates should possess strong interpersonal skills, a commitment to patient-centered and culturally responsive care, and the ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams.

title: Dental Technician
description: The primary purpose of the Dental Technician is to provide advanced dental laboratory technology expertise in support of patient care, education, and restorative and prosthodontic programs within the Adams School of Dentistry. The Dental Technician independently performs complex and highly specialized dental laboratory procedures utilizing conventional and advanced digital dentistry technologies, including CAD/CAM design and manufacturing, milling, 3D printing, and other evolving fabrication technologies. The Dental Technician applies comprehensive knowledge of dental anatomy, restorative materials, laboratory equipment, fabrication techniques, and digital workflows to evaluate complex case requirements and determine appropriate technical approaches. The position designs and fabricates complex dental restorations, appliances, surgical guides, and other prosthodontic products; troubleshoots design and fabrication issues; makes appropriate adjustments to product designs and fabrication processes; and develops innovative technical solutions based on clinical specifications and individual case requirements. The Dental Technician also serves as an advanced technical resource to faculty, residents, and students regarding dental laboratory procedures, materials, equipment, digital workflows, and fabrication techniques. The position provides instruction and consultation on complex conventional and digital dental technologies and develops educational materials to support the integration of dental technology into restorative education and clinical practice. The Dental Technician works under the direction of the Lead Dental Technician and collaborates with faculty, residents, students, and other School partners to support the quality and effectiveness of dental laboratory services.

title: Video Production Specialist
description: The Video Production Specialist reports to the Multimedia Team Lead and serves as a key visual storyteller for the University. This role will create compelling video content that advances institutional priorities, expands reach and strengthens the Carolina brand. This position researches, plans, captures, edits and publishes platform-specific video content that tells authentic, engaging stories about the University's people, research, teaching and impact. Working collaboratively with colleagues in University Communications and Marketing, this position develops high-impact, quick-turn video content, producing short-form videos, motion graphics and other digital assets optimized for social media, web and emerging digital platforms. This position will be expected to meet strict editorial deadlines, including producing b-roll and video interviews for media outlets as well as producing timely content for event coverage. In addition, this position will provide video support for executive communications' social media channels that amplify the Chancellor, senior leaders and other institutional priorities. The Video Production Specialist will be expected to have sound editorial judgement, identify emerging storytelling opportunities and adapt content quickly to real-time events and conversations while maintaining the University's brand standards and reputation.

title: Open Rank Faculty
description: The Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine is seeking a board certified or board eligible Pulmonary Medicine physician with expertise in the management of patients with sarcoidosis as well as other advanced airways diseases including COPD and asthma. The ideal candidate will provide high quality, patient centered care in both outpatient and inpatient settings, contribute to and lead multidisciplinary disease specific clinical and research programs, and participate in the rotation schedule for the inpatient pulmonary consult services.

title: Open Rank, Kenan-Flagler Business School
description: The Kenan-Flagler Business School at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking to hire qualified individuals to perform teaching, research, and/or service at the academic ranks of Adjunct Professor, Adjunct Associate Professor, Adjunct Assistant Professor, Adjunct Instructor, or Professor of the Practice; depending on education and experience. The successful candidate will be a creative and effective teacher capable of contributing to courses focused on private wealth management and investments.

title: Faculty Physician / Clinician Educator (Chatham Hospital)
description: The Department of Family Medicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, in partnership with UNC Health and Chatham Hospital, seeks a Family Medicine or Emergency Medicine Physician for the UNC Chatham Hospital Emergency Department. UNC Chatham Hospital is a 25-bed rural Critical Access Hospital located in Siler City, NC, approximately 30 miles from Chapel Hill. The newly renovated 15-bed ED sees approximately 18,000 visits annually and is staffed by Family Medicine and Emergency Medicine physicians and advanced practice providers. This is an excellent opportunity to join a diverse and energetic group of physicians providing emergency care to a rural community. The ED team is supported by advanced practice providers, telepsychiatry services, on-site interpreter services, a system transfer center, and UNC AirCare. We use Epic as our EHR with AI-powered documentation support. CT and ultrasound are available daily, with MRI available five days per week. Bedside ultrasound and GlideScope are also available. The Maternity Care Center is staffed 24/7 with cesarean section capability, and cardiology and general surgery consultants are readily available. Physicians in the ED practice group are employed through the UNC Department of Family Medicine, consistently ranked a top academic family medicine program in the United States. Our mission is to provide outstanding, compassionate health care to the surrounding rural community. The ED serves as a training site for medical students, residents, and fellows. Faculty interested in academic advancement have opportunities for professional development across the department's missions, including teaching, clinical excellence, research, and administration. The position offers flexible scheduling options with a mix of day, evening, and overnight shifts. Full-time equivalent is 1520 hours annually. The manageable patient volume allows for meaningful patient interactions while maintaining work-life balance in a collegial, team-based environment. Faculty rank and salary are commensurate with qualifications and experience. The position includes excellent UNC faculty physician benefits and clinical incentive pay. Benefits include: Competitive salary with clinical incentive compensation Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance Generous retirement contributions (UNC system) Paid time off and CME allowance Professional liability coverage Opportunities for academic advancement

title: Research Assistant Professor
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Center of Excellence for Eating Disorders (UNC CEED), established in 2003, is seeking candidates for a fixed-term Research Assistant Professor position in the Department of Psychiatry. The candidate will dedicate the majority of their time to research, specifically pursuing an active program of externally funded research (K- or R- level or equivalent) and actively and effectively pursuing and achieving publication in appropriate scholarly venues. Additionally, the successful candidate will offer a rich training environment for PhD students and post-doctoral fellows along with training and supervision of behavioral health trainees (including clinical psychology interns and psychiatry residents). This role also includes lectures to medical students and trainees in psychology, psychiatry, pediatrics, and other specialties. They will participate in the CEED Summer Research Fellow program, mentoring promising junior investigators in the field. Clinical responsibilities may include assessment and treatment services to children and families in inpatient and outpatient settings. We are seeking a candidate to contribute to the future vision and direction of CEED, who is passionate about advancing the science of eating disorders. CEED is world-renowned for excellence in research, treatment, and training in eating disorders. Our research goals are to develop a deeper understanding of the causes of eating disorders and to create more effective diagnostic, treatment, and prevention strategies.

title: Reproductive Psychiatrist - Open Rank
description: The UNC Department of Psychiatry is seeking a full-time reproductive psychiatrist (MD/DO) to join the Center for Women's Mood Disorders. Since its founding in 2004, the Center has been committed to delivering outstanding clinical care, scientific discovery, training the next generation of investigators and clinicians, and informing policy in women's reproductive mood disorders. The Center is the primary referral resource in North Carolina for perinatal patients with complex psychiatric illness, and it operates a dedicated Perinatal Psychiatry Inpatient Unit. Demand for the program's services continues to grow with many referrals from OB-GYN, family medicine, and statewide partners. The successful candidate will provide specialty outpatient care across the female reproductive lifespan, including perinatal mood and anxiety disorders, perimenopausal depression, and menstrually-related mood disorders; contribute to inpatient care on the Perinatal Psychiatry Inpatient Unit; participate in the NC-MATTERS statewide consultation line, extending reproductive psychiatry expertise to clinicians across North Carolina; supervise psychiatry residents and trainees within the Women's Mood Disorders clinical services; and participate in the research program of the Center. This is a fixed term faculty position. Rank will be determined based on the experience and qualifications of the candidate. This position is in person, with a limited hybrid component for the NC-MATTERS consultation line and administrative work.

title: Open Rank
description: Position Description The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a full time, fellowship trained Interventional Radiologist to join the Interventional Radiology Division. This position supports the department's clinical, educational, and academic missions within a high volume, tertiary care academic medical center. The Interventional Radiology Division performs a broad range of vascular and non-vascular procedures and provides CTA and MRA interpretation. Divisional clinical strengths include interventional oncology, treatment of vascular malformations, portal hypertension, venous disease interventions, women's health, and solid organ transplant-related interventions. The division maintains an independent outpatient clinic, an inpatient admitting service, and provides procedural services for a local outpatient dialysis access center. Clinical care is delivered across multiple state of the art locations, including nine interventional procedure suites with a 16 bed pre and post procedure holding area at UNC Memorial Hospital in Chapel Hill, two interventional procedure suites with a nine bed holding area at Hillsborough Hospital, onsite Interventional Radiology services at UNC Health Johnston locations in Smithfield and Clayton supporting both inpatient and outpatient populations, and an office based laboratory in Chapel Hill. The division supports comprehensive training for Integrated Interventional Radiology, Independent Interventional Radiology, and Diagnostic Radiology residents through a high procedural case volume. Position Responsibilities Perform image guided vascular and non vascular interventional radiology procedures using ultrasound, fluoroscopy, and CT guidance Provide clinical care across inpatient, outpatient clinic, admitting service, dialysis access, and office based laboratory settings Interpret CTA and MRA studies as part of the clinical service Perform a wide range of interventional procedures, which may include image guided biopsies; venous access procedures; thermal tumor ablation (microwave and cryoablation); chemoembolization and radioembolization; vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty; uterine artery embolization; prostatic artery embolization; and endovenous ablation procedures Participate in the education and supervision of Integrated IR, Independent IR, and Diagnostic Radiology residents Collaborate with multidisciplinary clinical teams across medical and surgical specialties Participate in quality improvement, scholarly, or research activities consistent with departmental needs Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications. Flexible work arrangements, including virtual and hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. This position may be eligible for a virtual or hybrid work arrangement, in accordance with UNC policy and subject to approval based on the unit's business needs. title: Open Rank
description: Position Description The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a Cardiothoracic Radiologist to join the Cardiothoracic Imaging Division. This position supports the clinical, educational, and collaborative missions of the department within a high volume academic medical center. The Cardiothoracic Imaging Division is staffed by radiologists with specialized expertise in cardiovascular and thoracic imaging. The division is responsible for interpretation of portable and conventional chest radiographs, thoracic computed tomography (CT) examinations, cardiac CT and MRI studies, and the performance of chest fluoroscopy. The service functions in close collaboration with pulmonology, oncology, internal medicine, cardiology, and cardiac and thoracic surgical services. The division also performs image-guided thoracic procedures, including CT-guided lung and mediastinal biopsies, with opportunities for interested faculty to participate in procedural practice. Division faculty participate as integral members of the Multidisciplinary Thoracic Oncology and Interstitial Lung Disease programs and contribute imaging expertise to coordinated diagnostic evaluation and treatment planning. Faculty are also involved in education and academic activities across the department. Position Responsibilities Interpret cardiothoracic imaging studies, including chest radiographs, thoracic CT, and cardiac CT and MRI studies Perform and/or supervise chest fluoroscopy as part of the clinical service Participate in multidisciplinary clinical care through collaboration with pulmonology, oncology, cardiology, internal medicine, and cardiac and thoracic surgical services Contribute imaging expertise to multidisciplinary conferences and programs, including the Multidisciplinary Thoracic Oncology Program Teach and mentor diagnostic radiology residents, chest imaging fellows, and medical students Participate in quality improvement, scholarly, or academic activities consistent with departmental needs Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

title: Admin Support Associate
description: The Institute for Global Health and Infectious Diseases (IGHID) seeks a Front Desk Administrative Support Associate to provide professional administrative support to faculty and staff. This position ensures smooth office operations, enabling faculty and staff to focus on patient care, research, and teaching. Serving as the first point of contact for the Institute, this role is responsible for maintaining a welcoming and professional office environment. The Administrative Associate manages the reception area, provides general administrative and clerical support, coordinates daily office activities, and ensures effective workflow and communication throughout the department. Key responsibilities include greeting visitors, verifying identities, issuing and tracking badges, managing phone, pagers, and email communications, distributing mail, scheduling appointments, coordinating meetings and travel, and assisting with document preparation. The position also ensures compliance with office security and HIPAA requirements, exercising discretion and confidentiality when handling sensitive information and correspondence. Much of the work involves detailed, procedural, and routine administrative tasks that play a vital behind-the-scenes role in supporting research operations. The work directly supports physician-scientists engaged in discovery and innovation that shape public health policy, healthcare delivery, and disease prevention. This position offers a unique opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to improving global health outcomes through exceptional administrative excellence.

title: Business Officer 1
description: This position serves within the SPAO Pre-Award Research and Support Office and provides professional research administration services to a portfolio of departments and investigators within the School of Medicine. The position manages and administers pre-award activities for sponsored research projects and applies knowledge of sponsor requirements, University policies, and federal regulations to support compliant proposal development and submission. Responsibilities include proposal review, budget development, interpretation of sponsor guidelines, regulatory compliance monitoring, and advising faculty and staff on grant administration requirements. The position analyzes funding opportunities, identifies administrative and compliance issues, recommends appropriate solutions, and exercises independent judgment in managing assigned research administration activities. The position also supports post-award administration activities as needed by providing pre-award specific support, monitors grant-related requirements and deadlines, helps prepare financial and administrative analyses, and collaborates with University offices including OSR, SPA, HR, Finance, the Provost's Office, and the Dean's Office. The role requires knowledge of sponsored research administration, sound decision-making skills, and the ability to independently manage multiple priorities while ensuring compliance with institutional and sponsor requirements.

title: Vehicle/Equipment Operator
description: The purpose of this position is to provide safe and reliable Point to Point (P2P) on-demand and shuttle transportation services to the campus community. This position drives or dispatches for the P2P transportation system operating all sizes of fleet vehicles and the transit dispatching software system. This position drives and or dispatches at varying day and nighttime shifts to ensure transportation services are available for students, staff, and faculty. This position must maintain a valid State of North Carolina Commercial Driver's License with a passenger (P) and air brake endorsement. This position is required to assist passengers with wheelchair access and mobility device access to P2P vehicles. P2P services provided by this position include transportation for ADA, After-Dark, Emergency Ride Back, Campus Health, and special circumstances as identified to support the campus operational needs including services to support campus emergency operations. Additional services include fixed-route shuttle services serving UNC Campus and Franklin Street operating 24/7 excluding holidays and break periods.

title: Social Work Practitioner
description: This position works within the UNC Center for Excellence in Community Mental Health on the Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) Team based in Wake County. ACT consists of professionals from multiple disciplines (including psychiatry, nursing, social work, rehabilitation counseling, and peer support) who use a team approach to meet the needs of individuals with severe and persistent mental illness in community-based settings. ACT works according to a recovery-based philosophy and provides person-centered services addressing the breadth of an individual's needs, helping him or her achieve their personal goals. ACT is generally the first responder and single point of responsibility for meeting the client's needs, which necessitates higher frequency and intensity of services and a low staff-to-client ratio. ACT Social Work Practitioners are responsible for the provision of direct services and coordination for an assigned group of individuals served by the ACT Team, including treatment planning, implementation of interventions using empirically supported approaches, and psychosocial rehabilitation. Area(s) of focus will be based on individual's expertise and skill as well as the needs of the caseload, and could include housing, employment, peer support services, co-occurring disorders, and psychosocial rehabilitation, among others. ACT Social Work Practitioners participate fully in team activities including daily team meetings, regular treatment planning meetings, and participation in the rotation of the on-call phone.

title: Clinical Preceptor
description: The Nurse Practitioner Preceptor serves as a clinical mentor and educator for graduate nursing students, providing hands-on learning experiences in a real-world healthcare setting. Preceptors play a vital role in supporting the clinical education, professional development, and competency of future nurse practitioners while collaborating with faculty to ensure student success. Key Responsibilities * Provide supervised, real-world clinical learning experiences for nurse practitioner students. * Offer guidance, mentorship, and clinical expertise to support students' development of diagnostic reasoning, assessment, and patient management skills. * Facilitate progressive student independence by assigning appropriate patient care responsibilities based on competency. * Review and approve student findings, diagnoses, and treatment plans prior to patient discharge. * Communicate regularly with assigned faculty regarding student progress, concerns, or questions. * Complete required student evaluations at mid-term and end of the clinical rotation. * Maintain a supportive and professional learning environment that promotes compassionate, high-quality patient care Clinical supervision ranging from approximately 60–240 hours per semester, depending on course requirement

title: Youth Behavioral Health Hospital Medical Director
description: The Department of Pediatrics seeks to hire a faculty member to join the Division of General Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine (GPAM) at the University of North Carolina. This position combines outpatient adolescent medicine clinical care, leadership responsibilities within the Youth Behavioral Health Hospital (YBH), and participation in YBH clinical call coverage. This is a full-time (1.0 FTE), fixed term faculty position appointed in the School of Medicine at UNC Chapel Hill. Clinical and administrative effort will be distributed as follows: Outpatient Adolescent Medicine Provide consultative care for adolescents with a wide range of medical, behavioral, and psychosocial needs. Deliver evidence-based adolescent health services within a multidisciplinary, team-based care environment. Collaborate with physicians, advanced practice providers, and behavioral health professionals to support high-quality patient care. Youth Behavioral Health Clinical Coverage Provide medical care and consultation for children and adolescents receiving services at the Youth Behavioral Health Hospital. Evaluate and manage acute and chronic medical conditions that arise during their stay at YBH. Coordinate with interdisciplinary care teams to support patients' overall health needs and ensure appropriate medical follow-up. Participate in the YBH call pool to address urgent medical concerns and provide clinical guidance related to patient care. Youth Behavioral Health Medical Director Provide physician leadership and medical oversight for healthcare services delivered within the Youth Behavioral Health Hospital Develop and maintain clinical protocols and processes related to the assessment and management of patients' medical needs. Collaborate with operational and clinical leadership to support quality improvement, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and program development. As a faculty member, this person will join a program that includes board certified general pediatricians, adolescent medicine specialists, nurse practitioners, and LCSWs. This position may involve the supervision of medical residents and advanced practice providers; a successful applicant will have a history demonstrating expertise in this set of skills. In addition to clinical programs, the division and institution have important research opportunities. Research interests in the division include the impact of social and contextual factors on health, childhood adversity, and health inequities. The Gillings School of Public Health and the Sheps Center for Health Services Research offer opportunities for broader pediatric and adolescent health research. The GPAM division is one of the largest divisions in the Department of Pediatrics and includes Adolescent Medicine, Primary Care, Complex & Diagnostic Care, and Child Abuse pediatrics. The division has a nationally known and productive research program and faculty in addition to a long record of teaching excellence. The Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill area of North Carolina is an attractive place to live and work with great climate, schools, and both mountains and beach within a day drive.

title: Thrive Advisor
description: The Office of Undergraduate Education seeks a passionate, committed professional to join one of the Thrive@Carolina Campus Hubs, comprised of individuals dedicated to providing student-centered, holistic and seamlessly delivered support to students from acceptance through graduation. Reporting to an Assistant Director, Thrive Advisors provide direct student support to an assigned caseload of students as they unlock their potential, activate their plans, secure their opportunities and build their community. During each academic year, Thrive Advisors will also teach up to 4 sections of a 1-credit hour course, First-Year Thriving, and therefore will need to meet the minimum SACS Accreditation requirements for instruction. Hubs staff bring positive energy and a collaborative mindset to their everyday work, partnering with campus staff, faculty and one another to eliminate barriers to student success and ensure all students thrive. Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others. The successful candidate will have a strong commitment to the liberal arts, a keen understanding and appreciation of utilizing an intersectional framework to support students and demonstrated experience maximizing student engagement through highly effective communications and programming. This is a 12-month, full-time, EHRA Non-Faculty position which will require some evening hours and may have non-standard work hours.

title: Research Associate Professor
description: The primary role of this position is to develop, implement, engage in,support and manage collaborative research projects within the Center for Hybrid Approaches in Solar Energy to Liquid Fuels (CHASE). This Department of Energy sponsored Fuels from Sunlight Energy Innovation Hub, headquartered at UNC-CH with partner institutions at Yale University, Brookhaven National Laboratory, the University of Pennsylvania, North Carolina State University, and Princeton University, will accelerate scientific breakthroughs for advanced energy technology development. Extensive collaboration with researchers across the Center is expected. This position will also interface closely with the senior research scientist who leads the High-Throughput Experimentation in Catalysis (HiTEC) Core Laboratory, to collaboratively advance HiTEC capabilities for characterizing hybrid photoelectrode performance and to ensure all CHASE researchers have advanced instrument capabilities and technical research support. Additionally, the ability to work with and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, as well as postdoctoral scholars, with varying degrees of experience in the laboratory are also essential. The professor will also provide expertise in electrochemistry, photoelectrochemistry, and semiconductor physics to further the department's instructional and research goals. The scope of research may be adjusted to meet specific research needs. There is no expectation to teach for this role. Research Assistant, Associate, or Full Professors must contribute to the missions of the Department, College, and University through strong technical and administrative leadership, through strong research and scholarly activities, and through strong training, and mentoring activities. Administrative duties may include oversight and management of personnel, research services (technical and non-technical), business operations (including overall project budgets), program development, and policy compliance (including relevant university, state, and federal policies). Research and scholarly activities can be varied including contributions to grant applications and publications, development and/or acquisition of new technologies and processes, participation in seminars, lectures, conferences, etc. Training and mentoring activities including instruction of users on state-of-the-art technologies and processes, presentations in courses, participation in seminars and workshops, co-mentoring of students, etc.

title: Senior Financial Analytics & Reporting Analyst
description: INTERNAL ONLY: Internal posting for permanent and SHRA time-limited employees of UNC-Chapel Hill only. This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement that includes a partially remote work location, consistent with System Office policy. UNC-Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. The Senior Financial Analytics & Reporting Analyst serves as the senior individual contributor within the Financial Data Analytics & Reporting team, supporting the development, maintenance, and enhancement of financial reporting, analytics, dashboards, and data solutions that support the University's budget, planning, and operational decision-making processes. The position partners with Finance, Human Resources, ITS, and campus stakeholders to deliver accurate, consistent, and actionable financial information. The role applies advanced analytical expertise to financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, data validation, and business intelligence initiatives. This role requires extensive knowledge of UNC-Chapel Hill financial systems, business processes, and institutional data structures, as well as a comprehensive understanding of how financial and HR data interact to support budgeting, compensation analysis, position management, and long-range financial forecasting. The position routinely integrates information from financial, payroll, and human resources systems to provide a complete view of the University's financial and operational performance. Deep understanding of the University's chartfield structure, funding sources, position funding methodology, budget development processes, and institutional financial controls is essential to ensure the accuracy and consistency of reporting used by campus leadership and external stakeholders. The position must understand how employee and position data flow through payroll, budgeting, and financial systems and how changes in workforce activity affect institutional budgets, forecasts, and financial performance. Because the role supports critical recurring financial reporting, annual budget development, workforce planning, financial forecasting, and executive decision-making, a thorough working knowledge of UNC-Chapel Hill-specific financial and HR processes is necessary to ensure continuity of operations and maintain the integrity of institutional reporting. This position provides expert guidance on financial business processes, reporting requirements, data governance, and interpretation of complex financial and workforce data, enabling campus leaders to make informed decisions based on reliable and consistent information.

title: Director of Faculty Affairs, Academic Operations, and Strategic Priorities
description: This position may be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement that may include a partially remote work location, consistent with System Office policy. UNC Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. The Director of Faculty Affairs, Academic Operations, and Strategic Priorities serves as a senior leader in the Kenan-Flagler Business School Dean's Office responsible for aligning faculty affairs, academic operations, and strategic initiatives across the School. The role provides executive-level support in faculty administration, operational planning, policy development, and institutional reporting in partnership with the Dean of Kenan-Flagler and the Dean's Leadership Team as it relates to faculty, academic operations, and strategic initiatives. As a partner in these areas, the role interfaces with related university offices on behalf of the School. This position converts complex academic, policy, and operational needs into clear processes, actionable analysis, and sustainable systems. The Director advances school priorities by overseeing faculty-related operations, guiding cross-functional implementation, strengthening data-informed decision-making, spearheading strategic initiatives and improving coordination across faculty affairs, programs, and administrative functions.

description: The Adjunct Clinical Instructor contributes to the educational and academic mission of the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery through participation in departmental educational initiatives, professional development activities, and other scholarly endeavors. The individual may provide substantive experience and expertise to support the development and enhancement of educational programs and continuing education opportunities for clinical professionals within the department. Responsibilities include contributing experience and expertise to departmental educational initiatives, supporting professional development and continuing education activities, collaborating with faculty and departmental leadership on educational projects as appropriate, and participating in other academic and educational activities throughout the year and on an as-needed basis in support of the department's mission.

title: Open Rank, Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Physician
description: The Department of Pediatrics at The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC)/ North Carolina Children's Hospital is seeking an individual for a 1.0 FTE, non-tenure track open rank, physician faculty position in the Division of Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine to provide clinical care and contribute to our other missions. Rank and salary will be commensurate with training, experience, and academic accomplishments. The North Carolina Children's Hospital is part of a quaternary care medical center with a 64-bed multidisciplinary Neonatal Critical Care Center (NCCC) that admits over 900 patients per year and supports active pediatric general surgery, pediatric cardiothoracic surgery, newborn airway programs, as well as being the referral center for central and eastern North Carolina. The Division of Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine currently consists of 19 faculty members and 7 fellows who are part of a fully accredited Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Fellowship Program. NIH-funded research projects include the ELGAN-ECHO Study and participation in the NICHD Global Health Network, the Neonatal Research Network, the Pediatric Trials Network, and investigation focused on neonatal intestinal inflammation. Greater Chapel Hill is a two-town, three-county region situated in the center of North Carolina, equidistant to the mountains and the beach, and offers small town charm and big city cultural and athletic events. Our region features one of the best public-school systems in the country, world class health care facilities, and access to one of the best workforces in America. Chapel Hill is a community filled with brilliant minds, award-winning restaurants, innovative businesses, outstanding public schools, and a vibrant music and performing arts scene. This community is considered one of the best college towns in America.

description: This position is a part-time position with the TEACCH Autism Program, located at the Carolina Living and Learning Center (CLLC). Our Direct Support Professionals (DSPs) work directly with our autistic residents with higher support needs. DSPs are charged with assisting our residents to live as fully and as independently as possible. They are not merely caregivers; they provide whatever support is necessary for our residents to thrive. Employees in this position are considered Mandatory Employees of the University, meaning they are required to work during any adverse event that prompts reduced/suspended operations ( such as adverse weather conditions). This position is also a CDME (Communicable Disease Mandatory Employee) as well and required to work during a State of Emergency Order.

title: Study Coordinator
description: This position plays a pivotal role in advancing cancer research and improving patient outcomes by facilitating the conduct of oncology clinical trials in compliance with federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and institutional policies. This position independently manages multiple complex trials throughout their life cycle, including activation, implementation, and closure, under the direction of a Clinical Operations Manager. Key responsibilities include: * Recruitment, consent, and enrollment of study participants * Coordination of study visits across various clinic settings * Documentation of procedures and visits, facilitation of sample collection, and data entry * Collaboration with research teams to ensure regulatory compliance and patient safety This position is integral to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Clinical Trials Office, maintaining research quality and safeguarding institutional integrity, and driving discoveries that shape the future of cancer care.

title: Study Coordinator
description: This position plays a pivotal role in advancing cancer research and improving patient outcomes by facilitating the conduct of multiple complex oncology clinical trials in compliance with federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and institutional policies. This position independently manages multiple complex trials throughout their life cycle, including activation, implementation, and closure, under the direction of a Clinical Operations Manager. Key responsibilities include: * Recruitment, consent, and enrollment of study participants * Coordination of study visits across various clinic settings * Documentation of procedures and visits, facilitation of sample collection, and data entry * Collaboration with research teams to ensure regulatory compliance and patient safety This position is integral to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Clinical Trials Office, maintaining research quality and safeguarding institutional integrity, and driving discoveries that shape the future of cancer care.

title: Applications Analyst
description: The Division of Global Women's Health (GWH) develops the FAMLI App, an iOS/iPadOS Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) application that pairs point-of-care ultrasound probes with embedded AI models to estimate gestational age, fetal weight, and other obstetric outputs in low-resource settings. The app is deployed with research partners on four continents and is being prepared for FDA submission. We are hiring a research software engineer to be the in-house owner of the FAMLI App as its development transitions from an external vendor to our local team. This is the central responsibility of the position: you are the engineer in charge of the app its codebase, its releases, and its day-to-day evolution. Around that core, the role includes maintaining our companion research data-collection app (Flutter/Dart with a native iOS layer), keeping our self-hosted research web tools running (including the image-annotation and QC platform our sonographers use), and providing engineering support to the machine-learning team integrating their models on-device and handling conversion and validation. Model research and ML direction are led by others; your work is engineering in support of their pipeline. This is a hands-on role covering the full stack of a deployed medical device application, working directly with clinicians, sonographers, ML scientists, and international research partners on production software deployed in active research.

title: Scheduling Specialist
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks a Scheduling Specialist within the Office of the University Registrar (OUR) to support the administration, coordination, and continuous improvement of the University's academic scheduling and classroom space management operations. Reporting to the Assistant Registrar for Scheduling, this position serves as a key operational and technical resource responsible for maintaining the University's schedule of classes, coordinating classroom assignments, and supporting the effective use of instructional space across undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. The Scheduling Specialist partners with academic departments and campus stakeholders to support course scheduling, classroom utilization, New Student Seat Release, final examination scheduling, and other institution-wide scheduling initiatives that promote student access, degree progression, and operational efficiency. The position also supports the administration of 25Live, SPOTS, and ConnectCarolina through system testing, documentation, training, business process support, and user assistance. Working collaboratively with faculty, Student Services Managers, University Events, the Student Union, ITS, and other campus partners, the Scheduling Specialist interprets scheduling policies, resolves complex scheduling and classroom assignment issues, analyzes classroom utilization data, and recommends process improvements that optimize instructional space, enhance scheduling operations, and support the University's strategic priorities for enrollment growth and student success.

This position serves as one of the Department's two contacts for a variety of granting agencies. Both grant managers are assigned a split of the current faculty research portfolios within the department. This includes ensuring compliance with regulatory agencies. Work performed by the Grants Managers requires a thorough understanding of the types of proposals and mechanisms used by various agencies as well as the terms and conditions of each request for proposal. This knowledge is necessary to interpret rules, regulations, and procedures as well as to plan and direct contracts and grants administration for the department of Health Behavior.

description: THIS POSITION WILL BE LOCATED 80% IN PITTSBORO, NC, AND 20% IN CARRBORO, NC, OR AT OTHER CLINICS STATEWIDE (AS NEEDED). This position is responsible for managing program/operational facilities for the Carolina Living and Learning Center. The position serves as the primary contact for maintenance, grounds, motor fleet, security and housekeeping issues, and is active in providing a proactive plan for addressing maintenance issues. This position is also responsible for performing maintenance to the facility if it falls into the scope of simple repairs or the upkeep of the residential facilities and office space. In addition, this position will oversee the maintenance and related needs of our seven regional clinics across the state as well as our main TEACCH administrative office. This includes responsibility for coordinating any relocation of offices to another space and/or be liaison with the various property managers for leased spaced regarding maintenance needs.

title: Nurse Consultant
description: The purpose of this remote part-time temporary position is to facilitate the conduct of oncology clinical trials, including subject and data management, according to federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and local and institutional policies. These responsibilities relate to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Protocol Office by maintaining the quality of research and by addressing patient safety and regulatory compliance which impact research quality and safeguard institutional integrity. The primary responsibilities of this position include the informed consent process, eligibility and screening, toxicity assessment, patient management, conducting in-services for nurses staff in treating clinic; planning of patient recruitment methods; logistics of patient visits; logistics of obtaining and coordinating clinical samples; specimen collection as needed, enlistment of support of necessary ancillary departments; coordinating the ordering of the required supplies; preparation of study tubes, collecting source documentation; Data entry / management for assigned studies, working with Clinical Research Associates to facilitate data collection for CRFs (case report forms) and/or eCRFs for trials as assigned; prepare and participate in monitoring visits; facilitate pre-site meetings, site initiation meetings, and plan, organize and run protocol start-up meetings. Key responsibilities include: Data coordination Supporting Activation Tasks Clinical Support Provides subject matter expertise and backup support for oncology clinical trial financial and billing compliance, including Epic treatment plans, research billing review, and staff guidance on compliant processes. Collaboration with research teams to ensure regulatory compliance and patient safety This position is integral to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Clinical Trials Office, maintaining research quality and safeguarding institutional integrity, and driving discoveries that shape the future of cancer care.

title: Lead Research Assistant - Tate Lab
description: NOTE: This position is located in Kannapolis, NC, approximately 2 hours from UNC's main campus. Chapel Hill received funding to establish both a targeted Health Care Provider Organization (HPO) for the All of Us Research Program and a Clinical Center (UNC-CC) site for the first ancillary study, Nutrition for Precision Health (NPH). All of Us is a unique research program funded by NIH to build one of the most diverse health databases in history. Nutrition for Precision Health, powered by the All of Us Research Program is a new initiative to develop algorithms that predict individual responses to food and dietary patterns. The NPH Consortium consists of 12 awardees across the US with whom UNC is partnering to implement data collection and analysis. The UNC-CC includes two recruitment/clinical data collection locations, one in Chapel Hill, NC, (UNC-CH), and one in Kannapolis, NC, located at the UNC Nutrition Research Institute (NRI). Come join our team as we work on these innovative studies. Working under the general supervision of the Research Project Managers and Coordinators, this Lead Research Assistant will be responsible for a variety of technical project support duties. Specific duties will vary depending on the needs of the study. We anticipate the primary and secondary duties as noted below, but these may be subject to change over the course of the study. Primary * Communication with study participants for purposes of recruitment, retention, and scheduling * Processing and shipping of biological specimens (blood, urine, saliva, and other specimens) * Data collection including obtaining informed consent, biospecimen collection, study measurements and providing instructions to study participants * Assist with other study activities to ensure the successful completion of the study aims * Assist with participant meal pick-up for the controlled feeding study * Attendance at community events for recruiting and outreach Secondary * Study device software and hardware management * Software system troubleshooting and support * Identification of staff protocol adherence challenge; development and implementation of bi-monthly protocol review sessions * Quality assurance support for scheduling and documentation * Participant and prospective participant educational and promotional material management * Coordination and communication with external services for biological specimens * Chapel Hill site emergency in person support * Phlebotomy support as needed Our goal is to work together as a cohesive team to ensure successful implementation of the study protocols. Additional benefits associated with this position include the opportunity to join a research team that highly values professional development. We will work with the selected candidate to help build the skills and experiences desired to further their individual career goals. Due to the requirements of this position, we anticipate work will be completed on site. The primary location for this position is at the UNC Nutrition Research Institute in Kannapolis, NC with the possibility of providing some support to our other data collection site in Chapel Hill.

This position serves as the Team Lead for the Pre-Award Research Office and Support (PROS) on all pre-award services, responsible for supervision, training, point of contact for escalations, handling the advanced/complex issues, and other related duties.

This position is also responsible for management and reporting activities for all three departments. This position will work closely with the Associate Chair for Administration and department leadership in all departments.

title: Catalog & Curriculum Editor
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks candidates for the position of Catalog & Curriculum Editor in the Office of the University Registrar (OUR). This position will maintain appropriate controls in order to maintain the integrity of all UNC-CH curricular documents and systems. The Catalog & Curriculum Editor will assist with the design and implementation of new catalog and curriculum-related systems, and the creation and editing of university publications. This position will serve as the editorial liaison between University Registrar units, other campus units, photographers, university offices, and external campus partners in the planning, writing, and/or assembly of the Academic Catalog and thoroughly proofread writing, artwork and proofs for quality and accuracy and ensure that corrections are made. This position will partner the Graduate School and Undergraduate Curricula to meet and work with departments to coordinate and manage onboarding of new programs and certificates to the catalog and curriculum related systems. The Catalog & Curriculum Editor may also occasionally assist with the production of the commencement program, if needed. Additionally, the Catalog & Curriculum Editor will coordinate the maintenance of the Master Inventory of Programs informing appropriate staff of approved program changes, including changes in program requirements, degree/major/minor titles, and general education requirements. The Catalog & Curriculum Editor will coordinate the correction of all electronic and printed materials regarding the curriculum and assist as needed with the management and maintenance of the related PeopleSoft tables. The Catalog & Curriculum Editor will manage the editorial duties of the published Undergraduate Catalog and the Graduate Catalog; serve as a resource to campus on other issues related to curriculum, and perform other duties as assigned.

title: Associate Director for Financial Aid Training and Staff Development
description: The Office of Scholarships and Student Aid is seeking an Associate Director for Financial Aid Training and Staff Development to lead the development, coordination, and delivery of comprehensive training and professional development programs for staff across the office. The Associate Director serves as the office-wide training leader and collaborates with Heels Hub One Stop partners to promote consistent, accurate, efficient, and student-centered service. The position serves as a subject matter expert in financial aid policies, procedures, systems, and regulatory requirements and ensures staff have the knowledge, resources, and tools needed to effectively administer financial aid. The Associate Director designs, implements, and evaluates training programs that include new employee onboarding, ongoing professional development, role-specific training, and education related to changes in federal, state, institutional, and operational requirements. The position develops and maintains training materials, process guides, job aids, and reference resources and translates complex regulatory and policy changes into clear, actionable training and communications. The Associate Director assesses training needs, identifies knowledge gaps, and applies adult learning and instructional design principles to support staff development and operational effectiveness. The Associate Director provides direct supervision and leadership to financial aid processing staff, including staff development, workflow management, performance expectations, and operational improvement. The position assists with establishing processing standards, evaluating business processes, and implementing strategies that improve accuracy, efficiency, consistency, and the student experience. The Associate Director works closely with leadership, program teams, Heels Hub partners, and campus stakeholders to strengthen service delivery and ensure staff are prepared to manage complex financial aid processes. The Associate Director oversees summer financial aid administration, including the development, implementation, and evaluation of summer awarding processes. Responsibilities include coordinating awarding practices, developing budgets and resource projections, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements, and collaborating with campus partners to support successful summer enrollment and financial aid administration. The Associate Director applies advanced knowledge of federal, state, and institutional financial aid regulations to advise on complex student situations, including enrollment changes, eligibility considerations, professional judgment, unique circumstances, and policy interpretation. The position may assist with escalated student concerns and provide recommendations that balance student support, compliance, institutional policy, and operational needs. The Associate Director provides professional consultation and support to office leadership and contributes to strategic initiatives that strengthen training, communication, knowledge management, and financial aid operations. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong knowledge of financial aid administration, leadership and supervisory skills, exceptional communication and organizational abilities, and experience designing and facilitating adult learning. The position requires the ability to translate complex information into effective training and operational practices that support staff success, regulatory compliance, operational excellence, and positive student outcomes.

title: Anesthesiologist (Open Rank)
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's Department of Anesthesiology is searching for a General Anesthesiologist (open rank) committed to patient care and Resident education. UNC Hospitals are located on the main campus of UNC Chapel Hill and provide full-service tertiary and quaternary care in a rich academic environment. The department also provides anesthetic care at several community hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers. The physician will be a member of the faculty practice and there are opportunities for scholarly contribution and development.

title: Social Work Practitioner
description: The position will include advanced-level case management and clinical social work services for children and families in the UNC Children's Complex Care Program. This role functions with minimal supervision and serves as the primary social work lead for the most complex cases. Essential functions include: Serving as the primary social work lead for children with medical complexity and high acuity psychosocial needs, exercising advanced clinical judgment and independent decision making. Independently conducting comprehensive psychosocial assessments and developing and implementing treatment plans with minimal review. Acting as a clinical consultant to other social workers, care managers, physicians, and interdisciplinary team members regarding assessment, treatment planning, and management of complex cases. Obtaining, interpreting, and communicating complex psychosocial, medical, and social information to clinical teams to support care planning and clinical decision making. Developing and maintaining collaborative relationships with community health, mental health, and social service agencies, and independently identifying and developing resources to meet patient and family needs. Coordinating and organizing complex care across medical, behavioral health, and community systems. Attending Complex Care Clinic (~2 days/week) to assess new patients and provide follow-up for existing patients. Attending multidisciplinary care conferences as the lead social work representative, providing expert input on psychosocial needs and care plans. Leading or independently contributing to the development and implementation of clinical protocols, family assessment tools, and quality improvement for the Complex Care Program. The position will also involve providing integrated behavioral health/counseling services in the UNC Children's Complex Care Clinic. Essential functions include: Providing evidence based counseling and behavioral health interventions for patients with complex medical and psychosocial presentations. Sessions to be conducted primarily in-person; partial telehealth option available after establishing a patient panel (maintaining roughly 50% in-person). Modifying therapeutic approaches to address high acuity, chronic, or crisis driven behavioral health needs. Coordinating behavioral health care plans with primary care providers and specialty teams, and providing consultation regarding treatment recommendations. Documenting and billing independently and appropriately for clinical services provided.

description: THIS POSTING IS FOR FOUR (4) IDENTICAL POSITIONS (POSITION NUMBERS 00003882, 00055144, 00059451, AND 00058533). BY APPLYING, YOU WILL BE CONSIDERED FOR ALL AVAILABLE POSITIONS.
