Participate in all procedures and treatments of Neurovascular disease, including aneurysmal disease, embolization of AVMs and tumors, treatment of dural arteriovenous fistulas, ischemic disease, including carotid stenosis, and treatment of head and neck cancers and trauma Provide post-procedure evaluation of patients including post op orders and notes Collaborate with multidisciplinary clinical teams across medical and surgical specialties

title: Associate Director for Sheps Integrated Research Solutions (SIRS)
department: Sheps Ctr for Hlth Serv Res - 633100
description: The Associate Director for Sheps Integrated Research Solutions (SIRS) provides strategic, technical, and operational leadership for the Cecil G. Sheps Center for Health Services Research. SIRS designs, builds, and supports secure web-based applications, databases, and workflow systems that enable health services research, multi-site clinical studies, community engagement, evaluation, and quality improvement initiatives. While Sheps(DATA)+ is not a Contract Research Organization (CRO), it functions similarly by providing the full suite of technical, data, and operational infrastructure needed to support health services research, while scientific leadership remains with the Principal Investigator. SIRS is a core component of this integrated service model, contributing to critical application development, data collection platforms, and workflow systems that enable coordinated, multiservice research efforts across the Sheps Center. In this role, the Associate Director is responsible for overseeing the delivery, quality and long-term sustainability of SIRS solutions, ensuring alignment with research goals, institutional policies, security and privacy requirements, and best practices in software engineering and product management. The Associate Director also plays a key role in identifying and advancing strategic initiatives for SIRS that are aligned with Sheps(DATA)+ strategic priorities and the broader mission of the Sheps Center. The Associate Director works closely with Principal Investigators, study teams, Sheps IT leadership, and technical staff to translate complex research workflows into reliable, scalable, secure and compliant digital systems.

description: The Add Health Contracts Coordinator supports the administration of the Add Health restricted-use data program by coordinating researcher access to restricted-use data and ensuring that related contracts, agreements, and access permissions are managed accurately and efficiently. Serving as a primary point of contact for researchers and institutional representatives, this position provides guidance throughout the application and contract process and helps ensure compliance with established data use and data security requirements. Responsibilities include overseeing the online Contracts Management System, facilitating the execution of Data Use Agreements, coordinating researcher access to secure computing environments, supporting Data Hosting Agreement applications, and maintaining records related to contracts and authorized data users. The position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate effectively with a diverse community of researchers and administrative partners.

title: Faculty Physician / Clinician Educator (Chatham Hospital)
description: The Department of Family Medicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, in association with UNC Health Care System, is seeking candidate for a Faculty Physician/ Clinician Educator opening based at Chatham Hospital in Siler City, NC. Chatham Hospital is a critical access hospital with an emergency department, hospitalist and maternity care teaching service entirely staffed by UNC Department of Family Medicine faculty physicians. This is a unique opportunity to join an academically diverse and energetic faculty engaged in the provision of care to a rural population while training the next generation of physicians and other health care providers to provide care to underserved populations. The mission of the UNC Department of Family Medicine is to promote the health of the people of North Carolina and the nation through leadership and innovation in clinical practice, medical education, research and community service. We are concerned with both current needs and future generations, and have a special commitment to the underserved, mothers and children, the elderly and other populations at risk in a time of rapid changes in the organization of health care. Learn more about the Department of Family Medicine at: https://www.med.unc.edu/fammed/ The Faculty Physician/ Clinician Educator positions will be an integral part of the maternity and surgical services at Chatham Hospital. Specific responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: Clinical: The clinical responsibilities will include covering labor & delivery, including surgical coverage; women's health clinic, and women's health surgery. Depending on the applicant's qualifications and training, other clinical responsibilities may include working as a hospitalist, continuity clinic, and/or specialty clinics. Teaching & Education: This will be a rich teaching environment which will include residents, medical students, and fellows. Research: All faculty are encouraged to develop a scholarly interest. Clinical faculty are expected to produce a scholarly product, which may include national presentations and should include manuscript submission, at a rate of one every one or two years. Supervision: This position likely will involve supervision of a midwife, nurse practitioner, and/or physician assistant. Institutional Citizenship: All faculty are expected to work as part of the larger team to improve access, reduce cost, improve quality, and promote efficiency and better health outcomes. You may be requested to engage in community outreach and attend professional events to assist with program development and building professional relationships with referring providers. In addition, attention to timely and complete documentation, patient satisfaction, and referring physician satisfaction are expected of each faculty member in our department. Faculty rank and salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience, plus excellent UNC faculty physician benefits and clinical incentive pay.

Key responsibilities include: Recruitment, consent, and enrollment of study participants Coordination of study visits across various clinic settings Documentation of procedures and visits, facilitation of sample collection, and data entry Collaboration with research teams to ensure regulatory compliance and patient safety This position is integral to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Clinical Trials Office, maintaining research quality and safeguarding institutional integrity, and driving discoveries that shape the future of cancer care.

title: Digital Project Specialist
description: UNC-Chapel Hill's University Communications and Marketing department seeks a digital content specialist to develop and publish content on its digital platforms, unc.edu, The Well and other websites. This is a perfect position for a communications professional who wants to showcase important University initiatives and programs and highlight the expertise of Carolina's world-class faculty and staff. Successful candidates will manage and share content that engages and informs the campus community and positions the University as a vibrant place to teach, learn and work. Part of the editorial and digital production team, the digital content specialist also maintains multiple websites using tools including WordPress and Photoshop. In addition, this position manages the production and distribution of a campuswide e-newsletter through Salesforce. This position will also assist with projects, resources and services that support campus, and will work closely with campus communicators, other University units and outside vendors to coordinate and facilitate these projects. Successful candidates will have excellent writing abilities, experience managing websites, strong organizational skills and the ability to meet deadlines.

title: Adjunct Associate Professor
description: The Division of Speech and Hearing Sciences, Department of Allied Health Sciences, University of North Carolina School of Medicine, invites applications for a faculty position (non-tenure track) in hearing science. Responsibilities include teaching in the Division of Speech and Hearing Sciences.

title: Director of Graphic Design – Men’s Basketball
description: Create social media, web, facility and other graphics for Carolina Men's Basketball that are dynamic and consistent with the Athletic Department's Branding Guidelines. Work with the Director of Men's Basketball Recruiting to determine graphics and social media needs for the program and assist with related photo shoots. Coordinate with the Director of Men's Basketball Recruiting and the Director of Creative Services to develop and plan content calendars. Communicate effectively and consistently with the Director on all graphic design-related activities. Responsible for the creation and distribution of video, graphics, animations and other digital projects within the football program. The purpose of this content is to inform, engage and excite prospective student-athletes and assist Carolina's Athletic Department in their efforts to recruit fans and donors while strategically telling great stories. This position will interface with various internal and external constituencies including, but not limited to, Athletic Communications, Marketing and Promotions, Go Heels Productions and The Rams Club.

title: Tenure/Tenure-Track Faculty
description: The School of Social Work (SSW) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for two (2) open-rank tenure-track faculty (nine-month) positions. By applying, candidates will be considered for all available vacancies. Consistent with the School's mission to advance equity, transform systems, and improve lives, we seek scholars whose research addresses pressing social challenges and advances social well-being through research, teaching, and community engagement. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, substance use prevention and treatment, gender-based and intimate partner violence, and child and family well-being. We also welcome expertise in related areas that may inform prevention and intervention strategies, including social policy and service systems, economic security, behavioral and mental health, and community-based interventions. Candidates whose work demonstrates strong potential for interdisciplinary collaboration, external funding, and the translation of research into practice and policy are especially encouraged to apply. Successful candidates will contribute to the School's nationally recognized missions of research, teaching, and community engagement through the development of rigorous and impactful programs of scholarship that advance social work knowledge, practice, and policy. Faculty appointed to these positions will have opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across the University and with community partners, mentor MSW and PhD students, and contribute to curriculum development and instruction across the School's growing portfolio of academic programs. These positions offer the opportunity to join a highly collaborative faculty committed to translating research into meaningful improvements in the well-being of individuals, families, and communities, and in the public systems that serve them. Competitive applicants will demonstrate a strong record, or clear potential, for externally funded research, peer-reviewed publication, and excellence in teaching. The standard tenure-track teaching load is four courses per academic year, with opportunities for course buy-outs based on research funding, and faculty are expected to engage fully in research, teaching, and service to the School, University, profession, and community. This position has a standard distribution of effort that includes 67% teaching and instruction, 16.5% research, and 16.5% service and community engagement.

title: Seasonal Admissions Reader (Adjunct Assistant Professor)
description: The UNC School of Social Work is seeking Adjunct Assistant Professors to serve as Seasonal Admissions Readers in support of the admissions process for both the online and on-campus Master of Social Work (MSW) programs. Admissions Readers will review and evaluate application materials, participate in components of the admissions review process, and make informed recommendations to the UNC Graduate School regarding admissions decisions. Readers will also assist in identifying highly qualified applicants for School-based scholarship and funding opportunities. This is a seasonal, temporary position that requires an average of approximately 5 hours per week during the admissions review cycle. Selected candidates will receive training prior to the review period and will complete structured evaluation forms for each assigned application. The primary goal of this role is to provide thorough, consistent, and equitable assessments that support the MSW Admissions Committee in selecting a talented and diverse student cohort across both program formats. This position is fully remote.

title: Adolescent Medicine Specialist
description: The Department of Pediatrics seeks to hire an Adolescent Medicine physician to join the Adolescent Medicine Section in the Division of General Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine (GPAM) at the University of North Carolina. Applicants should be board-certified or board-eligible in Adolescent Medicine. This position is an open-rank, open track faculty position appointed in the School of Medicine at UNC Chapel Hill. As a faculty member, this individual will join a section that includes board certified Adolescent Medicine physicians, nurse practitioners, LCSWs, and other pediatricians with interest in adolescent health. This individual will provide outpatient care at Raleigh and/or Chapel Hill clinical settings. Inpatient consultative care is delivered on an as-needed basis with plans for expansion as the section grows. Additionally, the Adolescent Medicine section includes opportunities to provide medical care at youth detention centers and a youth psychiatric inpatient facility. Members of the section also collaborate in a Hematology-Adolescent Medicine clinic to provide reproductive healthcare for patients with possible bleeding disorders and other hematologic issues; and with the UNC Center for Excellence for Eating Disorders, housed in the department of Psychiatry. There are also opportunities to expand to other outpatient specialty collaborative clinics. In addition to clinical programs, the GPAM division has a nationally known and productive research program and faculty, in addition to a long record of teaching excellence. GPAM's division-wide research areas include the impact of social and contextual factors on health, childhood adversity, and health inequities. Research interests in the Adolescent Medicine section include evaluation of the impact of telehealth services on adolescent consent and confidentiality, use of adolescent-friendly decision-making tools related to contraceptive options, evaluation of factors impacting reproductive health autonomy in adolescents, global health and HIV prevention, and eating disorders quality improvement and treatment outcomes. The Gillings School of Public Health and the Sheps Center for Health Services Research also offer opportunities for broader adolescent health research. Faculty may also have medical education efforts, such as medical student and resident teaching, curriculum oversight, and rotation supervision. The GPAM division is one of the largest divisions in the Department of Pediatrics and in addition to Adolescent Medicine includes Primary Care and Child Maltreatment. The Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill area of North Carolina is an attractive, vibrant, and family-friendly place to live and work with great quality of life, job markets, schools, and climate with both the mountains and the beach only a few hours away.

title: Senior Compliance Manager
description: The Senior Compliance Manager provides advanced leadership in support of the NC Collaboratory's multidisciplinary research practice partnership initiatives within the Physical Sciences team to address complex issues for the benefit of the State. This position manages research programs by monitoring compliance, ensuring the effective implementation of workflows, and serving as the first point of escalation for task management issues raised by other Program Managers. Reporting to the Research Director for Physical Sciences, the Senior Program Manager is primarily internal-facing and provides operational management for the execution of research programs. The NC Collaboratory develops yearly research initiatives that target a pressing policy issue or problem of practice faced by policymakers and practitioners at the State and local level in North Carolina, and awards funding to support mutually beneficial partnerships between academic research teams and partners in local governments, community organizations, State agencies, and private industries. Recent examples of these existing Physical Science programs include the PFAS Testing Network, the High-Performance Computing initiative, and the Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) Takeback Program in partnership with the NC Office of the State Fire Marshal. The Senior Compliance Manager provides technical oversight these activities from planning through execution and performance monitoring. Other duties include managing contract activities, recommending improvements to workflows, SOPs, forms, and templates, and optimizing documentation and data management practices for consistent program execution. The position also facilitates stakeholder engagement by coordinating input from researchers, program staff, and institutional partners.

title: STEP Psychiatrist - Open Rank
description: UNC School of Medicine's Department of Psychiatry is seeking a board-certified/board-eligible open-rank, fixed term Psychiatrist to provide clinical care to adults with serious mental illness. This position will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary academic medical center environment, where the successful candidate will have opportunities to provide patient care, teach, and engage in research. The primary practice location for this position is the UNC STEP Clinic in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. The psychiatrist will provide both in-person and virtual care to adults with serious mental illness as part of UNC's Center for Excellence in Community Mental Health (CECMH). CECMH is dedicated to promoting recovery and improving quality of life for individuals with mental illness through innovative clinical services, education, community partnerships, and research. We are seeking a clinician who values collaborative, team-based care and is committed to helping individuals build on their strengths, achieve their goals, and lead meaningful lives. Responsibilities include providing high-quality, evidence-based psychiatric care for adults with serious mental illness, including diagnostic evaluations, treatment planning, psychopharmacologic management, and ongoing clinical care. The psychiatrist will work closely with an interdisciplinary team of nurses, therapists, social workers, psychologists, and other healthcare professionals to support comprehensive, person-centered treatment. Additional responsibilities include addressing the physical health needs of individuals with serious mental illness through coordination with primary care and specialty providers, providing psychiatric consultation to healthcare teams across the medical center, and contributing to the academic mission of the department through teaching, supervision, mentorship, and scholarly activities.

title: Recovery Programs Coordinator
description: The Recovery Programs Coordinator provides strategic vision, development, implementation, and evaluation of evidence-based collegiate recovery initiatives, services, and outreach efforts, as well as other well-being-related programs. These efforts are delivered within the context of our Dimensions of Wellness, as well as holistic wellness and health promotion endeavors, often working with intersecting topics such as stress reduction, mindfulness, sleep health, nutrition, healthy relationships, alcohol and other drug and violence prevention, and other related student health and well-being indicators. The Coordinator also provides individual support for students and families in or seeking recovery.

title: Director of PATH Services
description: PATH Prevention, Advocacy, Therapeutic Support & Harm Reduction is UNC Chapel Hill's comprehensive substance use services program within the Division of Student Affairs/Student Success, delivering an integrated continuum of care spanning population-level prevention, evidence-based clinical interventions, referrals and case management, risk mitigation and harm reduction strategies, and collegiate recovery support to UNC-Chapel Hill's more than 32,000 students. Reporting to the Executive Director of Health and Wellbeing, the Director of PATH Services provides strategic leadership, administrative oversight, and operational direction for the University's comprehensive substance use prevention, intervention, and recovery program. This position establishes PATH's strategic plan, goals, measurable objectives, and evaluation framework; directly supervises four professional staff (an Administrative Assistant, a Licensed Clinical Addictions Specialist, a Prevention & Harm Reduction Coordinator, and a Recovery Programs Coordinator); manages the program budget across multiple fund sources (state allocation, student fees, grants, and philanthropy); and serves as the University's principal subject matter expert, internal consultant, and external voice on substance use health, policy, and student welfare. The Director holds clinical credibility sufficient to provide meaningful oversight of PATH's clinical services including SBIRT, brief motivational intervention, clinical substance use counseling, warm-handoff referral, and re-entry case management while operating as a public health systems leader who works upstream to shift campus culture and downstream to support individual students. The Director builds and sustains relationships across a wide range of constituencies, including students in recovery, residence life and Greek life, staff, parents, campus health and counseling partners, senior University leadership, and community coalition partners, adjusting register and approach for each. Standard work schedule Monday through Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm, with regular on-campus presence expected for student accessibility, staff supervision, and partner engagement. Occasional evening and weekend availability required, particularly during high-risk campus periods (orientation, move-in, homecoming, major athletic events, spring break, finals). Some regional and national travel expected for professional conferences and coalition participation. This is the inaugural leadership role for PATH, which is newly established and aspires to become a national model among public flagship universities. The Director is responsible for naming, branding, and institutionally anchoring the program.

title: Executive Assistant
description: The Executive Assistant's (EA) primary responsibility is to provide executive support to senior leadership at the Gillings School. In the case of this position, the position will support the Vice Dean. In this capacity, the EA will spend the bulk of their time providing calendar and operational support. In addition to overseeing the administrative functions related to ongoing projects, they ensure that assignments/requests/commitments of the executive they support are accurate, adequate, consistent, completed prior to deadlines and of high quality. This individual also works closely with, and will often receive guidance and assignments from, team members reporting up to their executive. Finally, this position reports directly to the Dean's Office Manager. As such, this individual serves as a key liaison to the Dean's Office team, communicating about, and helping to align work, and ensuring smooth exchange of information and coordination of schedules and priorities. The Gillings School administrative team has a matrix model, meaning that administrative staff are cross trained and support each other as needed. In this regard, the person in this position will occasionally rely on Dean's Office staff to cover their duties or provide surge help and vice versa. The person in this position must analyze, prioritize and keep track of multiple pieces of complex and often confidential information in order to make accurate, efficient decisions regarding workflow, and provide deft facilitation and processing of information and correspondence. In close collaboration with their executive, the Executive Assistant manages complex schedules, including requests for appointments, meetings, events and travel. This individual must be skilled in anticipating when adjustments in schedules need to be made. Because there often are more requests than available time slots, this task requires sensitivity, judgment, and the ability to prioritize. In addition, while many meetings and events are scheduled far in advance, frequently, requests from high level individuals within the School and university require rescheduling other meetings. This individual must also have excellent judgement about when problems need troubleshooting in a timely way, and provide their executive with critical information on timely matters. The individual must provide reminders for key deadlines (and ideally manage tracking systems) and ensure that work is done with high quality. The individual must be a strong communicator, verbally and in writing. The EA is responsible for independent problem solving, answering questions, providing information and taking action on behalf of their executive as authorized. The Executive Assistant also is the entry point for students, staff, faculty, university administrators at UNC and elsewhere, and a variety of callers and visitors who seek guidance. The EA must also be able to work with a high-level team that work within the units they support, playing an important role in ensuring that each team member receives key information in a timely manner. This individual must be able to work closely with others on Dean's Office administrative team, coordinating the flow of information across both teams and serving as back-up, if needed, within the Dean's Office. Similarly, this individual needs to consult about planned absences with the Dean's Office to ensure that the Dean's Office team can provide seamless continuation of support for their executive. The EA must facilitate completion of work at a rapid pace on time-sensitive matters with routine interruptions. Gillings Leadership participate in many outside research activities that benefit the School. In this context, the EA must communicate with staff from these groups and understand the nature of the topics on which these projects are focused.

title: Cogeneration Systems Facility Planner
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $7,500 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALMENTS WITHIN TWELVE (12) MONTHS OF HIRE: $3,750 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $3,750 12-MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. The Facility Planner works closely with the Cogeneration Systems Maintenance Superintendent to plan and schedule all mechanical maintenance and repairs, annual equipment system outages, emergency outages, preventive and predictive maintenance for the entire mechanical maintenance group. This position develops the scope of work and schedules for major repairs and outages at all facilities. Annual outages can be very complex and are required to be completed in a short duration to maintain system reliability. These outages can exceed $1,000,000 in multiple contracts. Activities by this position include, planning, tracking and continued updates for all groups. This position works with the Mechanical Maintenance Superintendent and Engineering staff to obtain the necessary resources to carry out the construction, maintenance and repair of the boilers, balance of plant and boiler auxiliary equipment and systems. This position often acts as a project manager of small informal projects and observes work progress in the field. This position requests purchase orders with the appropriate justifications for approval by the Maintenance Superintendent. The position requires expert level abilities in advanced scheduling software and the Maximo work management system.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate - Sharma Lab
description: The postdoctoral research associate will use genetic and molecular biological approaches to investigate the genetic and immunological basis of mucosal immunity and Inflammatory Bowel Diseases. The postdoctoral research associate will also train and supervise graduate and undergraduate students in the lab.

title: Assistant Professor
description: Application review will begin September 15 and continue until positions are filled. Up to four full-time tenure-track faculty positions in the rank of Assistant Professor in the Department of Epidemiology. Competitive candidates will demonstrate strong capacity for research that impacts public health, advances the field of epidemiology, and contributes to the department's teaching mission. As members of the Department of Epidemiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, faculty are expected to develop independently funded research portfolios, contribute impactful scholarly products, mentor master's and doctoral students, and teach core epidemiology methods and/or substantive area courses in epidemiology. The department's primary focus is the development and application of research methods to understand the patterns and causes of health and disease, and the application of that knowledge to improving the health of populations. The department provides strong training in research methods and opportunities to apply epidemiology to a wide range of health problems.

title: Open Rank
description: Application review will begin September 15 and continue until positions are filled. One or two full-time tenure-track faculty positions in the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor (open rank) in the Department of Epidemiology. As members of the Department of Epidemiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, faculty are expected to develop independently funded research portfolios, contribute impactful scholarly products, mentor master's and doctoral students, and teach core epidemiology methods and/or substantive area courses in epidemiology. The department's primary focus is the development and application of research methods to understand the patterns and causes of health and disease, and the application of that knowledge to improving the health of populations. The department provides strong training in research methods and opportunities to apply epidemiology to a wide range of health problems.

title: Golf Operations Associate
description: Assist golfers and golf shop staff which can include checking in players, retail services, cart staging, tending to the practice range and assisting with course needs. Must have a valid NC driver's license or the ability to obtain one on or prior to the start date of hire.

title: Hazardous Radioactive Materials Specialist
description: The Hazardous/Radioactive Materials Specialist is responsible for overseeing the receipt, storage, processing, and disposal of radioactive liquid and solid waste generated by the University and UNC Hospitals. This position collaborates with Hazardous Materials Technicians to transport radioactive waste to the storage facility for decay-in-storage management or temporary storage prior to shipment to an approved off-site disposal facility. This role also oversees medical waste disposal operations and coordinates the transport of hazardous waste to the storage facility. The Hazardous/Radioactive Materials Specialist provides technical expertise and operational support regarding hazardous waste accumulation, storage, and regulatory compliance requirements for non-laboratory areas across the University. In addition, the position is responsible for maintaining warehouse operations, including housekeeping, organization, routine inspections, and inventory management of supplies, materials, and equipment necessary to support waste management activities. The Specialist serves as a member of the University's Emergency Response Team, providing response support for chemical spills, hazardous materials releases, and other environmental emergencies. To ensure compliance with federal and state regulations governing hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs), this position must maintain required training and certifications. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations require personnel working at a TSDF to complete a one-time 40-hour Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) training course, as well as an 8-hour annual refresher course. Additionally, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's RCRA Part B Permit requires personnel to complete initial and annual training in accordance with 40 CFR 270.14(b)(12) and 40 CFR 264.16. Required Licenses and Certifications: * Valid North Carolina Class C or higher Commercial Driver's License (CDL) with Hazardous Materials (HazMat) endorsement. * 40-Hour HAZWOPER Certification and annual refresher training. * RCRA Hazardous Waste Training Certification (initial and annual).

title: General Surgeon
description: The Department of Surgery at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking applications for a full-time academic General Surgeon to join the recently established Section of General Surgery within the Division of GI Surgery. This position will include practice at both UNC Health Care at Hillsborough, as well as the Chapel Hill campuses. They will provide comprehensive general surgery services at UNC Health Care at Hillsborough, supporting the Department's mission to expand access to high-quality surgical care throughout central North Carolina, while building an elective practice with a focus in abdominal wall reconstruction, foregut, and/or minimally invasive general surgery. UNC Health Care Hillsborough is a 68-bed community hospital that combines the culture of a community hospital with the advanced technology and expertise of UNC Medical Center. The campus includes an outpatient medical office building with clinic and procedure space, growing emergency department volumes, robotic surgery capabilities, and expanded operating room capacity. The Department of Surgery is committed to growing both elective and emergency surgical services at Hillsborough while extending specialty surgical care closer to the communities we serve. Clinical responsibilities will include elective and urgent general surgery, emergency general surgery call coverage, outpatient consultation and follow-up, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across the UNC Health system. The successful candidate will work closely with colleagues across the Department of Surgery to ensure seamless coordination of care across campuses. This position is being recruited as an Open Rank, Fixed Term appointment between 0.5 FTE and 1.0 FTE faculty appointment, with academic rank commensurate with the candidate's qualifications and experience. The faculty member will be expected to perform clinical duties while fulfilling the academic responsibilities of an educational institution. Faculty members within the Division of GI Surgery are expected to contribute to the Department's three core missions of clinical care, education, and research. Individuals who exhibit exceptional skills and achievements may be considered for a leadership position within the Department of Surgery. Leadership roles are not guaranteed and are dependent upon the current needs of our surgical service lines. Faculty members are expected to participate in the education of medical students, residents, and other learners through clinical teaching and mentorship in both the academic medical center and community hospital settings. Candidates with interests in clinical research, outcomes research, quality improvement, health services research, surgical education, global surgery, or other scholarly endeavors are encouraged to apply. Faculty members must demonstrate a commitment to providing exceptional patient-centered surgical care while advancing access to high-quality surgical services in a community practice environment. Candidates should possess expertise in a broad range of general surgical procedures, including with minimally invasive and robotic surgery. The selected candidate must be collaborative, team-oriented, and able to work effectively with colleagues across multiple surgical specialties, hospital campuses, and interdisciplinary care teams.

title: Clinical Education Assessment Analyst
description: The Clinical Education Assessment Analyst is a key member of the Clinical Education team within Academic Affairs and provides specialized professional expertise in the evaluation of learner clinical performance, student progression, practice readiness, and educational outcomes within the predoctoral dental program. Reporting to the Director of Clinical Education, the position supports the School's clinical education mission through assessment analysis, program evaluation, and continuous improvement of clinical education. The position analyzes and interprets clinical education information from multiple sources to evaluate individual and cohort performance, competency development, completion of required clinical experiences, progression toward established educational expectations, and readiness for independent practice. The Clinical Education Assessment Analyst identifies trends, patterns, performance gaps, and areas requiring further evaluation and translates findings into meaningful information that supports faculty and Clinical Education leadership in educational planning and decision-making. The position also evaluates the effectiveness and consistency of clinical assessment practices and works with preceptors, course directors, faculty, care coordinators, Institutional Effectiveness, and other academic partners to strengthen assessment methodology, progression measures, faculty calibration, and program outcomes. The candidate will contribute to the training of new members in the lab regarding standard protocols. Finally, communicating on a routine basis with Dr. Kelada in person and digitally will be essential to success.

title: Temporary Housekeeper (3rd Shift)
description: Provides daily routine and detail cleaning of campus building interior and exterior areas, including but not limited to offices, lounges, restrooms, student housing, classrooms, laboratories, entrances, exits, and stairways. General duties include vacuuming, sweeping, mopping, dusting, and trash removal. Position will primarily be responsible for working in on-campus buildings during the academic year, summer break, and between semesters.

title: Research, CE, and Outreach Program Manager
description: This is a professional position based in the Gillings School of Global Public Health, NC Occupational Safety and Health Education Resource Center (NC OSHERC), University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, located within the Department of Environmental Sciences and Engineering at Chapel Hill. The purpose of this position is to support NC OSHERC's mission by providing technical expertise and administrative support to the NC OSHRERC's Outreach and Continuing Education programs. This includes working with the Outreach and Continuing Education (OCE) Director and the Center Director, NC OSHERC program directors, and internal and external stakeholders to develop and deliver high level, targeted technical assistance and training to serve the needs of the North Carolina and the Southeastern region's workforce, in particular the essential and underrepresented workers, as well as small- and medium-sized businesses who often lack resources to protect the safety and well-being of their workers. The individual in this position will be required to interact with faculty, staff, and students from the academic, targeted research training, and outreach and continuing education environments, as well as representatives from the public and private sectors and professional societies, and practitioners from all fields of occupational and environmental health and safety disciplines. The individual will (1) help develop and coordinate outreach and continuing education training programs, assist with NC OSHERC's research activities related to occupational safety and health, and will respond to technical assistance requests from private and public organizations as to their education and training needs; (2) provide technical and administrative support by identifying, tracking, and evaluating continuing education and outreach opportunities, and (3) assist in defining and executing the NC OSHERC policies and strategic plans to accomplish the mission and vision of the NC OSHERC.

title: General Utility Worker
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $3,497.00 IS AVAILABLE FOR THIE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $1,748.50 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $1,748.50 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE Requires working knowledge of machine operations, safety practices, snow removal operations, and horticultural and turf management practices. Also requires good oral communication skills so that task instructions are delivered and received in a clear manner. Responsibilities generally include manual work related to the upkeep of highways, grounds, buildings and equipment on the UNC-CH campus, and the performance of a variety of physical labor tasks requiring some specialized knowledge and experience. Work is routine and repetitive in nature and may require strenuous physical exertion. *Requires a valid N.C. Driver's License or the ability to obtain one prior to hire date.

title: Cancer Health Drivers Program Postdoctoral Trainee
description: The UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, founded in 1975, is a National Cancer Institute (NCI)-designated comprehensive cancer center. The Center’s mission is to reduce cancer occurrence and death in North Carolina and the nation through research, treatment, training, and outreach. The UNC Cancer Health Drivers Training Program CHDP has three primary objectives for all trainees: 1) Engage deeply in understanding drivers of cancer disparities and interventions to improve cancer outcomes, and demonstrate competencies in community engagement, advanced methods, digital health, or local to global health. 2) Gain mentored research expertise with the guidance from multidisciplinary mentors, on bio/behavioral and/or social/environmental domains according to the Cells-to-Society model. 3) Develop professional skills required for a successful research career, including leadership, acquiring research funding and publication skills.

title: Pre-/Post-Award Subject Matter Expert
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual/hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. As such, this position's work location is designated as virtual. Please note that the designated work location is subject to change based on the unit's business needs. The Pre-/Post-Award Research Administration Subject Matter Expert (SME) serves as a strategic leader and operational authority for research administration across the School of Medicine (SOM). This role is responsible for exercising independent judgment and discretion on matters of significance, including the interpretation and application of complex federal, state, and institutional policies. The SME leads the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of research administration processes, ensuring compliance, efficiency, and alignment with institutional goals. The position requires the ability to make critical decisions that impact research operations, funding, and compliance, and to serve as a trusted advisor to SOM leadership, faculty, and staff.

title: Open Rank
description: The Division of Hematology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking candidates with a clinical interest in non-Hodgkin and Hodgkin lymphoma to join the faculty in the Department of Medicine. Rank and track will be commensurate with experience. Job responsibilities may include the following: Research or scholarship: There will be an expectation of high-quality clinical and/or translational research for patients with lymphoma that will lead to scholarship. Clinical: The candidate will provide specialized care for patients with Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma in an outpatient setting and serve as an attending physician on the inpatient malignant hematology service at the North Carolina Basnight Cancer Hospital at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill. Teaching and mentorship: There will be an expectation of teaching and mentoring for hematology/oncology fellows, residents, and medical students. As this is an open rank posting, academic rank and track will be determined by the candidate’s experience and achievements. This position can be fixed term, tenure track or variable track.

title: Facility Maint Tech - MechTrd
description: Transportation and Parking maintains ten parking decks with approximately 8,200 parking spaces and an additional 14,300 spaces in surface parking lots located throughout campus. This position performs daily inspections, maintenance and minor repairs in UNC parking facilities to maintain clean and safe access for students, staff, and visitors. This position is required to respond to adverse weather that includes snow removal from parking decks and pedestrian pathways. This position maintains parking equipment, lighting systems, power cleaning equipment and yearly pavement marking and lot striping.

title: Property Security Officer
description: This position is responsible for the security at the assigned site. The officer will conduct patrols ensuring all doors and windows of the facility have not been compromised. The officer will lock and unlock doors within the facility as necessary and in accordance with post orders. The officer will check the identification of all suspicious persons. The officer will assist employees and guests with escorts, disabled vehicles, all hazards, power outages, heating and cooling problems and report same to UNC Dispatch. The officer is responsible for arriving on time and in full uniform. The Officer should notify supervisors and/or the Security Manager of any problems or incidents that might occur on their shift. This position is one that is necessary to ensure University operations continue uninterrupted during periods of adverse weather and /or other emergency situations, including those that cause the University to close. As such you may be required to report to work according to your usual schedule or upon notification to report outside of your usual work schedule. Monitor crimes in progress and communicate information to responding officers via UNC Dispatch. Provide attention to detail. Complete daily reports concerning task and assignments completed during duty hours. Work individually and independently in a generally unsupervised position. Performs protective, security, enforcement, and public contact work in a security assignment at the assigned site location. Work involves participating in the locking and unlocking of property and patrolling the interior and exterior of facilities via foot, protection of all artworks on site. Must resolve daily work problems and uniform/equipment problems, monitor radio traffic and file daily activity reports. Work includes guarding property against fire, damage, theft, or other hazards; monitoring assigned areas for possible violation of policies, regulations, and rules of conduct; recognizing and reporting unusual, suspicious, or hazardous situations; providing information and assistance to the public; operating and maintaining security equipment and providing escorts to patron's vehicles as requested. Work requires knowledge of standard safety, surveillance, security practices and equipment; knowledge of standard methods of reporting and handling emergencies such as disturbances and fires, medical and security threats; and knowledge of security/enforcement policies, rules, and regulations. Works with TPS Parking Enforcement requesting parking citations and towing. Maintains confidentiality and discretion in the course of conducting business; works individually and/or with others; and adapts to change and circumstances.

title: Senior Assistant Director
description: The Office of Scholarships and Student Aid (OSSA) seeks a creative, enthusiastic, and organized individual for the position of Senior Assistant Director. This is a full-time, permanent EHRA Non-Faculty position that will report to the Senior Associate Director of the Office of Scholarships and Student Aid and will provide on-site services at the Undergraduate Business Program located at the Kenan Flagler Business School for students in undergraduate business programs, scholarship processes and global program support. This position's responsibilities include: providing financial aid counseling to current and prospective students of the Undergraduate Business Program in person, via phone, via email, and via virtual platforms; providing assistance regarding the application and aid disbursement process; reviewing financial aid application data, FAFSA data, and other applications for financial assistance; applying federal and state administrative rules and regulations, and institutional guidelines to determine eligibility for financial aid, scholarships, and fellowships; committing funds on behalf of the University by making financial aid award decisions; acting as a liaison to other undergraduate KFBS offices, acting as a liaison to other University offices including the Cashier's Office and the Registrar's office. The person in this position will also collaborate with partners in OSSA and Enrollment to ensure financial aid or scholarship practices and policies enacted at the Undergraduate Business Program are in line with the mission and goals of the Division of Enrollment. The individual will serve as chair for the Undergraduate Business Program Scholarship Committee. They will be required to report on scholarships, and other funding sources and initiatives as required, such as the program enhancement fee. The position will also contribute to the overall financial aid and communications strategy for Undergraduate Business School students through collaborations with the Senior Associate Director for Communications and Student Success and other Processing and Student Success colleagues within the Office of Scholarships and Student Aid.

title: Clinical Assistant Professor
description: This is a 12-month fixed term position reporting to a Division Chair. The fixed term faculty member may have teaching responsibilities in didactic, clinical, laboratory, and/or simulation settings in the prelicensure programs, with expertise in psychiatric-mental health nursing. The faculty member may serve as course coordinator, oversee advisement of prelicensure honors projects, serve on BSN, MSN, DNP and/or PhD committees. Additional service and scholarship commiserate with rank.

title: Dental Assistant
description: The Surgical Assistant is responsible for providing surgical and dental assisting duties to the dental faculty practice, student, and graduate clinics within the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery specialty. Tasks include preparing the clinic, setting up surgical trays using sterile techniques, assisting with a variety of surgical and dental procedures, obtaining surgical consent from patients, obtaining and documenting pre- and post-op vitals, and preparing patients for their procedure and subsequently review post-op instructions. The Surgical Assistant is responsible for reviewing the surgical caseload at the beginning of each day and assisting with clinical education of students and medical emergencies when needed. The Assistant may be asked to take impressions, order x-rays, complete the appropriate pathology and microbiology forms, maintain operating room inventory and complete duties assigned by the direct supervisor or faculty member.

title: Orthopaedic Hand Surgeon
description: The Department Orthopaedics at the University of North Carolina is seeking applications for a full- time academic orthopaedic surgeon with specialization in hand and nerve surgery to join our Upper Extremity Service. The Department of Orthopaedics includes 34 faculty members who provide the full array of clinical orthopaedic services. This position will be a primary appointment in the Department of Orthopaedics. The clinical focus for this position will be hand, micro, and nerve surgery. Hand fellowship-trained applicants are encouraged to apply. The clinical position includes taking general orthopaedic call for the practice and will also include hand trauma, elective hand surgery, general reconstructive surgery, and microvascular reconstruction of the upper extremities. Faculty members must possess a desire to commit to the missions of the Department and School of Medicine, including the clinical, education, and research missions. Regarding the education mission, faculty members are expected to regularly participate in the education of medical students, residents, and fellows. Regarding the research mission, a commitment to any one of a broad array of research interests is desirable, including but not limited to clinical, outcomes, health services, basic science, translational, ethics, education, or global surgery research. Regarding the clinical mission, faculty members must be committed to delivering high quality clinical care that is of value to the patients of UNC. Selected candidate must be team-oriented and have the ability to interact well with colleagues inside and out of the Department. Outreach to our many rural referring hospitals is highly encouraged.

title: Social Work Practitioner
description: This position will serve as a Care Manager for the Center for Excellence in Community Mental Health (CECMH). The care management team at the CECMH offers robust and effective service models to address the comprehensive health needs of eligible beneficiaries through collaboration with insurance providers, UNC providers, and community partners. This position will provide care management services to an assigned panel of adults with serious mental illness and other behavioral health needs. The Care Manager will engage with assigned beneficiaries through frequent contact based on client need and acuity and will be responsible for ensuring referrals to psychiatry/medication management, therapy, participation in care team huddles, and development of individualized care plans. The Care Manager will also be responsible for monitoring care and ensuring timely hospital follow-up appointments and transitions of care. Due to the nature of this role, the Care Manager is expected to provide services in community-based settings and conduct field visits as needed. Reliable transportation is required to successfully perform the essential functions of the position. This position will complete required trainings and learning activities through UNC CECMH on topics including HIPAA/confidentiality, proficient use of the electronic medical record, corporate compliance and ethics, cultural competence, client rights, workplace safety, and other areas relevant to the population served. In collaboration with the Care Management Program Supervisor, this position will maintain current knowledge of the care management model, policies, procedures, and expectations as disseminated through relevant partners.

title: Director of Local Elected Official Programming
description: The Division of Public Leadership and Governance at the School of Government equips public officials with the knowledge, skills, and support needed to lead effectively in complex and evolving governmental environments. We serve local government managers and supervisors, elected officials, state agencies, and other public organizations through high-quality education, research, publications, consulting, coaching, and leadership development programs. Our work fosters thoughtful, ethical, and effective public leadership that strengthens organizations, communities, and public trust. The Director of Local Elected Official Programming coordinates the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of educational programs, resources, and support services for local government elected officials through the School of Government. Working collaboratively with School faculty, staff, and external partners, the Director ensures that programming is relevant, accessible, timely, and responsive to the evolving needs of elected officials across North Carolina. The Director provides operational leadership for the Local Elected Leaders Academy (LELA), overseeing program planning, scheduling, implementation, evaluation, participant engagement, and program administration. In partnership with School faculty and staff, the Director coordinates the delivery of courses, webinars, and other learning opportunities and maintains a comprehensive programming calendar to support consistent and effective program delivery. While curriculum content and instructional design remain the responsibility of School faculty, the Director works closely with faculty to ensure programs address emerging issues and respond to participant needs. The Director also administers the LELA recognition program; develops and disseminates practical resources for elected officials; cultivates relationships with elected leaders throughout the state; and strengthens partnerships with organizations that support local governance, including the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners, the North Carolina League of Municipalities, and the North Carolina City/County Management Association. In addition, the Director collaborates with School leadership, faculty, staff, and development personnel to identify funding opportunities and support the continued growth and sustainability of programming for local elected officials.

title: Open Rank - MFM/Critical Care Specialist
description: The University of North Carolina's Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology is recruiting a tenure track or variable track Maternal-Fetal Medicine Specialist with expertise in critical care obstetrics to provide inpatient and outpatient care to high-risk obstetric patients, including those requiring intensive care management. This is a unique opportunity to serve as the clinical and academic leader of Critical Care MFM at UNC, with responsibilities extending well beyond direct ICU service. The successful candidate will be expected to: (1) provide consultative and co-management critical care services for pregnant and postpartum patients; (2) lead the development and implementation of evidence-based critical care protocols for obstetric patients; (3) build and direct a joint MFM-Critical Care fellowship program in collaboration with relevant departments; and (4) develop and expand tele-critical care (e-ICU) capacity to extend critical care expertise to obstetric patients across UNC Health's regional network. Additional responsibilities include education of medical students, residents, and fellows, and active participation in the division's research mission. The division's clinical programs include high-risk obstetric care, perinatal consultation, prenatal diagnosis, ultrasound, genetic services, invasive fetal therapy, and perinatal outreach. Division faculty members are engaged participants in the activities of UNC's Collaborative for Maternal and Infant Health (www.mombaby.org), which provides multidisciplinary care coordination for families referred for fetal malformations. Division members actively participate in student and resident teaching and provide subspecialty training for six Maternal Fetal Medicine fellows through its 3-year American Board of Obstetrics & Genecology (ABOG) approved fellowship program.

title: Senior Digital Technology Contract Counsel
description: This position is a 100% remote work arrangement, consistent with System Office policy. UNC Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside in North Carolina, within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. The Senior Digital Technology Contracts Counsel provides legal advice and transactional support related to data privacy, information security, and technology procurement. The position is responsible for drafting, reviewing, updating, and negotiating data privacy and information security provisions contained in the University's standard terms and conditions and a wide range of technology-related agreements. Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor, Chief Privacy Officer, and Special Counsel, this position supports the University's digital risk, data privacy, information security, data governance, and technology acquisition activities by providing specialized legal advice related to technology licensing, data privacy, and information security provisions contained in University technology agreements. The Senior Digital Technology Contracts Counsel partners closely with the Office of University Counsel, Finance & Operations, Purchasing Services, the Information Security Office, research administration, and other administrative units to ensure appropriate contractual protections for institutional data and information systems. Responsibilities of the Senior Digital Technology Contracts Counsel include: Draft, review, and negotiate high-value and high-risk data privacy and information security provisions in technology-related agreements, including Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), software licensing agreements, cloud service agreements, software development agreements, non-disclosure and confidentiality agreements, data processing agreements, cybersecurity services, managed services agreements and other complex technology provisions contained in University contracts. Partner with Information Technology Services (ITS), Institutional Privacy Office (IPO), Information Security Office (ISO), the Office of University Counsel, Finance and Operations, Research Administration, and other administrative units to support compliant technology procurement. Assist in developing and maintaining contract templates, negotiation playbooks, and institutional guidance for technology and data-related agreements. Provide training and guidance to University units regarding contracting practices involving data privacy, information security, and technology procurement. Assist with resolution of contractual issues or disputes involving technology vendors. Lead contract and legal review of high-value and high-risk data technology procurement negotiations and escalations to ensure compliance with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and University policies. Mentor Junior Digital Technology Contracts Counsel position Other duties as assigned.

title: Maternal Fetal Medicine Specialist
description: The University of North Carolina Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology is recruiting for an open rank (non-tenure track or tenure track) faculty member within the Division of Maternal-Fetal Medicine. The Division's clinical programs include high-risk obstetric care, perinatal consultation, prenatal diagnosis, ultrasound, genetic services, invasive fetal therapy and perinatal outreach. Division faculty members are active participants in the activities of UNC's Center for Maternal and Infant Health (www.mombaby.org ), which provides multidisciplinary care coordination for families referred for fetal malformations. Division members actively participate in student and resident teaching and provide subspecialty training for six Maternal Fetal Medicine fellows through its ABOG approved fellowship program. The academically-oriented Division has an outstanding record of epidemiologic research and is one of the participating institutions in the NICHD Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network (MFMU). The Department has an active BIRCWH training program. Biomedical and public health graduate programs offer extensive opportunities for collaboration in basic science and translational research. Department Website: http://www.med.unc.edu/obgyn/

title: Dean, UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy
description: Reporting to the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost, the Dean is the School's Chief Executive and Academic Officer and will provide academic, intellectual, and administrative leadership to the School. The Dean leads the effort in creating a vision and advancing the mission of the School, with responsibility for the academic and research enterprise, advancement and development functions, personnel, general administration and management, compliance and risk management, and budget. The appointment is reviewed every five years. The Dean: 1. Serves as chief executive and academic administrative officer of the School of Pharmacy. The dean plans for, and stewards, the fiscal and material resources needed to offer the educational, research, and service programs of the School. 2. Administers the School's educational, research, and public service programs. Consults and collaborates with faculty and administrators on decisions related to school strategy, including academic affairs. 3. Recommends to the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost the appointments, promotions, and tenure of School of Pharmacy faculty members. 4. Serves as the School's representative on various University policy and decision bodies and is the official representative of the School to external constituencies. 5. Leads the School's advancement and development activities to promote the school's vision, mission, values and strategic plan. title: Research Operations Manager
description: UNC's Advanced Cellular Therapeutics Facility is looking for a qualified Research Operations Manager to join their team to support the work of developing and producing human cellular therapy products for patients receiving adoptive cell therapy for the treatment of cancer. The Advanced Cellular Therapeutics Facility manufactures human cellular therapy products under Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) that is regulated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The Research Operations Manager role supports the operation of the 31,542 sq ft, two floor manufacturing facility that includes 14 ISO 7 cleanrooms totaling roughly 17,500 sq ft. This role maintains continuous oversight of temperature, humidity, and room pressures to ensure all spaces remain within ISO 7 GMP specifications, providing 24/7 monitoring and rapid response to any environmental excursions that could jeopardize room accessibility, product integrity, or human patient treatments. This role serves as a key liaison with UNC Real Estate and Development Facilities to coordinate building maintenance, repairs, and construction activities, ensuring work is scheduled without disrupting manufacturing operations. The Research Operations Manager must be knowledgeable in HVAC and building systems to guide third party service providers, operate the Building Electronic Management System, and communicate alarms or troubleshooting needs. They work closely with manufacturing and quality teams to enforce room requirements, document impacts, and segregate affected areas when necessary. The role also includes investigating and resolving building issues with vendors, managing capital projects related to facility systems and equipment, tracking equipment lifecycles, planning replacements, and evaluating new equipment purchases. Additionally, the Facility Manager trains and mentors other team members, building internal capability for equipment maintenance and calibration to reduce reliance on external providers. They will be responsible for the equipment lifecycle from onboarding, calibration, preventative maintenance, and decommissioning. The Research Operations Manager role requires a person who understands Installation, Operational, and Process Qualification activities that must occur during the implementation of equipment used onsite, how those activities can impact the manufacturing process, and all related safety compliance measures. The role will be required to interact with vendors on a daily basis scheduling activities, reviewing technical reports for acceptance, managing supply logistics, and ensuring equipment is maintained on a schedule to complete all calibrations and preventative maintenance. This role is responsible for responding to equipment issues and facility problems, investigating root causes, developing a corrective action plan, having it approved, and putting it into place, while also supporting space planning to ensure operational continuity. This role needs to understand purchasing systems at the university as they will submit for purchase orders and quotes to have work performed at the facility. They will oversee any building work and ensure work is completed per quotes. The person must be able to work independently with little oversight and multi-task a number of ongoing activities. Additionally, the role must respond to equipment/ facility issues quickly to have them resolved so as to not impact products for a patient. This role will oversee 4 staff members as they execute qualification activities, manage equipment, and support external vendors. This role will plan and schedule their work accordingly as well as develop and educate them.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The Department of Pharmacology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to investigate the molecular and structural mechanisms that regulate G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling pathways in the laboratory of Dr. Henrik Dohlman. The successful candidate will leverage expertise in structural biology, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), protein biochemistry, and cell signaling to characterize receptor complexes, G protein signaling networks, kinase-mediated regulatory mechanisms, and downstream signaling events. Research efforts will focus on understanding the molecular basis of GPCR and G protein regulation, including mechanisms of signal desensitization, allosteric communication, and disease-associated signaling dysfunction, with the goal of advancing our understanding of signal transduction processes relevant to human health and disease.

title: Open Rank
description: This position will be in the Division of Hematology in the Department of Medicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The individual in this position will be expected to manage patients with leukemia specifically chronic lymphocytic leukemia. They will also be expected to manage individuals with monoclonal B cell lymphocytosis and occasionally low-grade lymphomas. This individual will have a robust clinical research program, which would include investigator initiated clinical trials, clinical trials working with pharmaceutical company partners and cooperative group trials. Additionally, this individual could have a robust translational oncology program that focused on a better understanding of the biology of chronic lymphocytic leukemia or MBCL or biomarkers of disease severity for those diseases. As this is an open rank posting, the candidate hired into this position could be hired into a fixed term, variable track or tenure track faculty appointment at any academic rank.

title: Health Services Coordinator
description: The Health Services Coordinator organizes and coordinates Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT), physical health and specialist appointments to ensure a beneficiary can access needed care services in accordance with the PCP. The Health Services Coordinator facilitates transportation to and from scheduled MAT, physical health, and specialist appointments, and ensures safe and secure transportation of any prescribed medications from the MAT provider to the residential program. The Coordinator will complete progress notes.

description: The Division of Nephrology at the UNC School of Medicine is recruiting for an Open Rank Faculty Position specializing in General Nephrology. title: Pediatric Endocrinology Clinical Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Pediatrics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, in partnership with the North Carolina Children's Hospital, is seeking a Pediatric Endocrinologist to support the Division's clinical and academic missions. This appointment is for a Clinical Assistant Professor, fixed term, 1.0 FTE, with compensation and responsibilities commensurate with the candidate's experience. North Carolina Children's Hospital is a leading academic medical center dedicated to delivering family-centered care through excellence in clinical care, advocacy, research, and education. The hospital is consistently ranked among the nation's best children's hospitals by U.S. News & World Report, and the Division of Pediatric Endocrinology is accredited by the American Diabetes Association. The faculty member will report directly to the Chief of the Division of Pediatric Endocrinology and join a well-established, multidisciplinary team, including board-certified pediatric endocrinologists, nurse practitioners, a clinical pharmacist, pediatric endocrinology fellows, pediatric residents, Certified Diabetes Educators, nutritionists, and nurses. Together, the team provides comprehensive care for children with endocrine and diabetes-related conditions. Clinical responsibilities will include both inpatient and outpatient care of children with diabetes and other endocrine disorders. Outpatient clinics are located at UNC Children's Specialty Clinics in Chapel Hill and Raleigh, NC, with regional care responsibilities as needed. In addition, faculty are expected to participate in scholarly activities, including quality improvement initiatives, clinical research, and medical education.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate - Williams Lab
description: The Postdoctoral Research Associate will be involved in developing peptide/small molecule inhibitors of chromatin remodeling complex. Work will include protein purification binding and kinetic analyses, structural biology, and FRET/BRET measurements.

title: Clinical Instructor
description: The Department of Psychiatry at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine is seeking a full-time, fixed-term faculty position at the master's level to serve as a Clinical Instructor with the UNC Assertive Community Treatment (ACT) Team operating in Wake County. ACT is an intensive, multi-disciplinary, community-based mental health service for adults with severe and persistent mental illness, with a particular focus on individuals with primary psychotic disorders. ACT targets individuals who have significant functional impairments, as well as complicating treatment factors that present barriers to participation in more traditional office-based services. The ACT Team provides crisis response services 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, through an on-call crisis line. This position participates in the rotation of the ACT on-call phone. Master's level ACT clinicians are responsible for the coordination of ACT services for an assigned group of individuals served by the ACT Team, including the assessment, treatment planning, and implementation of evidence-based interventions, rehabilitation, and support services. Area(s) of focus will be based on clinician expertise and skill as well as the needs of the caseload, and could include evidence-based therapy appropriate for the population, integrated dual disorders treatment for co-occurring disorders, housing, employment, and psychiatric rehabilitation, among others. This position may participate in the supervision of trainees during rotations or placement with the ACT Team. In addition to the duties listed above, this position may have additional supervisory and administrative responsibilities to function as the ACT Team Lead. These additional responsibilities, which will be outlined as a secondary appointment, are distinct from the Clinical Instructor appointment. These responsibilities include provision of clinical leadership for the ACT program in collaboration with the ACT Medical Director, provision of clinical and administrative supervision to staff, and oversight for the day-to-day operations of the team. They are responsible for ensuring that the team is providing the highest quality of care to service recipients and maximizing resources though attentiveness to authorization and billing practices. The Team Lead is a practicing clinician and provides direct services to individuals served by the ACT Team, including empirically based therapeutic modalities, psychoeducation and support for individuals' family members, clinical assessments, crisis response services, and development and implementation of person-centered treatment plans. The Team Lead provides clinical back-up for on-call staff and will participate in the rotation of the on-call phone.
