title: Research Scholar
description: The Laboratory for Analytic Sciences (LAS) advances innovative analytic capabilities through multidisciplinary research and collaboration. The Research Scholar role leads the design, prototyping, and refinement of data‑driven analytic tools, technologies, and tradecraft that address complex analytic challenges. The position applies advanced data‑science methods to create solutions that are operationally relevant and aligned with analyst workflows. It requires a disciplined, iterative development approach centered on rapid prototyping, usability evaluation, and continuous improvement. The Research Scholar also coordinates LAS and NC State resources that support analytic development; organizes and contributes to collaborative research teams; and supports strategic research priorities. The role is essential in integrating emerging technologies with analytic tradecraft to produce mission‑focused, high‑impact outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Technical Solution Development and Applied Research: Work with operational users and subject matter experts to develop analytic solutions that address strategic challenge problems. Design and implement software prototypes and solutions that support the transition of research concepts into classified, operational environments Provide technical guidance and oversight of multiple prototype development efforts. Understand how technical products mature and guide the development of prototype efforts into transitionable knowledge and products. Investigate methods of integrating multiple complementary technical efforts. Collaborate with operational analysts to develop technical solutions that improve analysts’ workflows. Serve as an organizational resource for expertise and knowledge of analytic approaches Implement, evaluate, and rigorously compare different analytic approaches, in particular approaches that utilize AI and Machine Learning models Collect and curate datasets necessary to support the unclassified investigation of research questions relevant to classified applications Contribute to LAS’s overall research direction, including the development of new projects and LAS’s annual research portfolio Project Management: Align the technical scope of projects with strategic objectives and resource constraints. Define reasonable and beneficial deliverables for research and development projects and help manage their progress. Communicate with project leads to identify and address the needs of various performers. Ensure that LAS leadership is informed on the current status and progress of research and development efforts. Work with LAS leadership to manage budget and resource needs for various projects. Other duties as assigned

title: Electronics Specialist
description: The primary purpose of the position is to perform the day-to-day operation of the NCSU Phytotron through proper function of the electrical, electronic, and mechanical systems of the facility. The position will also conduct daily surveillance and needed repairs of environmental chamber operations, diagnose any source of malfunction, and manufacture, assemble, install, calibrate, repair, and maintain/modify environmental control and measurement systems within the Phytotron with little supervision. In this role you must also be able to lift and carry up to 50 lbs., with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Assistant Professor in Elementary Teacher Education
description: The Department of Teacher Education and Learning Sciences (TELS) invites applications for an Assistant Professor in Elementary Teacher Education to be affiliated with undergraduate and graduate studies in elementary teaching and learning. This is a tenure-track appointment at the Assistant Professor level, with teaching, scholarship, service, and outreach expectations. We are seeking those who are scholars in elementary teacher education who will lead and contribute to research on approaches and programs that prepare pre-service teachers. You will engage in research primarily focused on elementary teacher preparation programs’ features and impact. This might include elements such as modality (e.g., face-to-face, hybrid, online), structure (e.g., traditional four-year programs, part-time programs for practicing teachers, competency-based education), or pathway (e.g., bachelor's degree, master's degree, residency, registered apprenticeship). Additionally, you will submit proposals for internal/external funding in support of the related research. The ideal candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary teacher preparation, including the Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program, with a strong preference for those who teach elementary social studies education. As a faculty member,you will provide service and leadership to the Elementary Education program area, the department, college, and university. You will participate in outreach and engagement activities with elementary schools locally and across North Carolina, and collaborate with faculty within the department, college, and across the university. Position Responsibilities Maintain a high level of scholarly research, publication, and grant-writing activity that aligns with a tenure track position in a university with high research activity. Produce high quality research on pre-service teacher preparation programs, features, and impact. Seek external funding for research and development activities. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary education, with a strong preference for social studies pre-service teacher education graduate and undergraduate programs Recruit, advise, and mentor graduate students and serve on doctoral committees. Engage in collaborative research with other faculty and researchers within the College of Education, including the Friday Institute for Educational Innovation and the Belk Center for Community College leadership, as well as across the university. Provide service and leadership in the elementary education program, department, college, university, and professional organizations. Participate in outreach and engagement for department and college initiatives with underserved communities and high need areas and engaging with stakeholders across the state of North Carolina. If you are passionate about preparing future elementary educators and interested in teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary teacher preparation, including the Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program, with expertise in elementary social studies education, we encourage you to apply and join our faculty.

title: Director of Leadership (Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research)
department: 134001 - Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research
description: The Director of Leadership provides strategic leadership and oversight within the Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research. Reporting directly to the Executive Director and serving as a member of the Belk Center leadership team, this position leads the development, implementation, and management of high-impact leadership development programs, executive learning initiatives, and statewide partnerships that support North Carolina’s community college system. The Director serves as the primary liaison to key partner organizations, including the North Carolina Association of Community College Presidents (NCACCP), North Carolina Community College System (NCCCS), grant partners, and other external constituents. In this role, you will help shape the future of leadership across North Carolina’s community college system. Working at the intersection of leadership development, applied research, and statewide collaboration, you will influence how leaders are prepared to meet the evolving needs of their institutions, students, and communities. Your work will extend the Belk Center’s reach and strengthen its role as a trusted partner and recognized leader in community college leadership and student success. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Statewide Leadership and Systems Advancement: Advance statewide and national partnerships and initiatives that strengthen community college leadership and institutional impact. Lead the Teaching and Learning portfolio, supporting Teaching and Learning Hubs serving more than 15,000 faculty across North Carolina. Convene statewide and national engagements that elevate promising practices and inform continuous improvement. Partner with research and evaluation colleagues to assess impact and translate findings into actionable strategies. Leadership Development and Program Innovation: Provide strategic leadership for executive leadership programs, curriculum, and learning experiences grounded in evidence and responsive to the evolving needs of the sector. Provide executive leadership for the North Carolina Community College Leadership Program, building on its 35-year legacy of developing community college leaders. Advance scalable approaches to leadership development informed by emerging trends, research, adult learning, and evolving leadership competencies. Strategic Partnerships and Organizational Leadership: Build high-level partnerships with NCACCP, NCCCS, grant partners, and other collaborators to advance mission-critical priorities. Represent the Belk Center through signature events, publications, and external engagements that expand its visibility and influence. Lead and develop staff, consultants, and affiliates while aligning research, programming, partnerships, resources, and strategic priorities. Use program outcomes and emerging statewide needs to inform strategic planning, resource allocation, and the continued evolution of the Belk Center. If you are a collaborative leader who understands the unique role of community colleges, brings a passion for developing leaders and advancing the field, and thrives at the intersection of strategy, innovation, and statewide partnership, we encourage you to apply.

title: Temporary Transformational Scholars Supervisor for Eastern/Central NC
description: Overview of the College of Education: As one of the nation’s top-ranked colleges of education, NC State’s College of Education leads the way in North Carolina in preparing extraordinary educators, conducting transformational research, and engaging communities where they are to improve the educational outcomes of all learners and advance the greater good.The college’s faculty are widely-recognized thought leaders who use their research to transform the practice of teaching, learning, and leading. They have particular strengths in improving technology-enhanced learning and teaching; fostering community-based learning and PK-16 partnerships; and innovating leadership and workforce development, educational policy, and evaluation. About two-thirds of the faculty are grant active. They are engaged in over 225 active projects totaling $151 million, making them the most productive in terms of research activity compared with other colleges of education in North Carolina and among the Top 5% in the nation. In FY24, the college’s research expenditures exceeded $20 million.The college has over 1,600 students studying across five graduate certificates, seven undergraduate majors, two undergraduate minors, 13 master’s degrees, three Ph.D., and two Ed.D. programs housed in three academic departments: Educational Leadership, Policy, and Human Development; Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Education; and Teacher Education and Learning Sciences, with approximately 130 tenure-track and professional-track faculty, 110 support and professional staff, and about 160 graduate and teaching assistants. The College of Education is also home to the Belk Center for Community College Leadership and Research, the Friday Institute for Educational Innovation, and Elevate, NC State’s inclusive postsecondary education program for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities.The college has over 18,000 living alumni, with over 6,000 working in public schools in every county in North Carolina. Those who are teachers rate among the highest in effectiveness on surveys of school employers in North Carolina. This role will support student teachers placed in Harnett, Duplin, Edgecombe, and Wilson counties. It is ideal for someone within commuting distance to those areas, as the work will primarily be performed on-site within these counties. The Transformational Scholars Student Teaching Supervisor plays a vital role in supporting and mentoring student teachers participating in the Transformational Scholarship Program. This is a temporary, part-time position running from November to May. This program focuses on developing teacher leaders committed to serving rural eastern North Carolina communities. Supervisors will provide guidance, observation, feedback, and support to ensure student teachers' success while adhering to program requirements and donor stipulations. This position requires strong communication, collaboration, and organizational skills. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Relationship Building: Supervisors will foster strong working relationships with their assigned student teachers This involves initial meetings, planning sessions, and establishing effective communication channels. Supervision and Evaluation Supervise and provide regular feedback to assigned Transformational Scholars student teachers. Conduct formal observations, utilizing established rubrics, and provide constructive feedback to promote growth and development. Complete all required documentation and evaluations in a timely manner. This includes: Weekly check-in meetings (virtual or in-person) with each student teacher. Bi-weekly in-person visits to each student teacher's classroom. Mentoring and Support: Offer ongoing mentorship and support to student teachers, addressing challenges and celebrating successes. Serve as a liaison between student teachers, cooperating teachers, and university faculty. Assist in conflict resolution and provide guidance on best practices. Community Liaison: Actively connect student teachers with relevant community resources, organizations, and individuals. This may involve identifying and facilitating partnerships with local businesses, non-profits, community leaders, and other stakeholders to enrich the student teachers' learning experience and expand their professional networks. Supervisors will help student teachers leverage these community connections to benefit their students and teaching practice. Program Coordination: Collaborate with program coordinators and fellow supervisors to ensure the effective implementation of the program. Attend relevant meetings and contribute to the overall success of the Transformational Scholars Program. Curriculum Alignment: Ensure that student teaching placements align with the program curriculum and learning objectives. Work closely with cooperating teachers to provide relevant support and materials. Communication: Maintain consistent and clear communication with student teachers, cooperating teachers, program administrators, and other relevant stakeholders. Provide timely updates and address concerns effectively. Travel: Travel to various school districts in eastern North Carolina to supervise student teachers Temporary position Dates of employment: August 16th-May 15th 2026 This role will support student teachers placed in Harnett, Duplin, Samson, Edgecombe, and Wilson counties. It is ideal for someone within commuting distance to those areas, as the work will primarily be performed on-site within these counties. . Schedule: 5-12 hours a week, subject to change based on needs

title: Assistant Learning Specialist (Intern 2026-2027)
department: 240201 - Academic Support Program for Student Athletes
description: Division of Academic and Student Affairs The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State University. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Office of Academic Support Program for Student-Athletes (ASPSA) is a comprehensive support program that strives to meet the academic, personal and professional development needs of all student-athletes, promoting excellence and effectiveness in undergraduate and graduate education as well as leadership and civic engagement. The NC State Academic Support Program for Student-Athletes Internship Program has existed since 2005 and was recognized as the National Association of Academic and Student-Athlete Development Professionals (N4A) Model Practices Award winner in 2013. Position Purpose This full-time internship is intended to provide hands-on experience and prepare individuals to perform at a high level in full-time positions in academic support for student-athletes following the internship. Please note: Campus Parking pass cost $33-$40/month Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Meet with a caseload of under-prepared students to develop academic skills, time management skills, learning techniques, and content acquisition. Monitor academic progress and maintain communication with academic coordinators and supervisors. Collaborate with a team of learning specialists to support academically under-prepared student-athletes in one-on-one and group sessions. Develop and deliver professional development workshops for support staff, including academic mentors, writing assistants, and tutors Assist with screening, assessment, and the development of academic support plans in collaboration with ASPSA’s associate director and academic coordinators Facilitate at least one small group session to support students in a historically challenging course Co-lead a group of academically underprepared student-athletes participating in SummerStart in the development of academic skills necessary to transition to the college classroom Support students with educationally impacting disabilities in registering and accessing academic accommodations Co-teach University Studies Courses (USC), which are designed to support first-year student-athletes in their transition from high school through the first year of college studies. Other duties as assigned by the associate director/learning specialist

title: Student Success Navigators for Elevate (IPSE)
description: Note: This position is open only to currently enrolled NC State students who are in good academic standing. Primary purpose of this position: NC State’s inclusive postsecondary education program for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities, Elevate is seeking a motivated and reliable Student Success Navigator to support in study halls, courses to promote self-determined learning among Elevate students. This role provides the opportunity to support students individually and in small groups in developing skills such as time management, navigation, and assignment completion. Job Responsibilities: Provide 5 to 15 hours per week of support, including academic and social mentoring responsibilities Provide individualized academic support in study sessions and Elevate program or inclusive Courses Provide individualized support during Elevate’s Living Learning class or workshops Assist students with navigation, assignment planning, and time management, including use of Google Suite tools and other mobile applications Support Elevate students with independent living, social goal, and academic goal attainment including attending events/ activities and facilitating event/ activity registration Document activities completed with Elevate students, as instructed by Elevate staff Participate in trainings led by Social or Academic Peer Coaches or Elevate program staff Clearly communicate availability and provide adequate notice if scheduling conflicts arise Opportunities to serve as a job coach for on campus student employment internship(s) Eligibility Requirements: Must be an undergraduate or graduate student currently enrolled at NC State University Strong academic, organizational, and interpersonal skills Must have a passion for inclusion Proficiency with Google Suite tools and digital scheduling and communication mechanisms used by the Elevate program

title: Cybersecurity Program Operations Analyst
description: The Friday Institute for Educational Innovation is a large, multi-faceted Institute housed in a 33,000 square foot state-of-the-art facility on NC State University’s Centennial Campus in Raleigh. Our work encompasses educational research, professional development, policy and program evaluation, and direct services to schools, districts, state departments of education and public- and private sector organizations. We are deeply involved in work throughout North Carolina, leading some of the major statewide K-12 education initiatives and working closely with the Department of Public Instruction, the State Board of Education, and the majority of school districts in the State on the transition to digital teaching and learning. Since opening in 2005, the Friday Institute has developed a strong national presence, working with organizations throughout the country, and is increasingly developing international connections. More information is available at http://www.fi.ncsu.edu . The Friday Institute supports the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction (NCDPI) K-12 Cybersecurity Program , which organizes and aligns business and technical functions across the state so that the Public School Unit (PSU) will have greater visibility into the people, processes, and technologies deployed for cybersecurity. The goal of the program is to help PSUs achieve Strong Cyber Hygiene and this position will be entirely focused on supporting this program. The K-12 Cybersecurity Program has expanded significantly, and the core team requires additional project and operational support. Friday Institute seeks a K-12 Cybersecurity Program Operations Analyst to assist with program communications and reporting, outreach, knowledge management, data utilization and metrics, dashboard development, project coordination, and other routine but critical activities that keep the program organized and efficient. This is a time-limited contract-based position that will provide services in support of the K-12 Cybersecurity Program under the terms, scope, and period of performance established in the applicable contract. Continuation of the position is contingent upon contract requirements, funding availability, satisfactory performance, and any applicable renewal or extension of the contract. Work in a North Carolina PSU is ideal, but not required. Familiarity with general K-12 IT practices and cybersecurity are essential. Due to access to security-sensitive information, only U.S. citizens living in the state of North Carolina should apply. All work must be completed on a university provided and managed Macbook.

title: UTS - Temporary Donor Services Specialist at NC State
description: The Donor Services Specialist (Gift Agreements, Namings Opportunities, and Donor Services General Assistance) plays a vital role in supporting the team with researching and assisting with the review of gift agreements, naming opportunities, and related administrative processes. This position ensures the accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of donor documentation while providing general support to facilitate the team’s daily operations. We seek a highly organized, detail-oriented individual who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. The ideal candidate will have experience drafting and copyediting documents (AP style preferred), strong data analysis skills, and proficiency with Excel and other spreadsheet tools. Experience in finance, donor relations, or higher education is a plus. Excellent tracking abilities and typing skills are essential. In this role, you will support the management and coordination of gift agreements and naming opportunities across the university. It follows a hybrid work model, requiring two in-office days per week. Key responsibilities include: Conduct research and gather information related to gift agreements. Draft, edit, and refine documents, memos, correspondence, and proposals. Draft, review, and approve gift agreements to ensure accuracy and alignment with university standards. Assist in reviewing gifts and gift agreements for compliance with IRS regulations, CASE standards, university policies, best practices, and Advancement operational guidelines. Coordinate the review process with campus partners. Develop talking points and briefing materials for front-line fundraisers. Track and coordinate all processes related to gift agreements to ensure timely completion. Provide support in researching gift agreements, endowment histories, and related records. Conduct general research in support of Donor Services initiatives. Perform additional duties as assigned to support the overall operations of Donor Services. We’re looking for someone with attention to detail, strong writing/communication skills, and a collaborative spirit.

title: Associate Vice Provost and Director of Scholarships and Financial Aid
description: Reporting to the Senior Vice Provost for Enrollment Management, the Associate Vice Provost and Director of Scholarships and Financial Aid provides strategic and operational leadership for the university’s comprehensive financial aid and scholarship enterprise. Leading a large and complex operation, the position shapes institutional approaches to financial aid, affordability, and student support while ensuring effective stewardship of university resources and compliance with federal and state requirements. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to university and division leadership, translating policy, data, and emerging trends into strategies that advance enrollment, affordability, student success, and institutional priorities. You will shape financial aid policies and awarding methodologies, guide continuous improvement across operations and technology, and lead a high-performing team committed to service, collaboration, professional growth, and operational excellence. Key Areas of Responsibility: Strategic Leadership & Institutional Advising: Advise university and Enrollment Management leadership on financial aid policies and strategies affecting enrollment, affordability, student success, and institutional resources. Contribute to the development and implementation of strategic priorities for Enrollment Management and Services. Financial Aid Strategy & Compliance: Establish financial aid packaging methodologies and oversee federal, state, private, and institutional financial aid programs. Ensure financial aid operations and policies comply with applicable federal and state regulations. Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement: Lead continuous improvement of financial aid operations, technology, data use, compliance, and customer service practices. Exercise independent judgment in policy interpretation, awarding methodology, resource allocation, and operational priorities. Organizational & Collaborative Leadership: Lead a complex financial aid and scholarship operation while fostering service, collaboration, professional development, and operational excellence. Build strong partnerships across the university to advance shared enrollment and student success priorities. If you are a strategic financial aid leader who can translate complex policy, data, and operational challenges into thoughtful strategies that advance affordability, enrollment, and student success, we encourage you to apply.

title: Lecturer of Data Science
description: Join a collaborative community of instructors and help learners across and beyond NC State apply data science and AI in meaningful, real-world ways. The Data Science and AI Academy offers courses grounded in our ADAPT (All Campus Data Science and AI Project-based Teaching and Learning) course model. We seek instructors from industry, government and academia to teach permanent and special topics undergraduate courses at the 200 - 295 level (no prerequisites), 400 - 495 level (skills-based prerequisites) and graduate level courses at the 500 - 595 level. As an instructor with The Data Science and AI Academy,you will also join a professional teaching community that meets twice monthly to discuss data science and AI teaching and learning research and practice. The DSA occasionally offers not-for-credit customized courses through the Data and AI at Work program. We also seek applicants to teach these professional, customized and continuing education courses. For more information see example course topics here: https://datascienceacademy.ncsu.edu/courses/data-at-work/. The for-credit courses meet for 50 minutes once a week for a semester and can be delivered in person or online. Data and AI at Work (not-for-credit) courses have a customized schedule. For-Credit Course Offerings: Introduction to R/Python for Data Science, Introduction to Data Visualization, Data Communication, Introduction to AI Ethics, Data Science for Social Good, Introduction to Data Science for Cybersecurity Measuring Success Data Wrangling and Web Scraping, Exploratory Data Analysis for Big Data, Data Internships Preparation for Social Impact, Exploring Machine Learning, Predictive Analytics for Improving Services, Appointments will be for one or two semesters with the possibility of renewal. Note that this position is only for teaching a few (often just 1) credits, not full-time. If you are passionate about data science and enjoy helping others build practical skills, we invite you to bring your expertise and perspective to the Data Science and AI Academy.

title: UTS - Temporary Radiology Technician at NC State
description: The primary duties of this position include the following: Taking X-ray images of the human body per order by provider. Interact with internal staff, patients, and referring providers through email, phone, and in-person communications. Keeping equipment clean and in working order. Responsible for maintaining equipment and quality control. Attend scheduled meetings, drills, and training. Perform technical procedures, including patient positioning for radiographs and digital image capturing. Provide excellent patient care by applying full knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and disease processes. Provide quick and accurate information regarding each patient, acting as a liaison between clinicians and radiologists. Proficiently enter data into the electronic health record. Maintain a clean working environment to ensure standards are followed and infection is not spread. Handle medical, biological, and infectious waste appropriately. Follow all radiation safety, OSHA, and Environmental Health and Safety standards.

title: Crew Leader I
description: Join our dynamic Environmental Services team as a Crew Leader I, where you’ll lead essential projects, such as power washing entrances, window washing, waxing floors, and more. This role offers an exciting opportunity to guide a dedicated team, ensuring the cleanliness and functionality of campus spaces. You will be responsible for coordinating daily operations, resolving maintenance issues, and delivering excellent customer service . Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited: Lead projects, including power washing, window washing, floor waxing, and re-lamping fixtures and dispensers Inspect and verify maintenance discrepancies and ensure timely resolution Provide support to other zones as needed, filling in for vacant positions or absenteeism Collect and submit timesheets within established timelines Perform critical duties during adverse weather or emergencies as assigned Complete accident reports within 24 hours of an incident Assist with equipment inventory and maintain monthly inventory of storage closet supplies Submit supply orders for manager approval to ensure adequate stock levels Train new employees, ensuring they understand tasks and safety protocols Transport employees to various locations for assignments Collaborate with maintenance staff inside and outside the unit to resolve issues efficiently Address and resolve customer requests via radio communications, work orders, and direct interactions If you’re passionate about leadership and committed to maintaining a high standard of cleanliness, this role is for you!

title: Medical Lab Technologist
description: Lab technologist to perform routine testing in Cytology, Coagulation, Hematology, Chemistry, Special Chemistry, and Urinalysis. Perform accessioning and communicate with hospital clinicians and staff. Assist in training DVM students and new employees.

title: Assistant Director of Donor Relations and Stewardship
description: Are you a compelling storyteller with a passion for donor impact? The NC State College of Veterinary Medicine is looking for a dynamic professional to elevate the stewardship program. The Assistant Director of Donor Relations and Stewardship is responsible for developing and implementing both short- and long-term strategies to advance innovative and comprehensive donor engagement for supporters of the NC State College of Veterinary Medicine and the North Carolina Veterinary Medical Foundation. This role partners closely with the Assistant Dean of Philanthropy and advancement leadership to design, execute, and continuously strengthen stewardship, recognition, and engagement initiatives that deepen relationships and enhance philanthropic impact. Core Responsibilities Develop and execute strategic donor relations and stewardship plans that align with college and foundation priorities and support long-term donor retention and growth. Collaborate with advancement leadership to craft compelling language and messaging, stewardship communications, impact reporting, and broader engagement initiatives. Plan and execute in-person and virtual donor events both on campus and regionally, in partnership with the development team, ensuring a high-quality, mission-aligned donor experience. Coordinate donor meetings on and off campus, supporting donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship efforts. Manage the creation, production, and distribution of stewardship reports and donor communications that clearly articulate the impact of philanthropic support. Serve as a key resource to the CVM philanthropy team and university stewardship office to ensure coordinated and consistent donor engagement practices. Collaborate in broader strategic planning efforts to strengthen donor and volunteer engagement across the college. Oversee and enhance signature recognition programs, including the Walk of Honor and Gallop of Honor, ensuring effective program management and continued relevance.

title: Intermediate Care Veterinary Assistant
description: The Randall B. Terry Companion Animal Medical Center is seeking a highly skilled Patient Care Technician to join our Intermediate Care (IMC) department. This role is designed for a technician who thrives in a high-acuity environment and enjoys the balance of advanced clinical practice and clinical mentorship. As the primary technical point of contact for the IMC, you will manage complex hospitalizations, execute advanced treatment plans, and facilitate communication between specialty services, students, and clients. Core Responsibilities Advanced Clinical Intervention: Execute high-level technical procedures including long-term central venous access, TPN and chemotherapy administration, blood transfusions, and complex wound management. Case Coordination: Serve as the central liaison for the unit; admitting patients, synthesizing diagnostic updates, and ensuring the projected plan of care is communicated effectively to clinicians and students. Clinical Mentorship: Provide direct supervision and coaching to 4th-year veterinary students, interns, and residents, evaluating their technical proficiency and patient care standards. Patient Advocacy: Manage comprehensive post-operative monitoring and specialized drug administration, applying a deep understanding of anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology. Departmental Operations: Maintain rigorous infectious disease protocols, manage internal billing for procedures, and ensure the unit is stocked and transition-ready. Technical Qualifications Clinical Experience: Previous experience in a feline/canine veterinary setting is required. Communication: Proven ability to maintain professional composure and clear communication during emotionally charged or high-pressure situations. Technical Proficiency: Strong command of medical software, diagnostic equipment, and specialized pharmacology. Physical Standards: Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: HR Generalist for HR Data and Operations
description: The HR Generalist – HR Data & Operations serves as a front-line HR resource responsible for managing and auditing sensitive employee and position data within university HR systems. This role is fundamental to the integrity of college HR operations and records, ensuring the accuracy and security of personnel information while identifying opportunities to improve HR processes and reduce redundancies in workflows. As a vital member of the Wilson College of Textiles, you will support the only college in North America solely focused on textiles. Our faculty and researchers apply “textiles thinking” to solve the world’s grand challenges, from medical innovation to environmental sustainability. As the HR Generalist – HR Data & Operations , you provide the critical data integrity and operational stability that allow these world-class innovators to focus on their mission of global advancement. HR Data Management & Onboarding Independently manage and evaluate HR data transactions associated with new hires, job changes, and other employee lifecycle events, ensuring transactions are accurately processed and consistent with university requirements. Administer payroll and leave-related HR processes, including management and tracking of family medical leave and other leave types, and review leave balances and potential overdrawn leave situations to determine appropriate next steps. Manage student hiring and graduate appointment processes, including evaluating eligibility and ensuring appointments are processed in accordance with applicable university requirements. Process summer salary appointments and related additional compensation transactions. Review HR data and documentation to identify discrepancies, determine appropriate next steps within established policies and procedures, and coordinate resolution with central HR or other appropriate resources when necessary. Maintain electronic personnel records and serve as the college’s OnBase data custodian, ensuring records are maintained in accordance with applicable record retention, security, and confidentiality requirements. Manage I-9 and E-Verify processes, including applicable visa documentation, and identify employment eligibility or compliance issues requiring additional review or escalation to University Human Resources. System Auditing & Compliance Independently review HR workflows, transactions, and compliance requirements to identify errors, inconsistencies, process gaps, and areas of risk or noncompliance, and coordinate appropriate corrective actions. Use HR and business systems to develop, implement, and maintain HR processes and workflow tools that improve efficiency and reduce manual work. Analyze recurring data, compliance, and workflow issues to determine underlying causes and recommend appropriate process or system improvements. Reporting & Analytics Analyze HR data from multiple internal systems and data sources, including PeopleAdmin, PeopleSoft HR/FIN/SIS, and other institutional data sources, to identify trends, discrepancies, and operational issues and support college leadership’s evaluation of student hiring trends, ratios to measure performance, salary equity across job families, and other annual reporting needs. Evaluate the reliability and completeness of data sources, determine appropriate methods for compiling information, and develop and produce recurring and ad-hoc reports in response to operational and management needs. Interpret findings and communicate relevant trends, data issues, and recommendations to HR leadership and managers to support operational decision-making. Support, Guidance &Training Serve as a primary HR resource for managers and team members, providing guidance on HR data, position and employee transactions, HR systems, policies, procedures, and related administrative processes. Assess and resolve moderately complex HR process and system inquiries, identifying appropriate solutions, resolving issues independently, and escalating matters when appropriate. Coordinate HR services and processes with the HR team, college administrative units, and central university service areas, including onboarding, systems access, required training, compliance activities, and candidate interview logistics. Develop or deliver guidance for training and process needs on HR systems and processes, including time and leave management, performance management, and other tools that support effective HR administration. Participate in college committees and initiatives related to employee engagement, recognition, well-being, culture, and college-wide activities. If you are someone who takes pride in keeping things organized, enjoys solving problems, and approaches your work with care and sound judgment, we invite you to apply. If you value being a dependable resource for others, enjoy finding ways to make processes work better, and take pride in providing accurate, responsive service, we would welcome the opportunity to have you join the Wilson College of Textiles HR team.

title: Utilities Distribution Technician
description: Join NC State University’s Utilities and Engineering team as a Utilities Distribution Technician and play a hands-on role in maintaining the essential infrastructure that keeps our campus operating safely and reliably. This position supports NC State’s Main, Centennial, and CBC campuses , performing skilled mechanical and piping work, diagnostics, maintenance, and repairs on critical utility systems, including steam tunnels, pump stations, heat exchangers, pressure-reducing valves (PRVs), and grease traps . You’ll have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects, from routine maintenance and repairs to new construction, renovations, and welding projects , while helping ensure reliable utility services for research, academic, and animal hospital facilities. If you enjoy troubleshooting, hands-on work, and solving mechanical challenges that make a meaningful impact, we invite you to apply and become part of the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Diagnose and repair equipment such as fans, pumps, receivers, steam lines, condensate lines, and pressure-reducing stations. Inspect, maintain, and repair steam and hot water systems, including components like traps, strainers, expansion joints, and piping. Utilize welding technologies for torch work, including welding, brazing, soldering, and cutting, and fabricate parts from blueprints, sketches, and verbal instructions. Install, operate, maintain, and rebuild mechanical pumps, PRVs, and associated piping and equipment. Cut, thread, solder, and assemble piping; connect valves and test gas, water, sanitary, and storm lines; eliminate leaks and replace faulty fittings. Test and certify backflow preventers, conduct fire hydrant flow tests, and perform inspections of wastewater collection systems, including grease traps and SSOs. Conduct annual inspections of wastewater distribution systems and report findings to the Environmental Engineer and shop supervisor. Align motors and pumps, set frames, and install related equipment such as fans, PRVs, and turbines for steam generation and control. Serve as backup ORC for wastewater collection system compliance, ensuring adherence to permit requirements. Anticipate, identify, and address customer service needs by balancing multiple priorities, ensuring repairs or solutions meet expectations, and fostering positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including vendors and subcontractors, while proactively developing options, implementing solutions, and verifying customer satisfaction.

title: Data Science Lead
description: The Data Science Lead will play a pivotal role in advancing NC State’s data and analytics capabilities. Applying advanced analytical and statistical techniques, methods, and tools, this role will develop and implement predictive models and other sophisticated analytics solutions. Working within University Data and Analytics (UDA), the Data Science Lead oversees a specialized team of up to three data scientists dedicated to developing and delivering analytical products and services that provide actionable insights, drive strategic decision-making, and enhance overall institutional effectiveness. As the Data Science Lead, you will oversee a small team of data scientists responsible for developing advanced analytical solutions that support institutional planning and decision-making at NC State. You will apply statistical methods, predictive modeling, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to analyze complex university data and address institutional needs and uncover insights that support better outcomes. Additionally, you will coordinate data science projects, collaborate with partners across University Data and Analytics (UDA), and provide day-to-day leadership and supervision of the Data Science team. Key Impact Areas include: Develop Advanced Analytics Solutions: Design, develop, and optimize predictive models, artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions, and other advanced analytics to address university needs and support institutional decision-making. Supervise and Support the Data Science Team: Provide day-to-day supervision and leadership for the Data Science team, including coordinating work assignments, setting team priorities, coaching and developing staff, managing performance, and supporting a collaborative environment focused on continuous improvement and high-quality work. Collaborate Across UDA: Partner with Institutional Reporting, Research and Analysis, Business Intelligence, Data Governance, UDA leadership, and other stakeholders to provide data science expertise and support cross-functional initiatives. Coordinate Data Science Projects: Coordinate the execution of data science initiatives by tracking project progress, facilitating collaboration among stakeholders, managing project timelines and risks, and supporting alignment with UDA and institutional priorities. Support Responsible and Reliable Data Science Practices: Apply appropriate practices for model development and evaluation, data governance, security, privacy, and ethical use to support accurate, reliable, and responsible analytical solutions. If you are a person who has strong technical data science expertise, experience working with complex data and analytical problems, and the ability to supervise and support a small team of data scientists, we encourage you to apply.

title: Microbiology Laboratory Research Technician
description:
Posting Number: PG195197SP
Internal Recruitment: No
Working Title: Microbiology Laboratory Research Technician
Anticipated Hiring Range: Commensurate with experience ($45,000 - $47,746)
Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8 am - 5 pm
Job Location: Raleigh, NC
Department: Plant & Microbial Biology
About the Department: The Kleiner Lab studies plant and animal microbiomes using a diversity of cultivation-dependent and independent approaches. We seek to understand how functional interactions between organisms lead to beneficial or detrimental outcomes for the host. One of the core approaches that we use is high-resolution mass spectrometry-based metaproteomics. The Kleiner Lab is part of the NCSU Chancellor’s Excellence Cluster on Microbiomes and Complex Microbial Communities, which provides a vibrant community of researchers at NCSU and frequent exchanges with the community across campus. The Kleiner Lab is involved in collaborative research at NCSU , nationally, and internationally.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. What we offer: Medical , Dental , and Vision Flexible Spending Account Retirement Programs Disability Plans Life Insurance Accident Plan Paid Time Off and Other Leave Programs 12 Holidays Each Year Tuition and Academic Assistance And so much more! Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare benefits, Wellness & Recreation Membership , and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community. Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part-Time or Full-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.
Essential Job Duties: The Kleiner Lab at North Carolina State University is seeking a Research Technician to support research focused on complex microbial communities, microbial symbioses, and metaproteomics. Reporting to the Kleiner Lab research team, this position contributes to the design, execution, and analysis of experiments that advance the lab’s research program and generate findings for publications, conference presentations, and grant development. You will work in a dynamic, collaborative research environment where your technical expertise and attention to detail directly contribute to ongoing scientific projects. Additionally, you will assist with laboratory management, including maintaining safety documentation and compliance, coordinating undergraduate research assistant schedules, and overseeing equipment purchasing, maintenance, and repair. Key Responsibilities: Manage multiple concurrent research projects and coordinate day-to-day research activities. Cultivate and maintain bacterial cultures and perform molecular and biochemical assays. Compile, analyze, and interpret experimental data to support research objectives. Contribute to research outcomes through publications, conference presentations, and grant development. If you are a detail-oriented and collaborative researcher who enjoys hands-on laboratory work, managing multiple priorities, and contributing to meaningful scientific discovery, this is an opportunity to make a direct impact on the Kleiner Lab’s research and day-to-day operations. Your technical skills, organization, and commitment to high-quality research will help advance projects investigating the complex interactions within microbial communities.
Other Responsibilities: Depending on funding availability and project priorities, up to two weeks of travel per year may be required for project meetings, fieldwork, and the annual research group retreat. During fieldwork, the Research Technician will work as part of a small research team at agricultural research stations or marine field stations, supporting logistics, sample collection, and sample processing.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Gene cloning for heterologous protein expression, protein purification, and enzyme assays. Operation of analytical HPLC and high-resolution, accurate-mass mass spectrometry systems for proteomics research, including instruments such as Thermo Exploris or Astral. Proteomics data analysis and basic Linux command-line skills for running bioinformatics tools. Fluorescence in situ hybridization, advanced microscopy, or related imaging techniques. Field research and/or ultracentrifugation using density gradients for subcellular fractionation.
Required License or Certification: A valid NC Driver’s License and the ability to obtain an NC Driver’s License within 60 days of hire. A valid Driver’s License must be maintained throughout employment.
Valid NC Driver's License required: Yes
Commercial Driver's License Required?: No

title: Facilities Maintenance Technician - Journey
description: Join NC State University’s Building Maintenance and Operations (BMO) team as a Facilities Maintenance Technician – Journey Level and put your hands-on mechanical skills to work supporting a safe, reliable, and comfortable campus environment. This position performs skilled maintenance, installation, troubleshooting, and repair of HVAC, piping, insulation, plumbing, steam, and other building mechanical systems . You’ll work with a variety of systems, from domestic and chilled water to steam, gas, air, and waste systems, while also supporting HVAC controls and secondary electrical systems. This role is ideal for a skilled trades professional who enjoys problem-solving, working with their hands, and finding practical solutions to both routine and complex maintenance challenges . If you take pride in quality workmanship, enjoy collaborating with other trades, and want your skills to make a direct impact on the NC State campus, we invite you to apply today and become part of the Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Perform maintenance and repairs on domestic water, chilled water, hot water, steam piping, and ductwork insulation . Perform preventive maintenance on plumbing and building systems , including air, gas, water, and waste systems. Install, maintain, and repair plumbing systems and fixtures , including lab drainage, sinks, toilets, valves, and piping. Cut, thread, assemble, and install piping; connect valves; caulk joints; and test installations for leaks and defects. Install and maintain gas, water, and sanitary fixtures, including appropriate supports, hangers, and foundations. Diagnose and troubleshoot mechanical and plumbing issues , including complex and non-standard repairs, and develop effective solutions. Support troubleshooting and maintenance of secondary electrical systems up to 600 VAC , including conduit, breakers, switches, panels, motors, and control circuits. Assist with HVAC preventive maintenance and repairs , including temperature controls, thermostats, humidity sensors, and regulators. Troubleshoot and repair steam systems and related equipment , including boilers, pumps, turbines, condensate systems, and air compressors. Collaborate with HVAC, electrical, mechanical, and other trades to resolve multi-system issues and complete maintenance projects safely and effectively . Follow established safety procedures, regulations, and university standards while performing all work. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follows verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs. Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations. Lift, carry, and maneuver materials weighing 60–90 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Social Media Manager, Enterprise Content
description: The Social Media Manager for Enterprise Content helps shape how NC State connects with its audiences across the university’s official social media channels. As a member of the Social Media Hub within University Communications and Marketing, this role manages the day-to-day creation, publishing and community engagement that bring the university’s stories to life. From faculty research and student experiences to major university events, the Social Media Manager turns complex ideas and moments into timely, engaging digital content. In this hands-on role you will be a part of shaping the @NCState social presence, combining digital storytelling, short-form video production and community management to connect people with the university and with one another. You’ll have the opportunity to be where the action is through conceptualizing and capturing content, covering events in real time, collaborating with students, faculty, staff and alumni, and responding to the conversations happening across NC State’s social channels. The Wolfpack community and the university’s communication priorities will be strengthened through your efforts. These efforts will include these key impact areas and responsibilities: Manage daily social content and community engagement across official enterprise channels, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube and TikTok. Create social-first stories and short-form video from concept through filming and editing, translating university priorities, research, events and experiences into compelling content. Capture the university in the moment through live social coverage of events and timely content that keeps audiences connected to what’s happening across NC State. Build meaningful community connections by monitoring conversations, trends and emerging issues; responding thoughtfully to comments and interactions; and appropriately managing sensitive content. Collaborate across the university with students, faculty, staff, alumni and student content creators to develop authentic, audience-focused content aligned with enterprise social strategy. Use social insights and performance data to understand what resonates with audiences and inform future content and engagement strategies. If you’re a creative storyteller who thrives in a fast-paced environment, brings strong communication and collaboration skills, and enjoys finding new ways to connect people through social media, we encourage you to apply.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Psychology is seeking an Assistant Professor to advance research, teaching, and service in applied social psychology. This position requires the establishment of an independent research program with demonstrated or potential for external funding, dissemination of scholarship through scholarly outlets, teaching and mentorship of undergraduate and graduate students, and service to the Applied Social Psychology program area, department, college, university, and broader field. As an Assistant Professor, you will conduct a productive program of research that contributes meaningful scholarship to the discipline and strengthens the department’s research profile. You will teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, helping them develop as scholars and professionals, while contributing your expertise to the continued growth of the program and the broader discipline. Key Responsibilities: Develop and sustain an independent, externally funded research program. Disseminate research through scholarly publications, presentations, and other professional outlets. Teach courses that support undergraduate and graduate education in psychology. Mentor undergraduate and graduate students in their academics, research, and professional development. Contribute service and professional leadership within the Applied Social Psychology program area, department, college, university, and broader field. If you are an emerging scholar in applied social psychology who is excited to build a meaningful research program, engage students through teaching and mentorship, and contribute to a collaborative academic community, we encourage you to apply.

title: Director of Philanthropic Strategy & Prospect Management
description: The Director of Philanthropic Strategy & Prospect Management serves as the College of Engineering’s strategic advisor on fundraising performance, portfolio optimization, campaign readiness, and prospect strategy. This position partners closely with the Assistant Dean for Philanthropy and frontline fundraisers to maximize philanthropic results through data-informed decision making, fundraising analytics, CRM leadership, and strategic portfolio management. Rather than serving solely as a prospect manager, this role functions as a strategic partner to fundraising leadership by helping ensure gift officers are focused on the highest-impact opportunities and equipped with the information, systems, and strategy necessary to maximize fundraising success. Core Responsibilities 1. Philanthropic Strategy Provide strategic guidance that strengthens fundraising performance across the College. Key Responsibilities Serve as strategic advisor to the Assistant Dean and Executive Director on fundraising priorities and campaign readiness. Lead portfolio optimization and prospect assignment strategies. Facilitate prospect strategy meetings with frontline fundraisers. Identify opportunities, risks, and trends within all levels of the major gift fundraising pipeline – focusing on the continuum from major gift discovery to major gifts to principal giving. Develop recommendations to maximize fundraising productivity and philanthropic outcomes. Support campaign planning and principal gift pipeline development. 2. Prospect Management Lead the strategic management of prospect portfolios to maximize fundraiser effectiveness. Key Responsibilities Oversee portfolio management and assignment processes. Monitor prospect movement through the donor pipeline. Ensure portfolio health and accountability. Conduct regular portfolio reviews with gift officers. Coordinate closely with University Advancement Prospect Development on prospect management and research, working closely with analysts on research projects to fill fundraiser portfolios & gaps. Develop recommendations for prospect assignment and portfolio balancing. 3. CRM Strategy & Salesforce (Lobo) Leadership Serve as the College’s functional expert for Salesforce (Lobo), ensuring the CRM effectively supports fundraising strategy and frontline success. Key Responsibilities Serve as the College of Engineering’s primary functional lead for Salesforce (Lobo). Partner with University Advancement on CRM implementation, enhancements, testing, and user adoption. Develop best practices, workflows, and business processes within Salesforce. Train and support frontline fundraisers in the effective use of the CRM. Ensure data quality and consistency across fundraising operations. Translate fundraising needs into CRM solutions that improve efficiency and effectiveness. Identify opportunities to leverage Salesforce to improve fundraising performance and reporting. 4. Fundraising Analytics & Performance Provide meaningful data and analysis that informs leadership decisions and drives fundraising success. Key Responsibilities Develop executive dashboards and performance reports in Salesforce that track activity, strategy and pipeline health. Monitor fundraising KPIs and portfolio metrics. Analyze pipeline health and fundraising trends. Forecast fundraising performance and campaign progress. Track proposal activity and donor movement. Produce regular reports that support strategic decision making by the Assistant Dean and fundraising leadership.

title: Assistant Director, Facilities HR Programs
description: The Assistant Director of Facilities Human Resources (FHR) serves as a key member of the Facilities Human Resources leadership team and provides strategic direction, oversight, and continuous improvement for a comprehensive portfolio of HR programs that support the employee lifecycle across the Facilities Division. Reporting directly to the Director of Facilities Human Resources, this position leads a team of 3-4 HR professionals and is responsible for advancing division-wide initiatives related to talent acquisition, onboarding, training and development, engagement and recognition . As a trusted HR leader and consultant, the Assistant Director works collaboratively with Facilities executives, managers, supervisors, employees, and University Human Resources to ensure the delivery of responsive, consistent, and high-quality HR services that support the division's operational goals and NC State University's strategic priorities. The position plays a critical role in fostering a positive workplace culture by developing programs and practices that enhance employee engagement, strengthen workforce capability, promote employee success, and support long-term talent retention. This role combines strategic program leadership, staff supervision, workforce analytics, change management, and process improvement . The Assistant Director evaluates organizational needs, identifies emerging workforce trends, and implements innovative solutions designed to improve the employee experience and operational effectiveness. The position also serves as a senior HR advisor on complex employee and organizational issues, providing guidance that balances business needs, policy compliance, legal requirements, and employee well-being. This position offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on the Facilities Division by shaping HR programs, developing talent, improving organizational processes, and ensuring employees have the resources and support necessary to thrive and contribute to the University's mission. Individuals who are passionate about building innovative HR programs, developing people, leading teams, solving complex organizational challenges, and creating meaningful workplace improvements are encouraged to apply and join the Facilities Human Resources team at NC State University. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Provide strategic leadership and oversight for division-wide programs related to recruitment, onboarding, employee development, engagement and recognition . Lead the design, implementation, assessment, and continuous improvement of HR initiatives that enhance the employee experience and support Facilities Division goals. Oversee recruitment and talent acquisition strategies , partnering with leaders and hiring managers to strengthen hiring practices and improve the attraction, selection, and retention of high-quality talent. Oversee onboarding programs that ensure a welcoming, informative, and consistent experience for new employees while supporting successful integration into the organization. Assess organizational and workforce development needs and implement training, leadership development, mentoring, e-learning, and professional growth opportunities for employees and supervisors. Develop and execute employee engagement initiatives by analyzing survey results, feedback, workforce trends, and organizational data to identify opportunities for improvement. Manage employee recognition programs that celebrate achievements, reinforce organizational values, and promote a culture of appreciation and belonging. Supervise, coach, mentor, and evaluate a team of HR professionals , establishing performance expectations and ensuring high-quality, customer-focused service delivery. Research and analyze complex HR issues and develop practical, compliant, and business-focused solutions aligned with University policies, employment regulations, and organizational priorities. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with Facilities leadership, University Human Resources, and campus partners to ensure consistent application of HR practices and successful implementation of initiatives. Utilize workforce data, operational metrics, and employee feedback to evaluate program effectiveness, identify trends, and support strategic decision-making. Develop and deliver presentations, training programs, communications, reports, and recommendations to a variety of stakeholders, including senior leadership. Monitor changes in HR best practices, employment law, higher education trends, and workforce strategies and recommend program enhancements as appropriate. Lead HR technology initiatives and process improvement efforts, including collaboration on the continued enhancement and utilization of AiM and other HR systems to improve data management, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency. Support organizational change initiatives and special projects that advance Facilities Division and University objectives.

Opening and processing plant root masses in the laboratory to extract, collect, and document beetle larvae using hand tools and following established laboratory protocols. title: Facilities Maintenance Technician - Contributing
description: ​Join NC State University’s Building Maintenance and Operations (BMO) team as a Facilities Maintenance Technician – Contributing and build your skills while helping keep our campus facilities safe, reliable, and operating at their best. This hands-on position works within a zone maintenance shop on NC State’s Original Campus, Centennial Campus, or Centennial Biomedical Campus (Veterinary School) and supports routine maintenance, operations, and repairs across building systems. In this role, you’ll develop practical experience across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, steam, and other building systems while working alongside experienced mechanics and technicians. You’ll perform preventive maintenance, assist with repairs, operate basic tools and equipment, monitor equipment, identify potential problems, and know when to elevate more complex issues to higher-level mechanics. If you’re dependable, hands-on, eager to learn, and interested in developing your skills in the skilled trades, we invite you to apply and become part of the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Perform basic maintenance, preventive maintenance, and repairs across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, steam, and other building systems . Assist higher-level mechanics with maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, installations, and other assigned work. Perform routine tasks such as lubricating, cleaning, inspecting, re-lamping, repairing plumbing fixtures, and checking equipment . Take readings on boilers, chillers, and other equipment; check chemical levels and report unusual conditions or discrepancies. Recognize signs of equipment or system problems, including leaks, unusual noises, temperature changes, electrical outages, and equipment malfunctions. Troubleshoot basic maintenance issues and determine potential causes. Operate and maintain the basic tools and equipment used in assigned trades and follow appropriate procedures for each task. Follow preventive maintenance work orders and maintenance requests, completing assigned work accurately and within established timelines. Accurately document work performed, including time, materials, equipment readings, and identified issues . Develop working knowledge across multiple building systems and cross-train in building equipment operations and maintenance. Properly isolate and lock out equipment and systems as required before performing maintenance or repairs. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment and follow all University safety, health, and established safe-work practices. Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations. Lift, carry, and maneuver materials weighing 60–90 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follows verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Research Engineer
description: Reactor Operations and Training: Receive comprehensive training to obtain licensure as a Senior Reactor Operator from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). System Design and Maintenance: Participate in the design, installation, testing, operation, and maintenance of reactor plant and experimental facility systems. Procedure and Protocol Development: Develop detailed specifications for reactor and experiment system components, including design requirements and operational and maintenance procedures. Create and implement laboratory safety and radiation protection procedures and protocols to support reactor research. Computational Modeling and Simulation: Formulate and execute reactor core and system simulations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to ensure safe reactor operation. Research and Development: Design experimental facilities and conduct complex research utilizing computational resources. Formulate research methodologies and propose enhancements to improve research quality. Documentation and Publication: Contribute to project documentation and reporting, author scholarly papers, and support the development of proposals for new projects. Nuclear System Analysis: Perform nuclear system simulations, experimental facility design, and nuclear data generation to support the safe operation of the PULSTAR nuclear research reactor. Utilize HPC resources to run atomistic simulation, nuclear data generation, and radiation transport codes.

title: Director of Research Communications
description: This is an internal posting for current NC State permanent and temporary employees, and candidates with RIF priority. The University Communications team is seeking a skilled research communicator and collaborative leader to shape how the university’s research and innovation enterprise is understood, valued, and shared. This position leads enterprise-wide research communications that translate complex discoveries, expertise, and innovation into clear, compelling narratives for the audiences who influence NC State’s reputation, resources, and impact—including news media, policymakers, peer institutions, donors, partners, prospective students, faculty, and the public. In this role, you will serve as the university’s strategic communications partner to the research enterprise, working across University Communications and Marketing and closely with the Vice Chancellor for Communications and Marketing and the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation. You will shape research storytelling and national and trade media visibility, connect research communicators across the university, and help position NC State’s discoveries and expertise in conversations that matter beyond campus. Your ability to move comfortably between the laboratory and the newsroom will be essential—you will build trust with researchers, identify the stories behind their work, and make complex research meaningful to audiences who may never read the original paper. Key responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Research Storytelling and Content Strategy: Shape the university’s research narrative and content strategy, identifying and elevating compelling stories across fundamental discovery, translational science, interdisciplinary research, and community-engaged scholarship for audiences and platforms that extend NC State’s reach and influence. Translate complex scientific and technical work into compelling, accessible narratives that maintain research rigor while connecting discovery to the people, questions, and real-world impact behind the work. Develop enterprise research communications strategy in alignment with the division’s integrated communications strategy and NC State’s “Think and Do” brand, message pillars, and visual standards. Earned Media and National Visibility for Research: Expand NC State’s national and industry visibility as a research and innovation leader through proactive media strategy and outreach that increases share of voice and positions faculty as trusted experts on issues of consequence. Orchestrate communications around high-impact research moments, including major discoveries, awards, rankings, funding, and other milestones, in partnership with the division’s media relations function. Cultivate relationships with science, research, trade, and industry journalists while strengthening faculty readiness to serve as credible, compelling expert sources. Campus Research Communications Network: Lead and strengthen a university-wide research communications network spanning colleges, centers, institutes, and the Office of Research and Innovation, creating greater alignment, visibility, and strategic value while respecting decentralized ownership. Connect communicators, research leadership, faculty, and University Communications and Marketing around shared priorities, creating coordinated pathways for identifying, developing, and amplifying research stories across university channels. Establish shared standards, story pipelines, and collaborative practices that increase the consistency, efficiency, and reach of research communications across the enterprise. Issues and Sensitive Research Communications Provide strategic counsel on emerging and sensitive research-related issues, helping ensure accurate, timely, and coordinated communications in partnership with university leadership and the division’s issues and crisis communications function. Navigate and translate an evolving federal research funding and policy environment, helping internal and external audiences understand implications for NC State’s research enterprise in coordination with the Office of Research and Innovation, legal counsel, and divisional partners. Guide coordinated research communications during periods of disruption or heightened scrutiny, including funding changes, policy transitions, leadership changes, and other issues affecting the university’s research mission and reputation. Collaboration, Culture, and Operations Leverage the division’s existing digital, editorial, marketing, and communications infrastructure to strengthen the reach and effectiveness of research storytelling across web, marketing, and other strategic channels. Lead and develop assigned communications staff, fostering a high-performing, collaborative culture grounded in professional growth, strong execution, and shared accountability. Use audience insight, analytics, and performance measures to strengthen communications strategy, continuously refining storytelling, channels, and engagement based on what advances organizational goals. Oversee external partners, vendors, and project delivery for research communications initiatives, ensuring resources and timelines support strategic priorities. If you are a strategic communicator who can move seamlessly between scientific discovery, institutional strategy, and compelling storytelling, we encourage you to apply and help shape how NC State’s research and innovation are understood, valued, and shared with the world.
