title: Director of Information Technology
description: Are you a visionary technology leader who is passionate about driving innovation, building high-performing teams, and advancing academic excellence through technology? We are seeking a Director of Information Technology to lead and oversee IT operations for the College of Sciences and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of technology across teaching, research, and administration. In this influential leadership position, The Director of Information Technology will direct, manage, and provide strategic technology support for faculty, staff, postdoctoral researchers, and students across six academic departments. The Director serves as a trusted advisor, technology advocate, and change leader, ensuring IT resources effectively support the College's mission and goals. Reporting the Dean of the College of Sciences, the Director of Information Technology will be at the forefront of technological advancement, helping create innovative solutions that enhance instruction, research, and operational excellence. The Director will lead a talented team of IT professionals while collaborating with university leadership to develop forward-thinking technology strategies that support the evolving needs of higher education. What You'll Do Drive Strategic Technology Leadership Develop and execute IT strategies aligned with the College's mission and long-term objectives. Lead strategic planning, innovation initiatives, and resource allocation. Identify emerging technologies that enhance teaching, research, and administrative effectiveness. Oversee IT Operations & Infrastructure Manage the deployment, maintenance, upgrade, and support of hardware, software, servers, operating systems, and networked resources. Ensure IT systems remain reliable, secure, scalable, and responsive to user needs. Support instructional and administrative computing services throughout the College. Maintain clear and consistent communication with leadership, faculty, staff, and end users regarding technology initiatives. Lead and Develop High-Performing Teams Provide leadership, mentorship, and professional development opportunities for IT staff. Foster a collaborative, service-oriented team culture. Oversee recruitment, retention, training, and supervision of technical support personnel, including student employees. Manage Budgets and Technology Investments Develop and administer annual IT budgets. Ensure effective stewardship of resources and maximize return on technology investments. Lead procurement efforts for IT hardware, software, and services. Champion Security, Compliance & Continuity Establish and enforce policies that safeguard the integrity, privacy, and security of institutional data and technology assets. Ensure compliance with applicable regulations and industry standards. Lead disaster recovery and business continuity planning efforts. Provide strategic guidance on technology needs for classrooms, laboratories, buildings, and future facilities. Lead Technology Projects Oversee complex IT projects from planning through implementation. Deliver projects on time, within scope, and within budget. Collaborate with departments to identify technology needs and implement effective solutions. Build Strong Partnerships Serve as the primary IT resource for faculty, staff, and departmental leadership. Collaborate with vendors, service providers, and campus partners to ensure exceptional technology support. Provide proactive guidance for instructional, research, and administrative technology needs. This role extends beyond departmental leadership. The Director will represent and advocate for the College's technology interests on key university-wide committees and initiatives, including: IT Strategic Advisory Committee Academic IT Directors Committee Campus IT Directors Committee Data Science and AI Initiatives Other University Technology Governance Groups This is an exceptional opportunity for a forward-thinking technology leader to shape and advance the College's technology strategy. The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker, collaborative leader, and skilled IT professional who can balance operational excellence with innovation. They excel in dynamic environments, build strong relationships across varied stakeholder groups, and are committed to delivering exceptional technology services that support teaching, learning, research, and administrative success. Through leadership, vision, and partnership, this individual will help drive transformative technology initiatives that advance the College's mission and position it for the future. If you're ready to lead transformative technology initiatives, inspire a talented team, and make a lasting impact on the future of education and research, we encourage you to apply today and help drive innovation, collaboration, and excellence through technology.

title: Financial Operations Supervisor
description: As the Financial Operations Supervisor, you will serve as a strategic financial anchor within the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS), providing direct leadership and accounting oversight for a centralized financial operations team. Reporting to the Director of Business Services, you will safeguard the integrity, accuracy, and compliance of high-risk transactions across a complex multi-funding environment—including federal (USDA NIFA, Hatch, Smith-Lever), state, and receipt-supported funds within CALS’ unique Ledger 4 structure. In this high-impact role, your expertise will directly mitigate regulatory risk, ensure audit readiness, and maintain the university's trusted financial standing. In this role, you will turn complex accounting requirements into seamless, efficient operations. By fostering a collaborative and accountable team culture, you will empower your staff to master intricate cost principles while serving as a supportive mentor who elevates their professional growth. Your direct influence will bridge the gap between central administration and non-financial department stakeholders, translating dense federal regulations into clear, actionable guidance. Ultimately, you will drive continuous improvement, building robust internal controls that allow the college’s critical research and extension programs to thrive with complete financial confidence. Key responsibilities will fall within the following functional areas: Leadership & Team Supervision Provide direct supervision, coaching, and performance management, cultivating a collaborative team culture focused on accountability, precision, and service excellence. Optimize Capacity: Assign, prioritize, and balance workloads across functional areas (AP, AR, Travel, P-Card) to maximize operational efficiency and maintain compliance standards. Design robust onboarding programs to ensure the team thoroughly understands core accounting principles, financial systems, and funding-specific requirements. Identify recurring operational bottlenecks and implement standardized workflows, proactively guiding corrective actions to improve team accuracy. Financial Oversight & Transaction Review Review and approve complex transactions, using critical evaluation to ensure accurate accounting treatment across federal, state, and receipt-supported funds. Direct staff analysis of CALS’ Ledger 4 project structures to guarantee correct funding source identification and regulatory framework application. Oversee reconciliation processes to ensure data accuracy, applying sound judgment to resolve financial discrepancies promptly. Serve as a key decision-maker and escalation point for ambiguous or high-risk financial and compliance issues, applying relevant accounting principles and policy precedents Policy, Compliance & Internal Controls Interpret and apply complex regulatory guidelines—including USDA NIFA, Hatch, Hatch Multistate, and Smith-Lever requirements—ensuring strict allowability and allocability. Oversee and strengthen internal controls, including segregation of duties and documentation standards, to ensure audit readiness and mitigate compliance risk Address identified control weaknesses, monitor audit findings, and implement long-term solutions to prevent recurrence. Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory Communicate intricate policy requirements, financial decisions, and process changes into clear, user-friendly guidance for faculty, staff, and non-financial partners. Serve as a diplomatic liaison between central university offices, CORE Support, and academic departments to streamline financial operations and resolve escalated concerns. Represent the financial operations unit in campus-wide meetings, championing collaborative solutions for system and workflow enhancements If you are a financial professional who enjoys leading a team, solving complex problems, and helping others navigate challenging financial and regulatory requirements, this role offers an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.. If you are a financial professional who takes pride in leading a team, solving complex problems, and providing thoughtful guidance, we invite you to apply.

Lead proactive storytelling that highlights student success, faculty achievement, and institutional and research impact. Partner with research leadership to increase visibility in prestige, trade, and industry media. Align executive communications with broader reputation and media strategy to ensure consistency and trust. title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Abolhasani Research Group in the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering at North Carolina State University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scholar to develop artificial intelligence and machine learning methods for autonomous scientific experimentation as part of the NSF-funded SPEED Programmable Cloud Laboratory. The successful candidate will develop AI/ML methodologies that enable autonomous laboratories to learn from experimental data, select informative experiments, optimize complex chemical and materials systems, and generate transferable scientific knowledge. Research topics may include Bayesian optimization, active learning, uncertainty quantification, representation learning, multimodal scientific data, surrogate modeling, sequential decision-making, and AI-driven experimental design. A major emphasis will be translating AI/ML methodology into algorithms that operate directly with automated experimental platforms and real-world experimental data. Duties and Responsibilities include: Develop AI/ML algorithms for autonomous experimental design and optimization. Develop surrogate models and uncertainty-aware approaches for learning from sparse and heterogeneous experimental datasets. Develop chemical and materials representations suitable for closed-loop experimental optimization. Implement Bayesian optimization, active learning, and related sequential experimental-design methods. Develop methods for incorporating prior knowledge and historical experimental datasets into experimental decision-making. Integrate AI/ML algorithms with SPEED automated experimental platforms. Analyze multimodal experimental datasets and identify scientifically meaningful structure-property-processing relationships. Evaluate algorithm performance using both benchmark datasets and physical experimental campaigns. Develop reusable software modules and documented computational workflows. Collaborate closely with experimental scientists, automation engineers, and SPEED users. Prepare peer-reviewed publications, presentations, technical reports, and research proposals.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Abolhasani Research Group in the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering at North Carolina State University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scholar to develop next-generation self-driving laboratories and autonomous experimentation technologies as part of the NSF-funded SPEED (Self-driving Platforms for Expedited Experimental co-Design) Programmable Cloud Laboratory. The successful candidate will develop and deploy closed-loop experimental platforms that integrate automated synthesis and experimentation, real-time characterization, data analysis, and AI/ML-based experiment selection. The research will focus on creating modular, reliable, and user-accessible autonomous laboratories for accelerated discovery and optimization in chemistry and materials science. Highly motivated candidates with experience in laboratory automation, autonomous experimentation, robotics, scientific instrumentation, process control, or related areas are encouraged to apply. Experience with Python-based automation and integration of laboratory hardware and analytical instruments is highly desirable. The successful candidate will work in a highly interdisciplinary environment involving chemical engineers, chemists, materials scientists, computer scientists, AI/ML researchers, and external academic and industrial partners. Duties and Responsibilities include: Design, develop, and deploy self-driving laboratory platforms for autonomous chemical and materials experimentation. Integrate synthesis, sample handling, analytical characterization, and data-processing tools into automated experimental workflows. Develop Python-based interfaces for laboratory hardware and scientific instruments. Implement closed-loop workflows connecting experimental platforms with AI/ML experiment-selection algorithms. Develop methods for automated calibration, fault detection, error recovery, and experimental quality control. Establish standardized workflows and interfaces that allow experimental platforms to be used by external SPEED users. Conduct autonomous and high-throughput experimental campaigns. Analyze experimental data and evaluate the performance and robustness of autonomous workflows. Collaborate with SPEED researchers in chemistry, materials science, AI/ML, data science, and automation. Prepare manuscripts, presentations, technical documentation, and regular project reports. Meet regularly with the PI and SPEED team to review progress, milestones, and future research plans.

title: Lead Project Manager
description: In this role, you will provide project and change management expertise to lead complex, cross-team initiatives across DELTA. This role brings structure, collaboration, and organizational excellence to projects that span technology, instructional development, media production, marketing, communications, support, governance, and other strategic priorities. The Lead Project Manager independently manages high-impact projects, coordinates teams and resources, advises colleagues, and helps advance organizational excellence practices across DELTA and the university. Reporting to the Director, Project Management, this position works in a collaborative, team-based environment and serves as a trusted resource for project management, change management, coaching, and organizational improvement. Key Responsibilities: Lead the prioritization, definition, coordination, and management of complex DELTA projects, processes, and initiatives involving multiple teams, deliverables, resources, and organizational impacts. Partner with development teams, production managers, faculty, clients, vendors, and university colleagues to define project scope, goals, deliverables, dependencies, resources, and timelines. Analyze proposed projects and resource requirements to support effective prioritization and organizational planning. Develop project schedules, timelines, reports, and workflows that promote visibility, accountability, and effective resource management. Facilitate feasibility discussions, resolve competing priorities, negotiate deadlines, and bring teams together to address challenges related to scope, resources, timelines, and deliverables. Lead teams and groups without formal supervisory authority, providing direction, coaching, and informal leadership to colleagues. Manages and mediates complex conversations involving competing priorities, differing perspectives, sensitive topics, or organizational tensions with sound judgment and professionalism. Serve as a subject-matter expert and thought leader in project and change management, applying methodologies and practices such as Agile, Scrum, Prosci, and ADKAR. Collaborate with senior leadership to align projects and organizational practices with DELTA’s strategic goals. Research, evaluate, and implement emerging project and change management tools, techniques, and practices to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Administer DELTA’s project management system and lead related training, updates, and process improvements. Review and recommend improvements to procedures, workflows, and project management practices. Provide consultation, training, presentations, and guidance on project and change management across DELTA and the university. Represent DELTA and NC State University on campus committees, interest groups, conferences, and presentations, sharing project and organizational excellence expertise. Build and maintain strong professional relationships across DELTA and the university while fostering effective collaboration and communication. Mentor new project managers and part-time employees and, as needed, provide oversight of part-time staff. The successful candidate will bring excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong interpersonal and organizational abilities, and the confidence to communicate effectively with individuals and groups at all levels. You will be comfortable coordinating across technical, design, instructional, production, and administrative teams and working with internal and external clients and vendors. Experience with web-based collaboration tools and project management platforms such as ClickUp or Monday is highly valued. Most importantly, you will bring the ability to lead through influence, navigate competing priorities, build productive relationships, and use project and change management expertise to move complex work forward.

title: Business Officer
description: Reporting to the Director for Student Leadership & Engagement, you will support the financial, administrative, human resources, and operational success of the department. Working across finance, human resources, office operations, and campus partnerships, you will partner with professional staff, student employees, university departments, and campus stakeholders to maintain efficient operations and provide the administrative infrastructure needed to support the department’s programs and services. Assist with developing and maintaining office operations, procedures, and administrative policies. Support departmental workflows, documentation, and internal reporting processes. Manage department storage facilities and ensure resources are organized and maintained. Monitor and maintain office supply inventories to support daily operations. Coordinate facility and operational needs with campus partners, including NC Student Centers and DASA Facilities. title: Assistant Professor and Extension Specialist in Row Crop Entomology
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor (12-month) to provide statewide leadership in arthropod management for North Carolina row crop production, with a focus on sweetpotato, peanut, and soybean. The position is 70% Extension and 30% research , connecting applied research, grower needs, and emerging technologies to strengthen sustainable pest management across North Carolina agriculture. You’ll have the opportunity to build on your expertise in row crop entomology, integrated pest management, pest ecology, and insecticide resistance while shaping innovative approaches to pest prediction, decision support, and resistance management. Your work may draw on field experimentation, landscape-scale studies, pest monitoring, and data-driven tools, including artificial intelligence, precision agriculture, remote sensing, and drones. Through your research and Extension program, you’ll translate new knowledge into practical solutions that help growers and agricultural professionals make informed, sustainable pest management decisions. Key responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Extension & Outreach: Shape a statewide Extension program that helps North Carolina growers address arthropod pest challenges in major row crops, including sweetpotato, peanut, and soybean. Translate research into practical recommendations that help growers, consultants, and industry stakeholders make informed pest management decisions. Connect with agricultural professionals and growers through field days, Extension programming, and innovative digital decision-support tools. Build strong partnerships with commodity groups, Extension agents, and state and federal partners to address emerging arthropod management challenges. Support the growth and development of graduate students and other trainees through mentorship, research guidance, and professional development opportunities. Strengthen agricultural workforce capacity by developing training and professional development opportunities for Extension agents, consultants, and agricultural professionals. Advance adoption of integrated pest management through innovative technologies and decision-support tools that translate research into practical solutions for North Carolina agriculture. Research & Discovery: Build an applied, externally funded research program that responds to grower needs and strengthens the impact of your Extension work. Advance understanding of pest ecology and management through field- and landscape-scale research addressing current and emerging crop protection challenges. Share new knowledge and practical solutions through peer-reviewed publications, Extension resources, and other scholarly contributions. Secure and steward extramural funding to advance applied research and strengthen the impact of Extension priorities. Mentorship, Teaching & Service: Mentor graduate students and other trainees through research guidance, professional development, and career preparation. Contribute to undergraduate and graduate instruction through teaching courses and supporting the department’s educational mission. Contribute expertise and perspective through departmental, college, university, and professional service activities. If you are a collaborative entomologist who enjoys connecting research with real-world agricultural challenges, building strong relationships with growers and partners, and developing innovative solutions for sustainable crop protection, we encourage you to apply.

title: Educational Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: This Educational Postdoctoral Research Scholar is designed to bridge the gap between clinical expertise and educational scholarship. By combining research training with hands-on teaching experience, the Postdoctoral Research Scholar will develop the skills necessary to become a leader in veterinary education and communication and professional pedagogy. Program Overview: Duration: 12-24 months Primary Objective: To equip DVM or PhD professionals with the methodological toolkit required to conduct high-impact research in health communication, communication and educational theory, and professionalism/professional identity. Eligibility & Qualifications : Must hold a DVM (or equivalent) or a PhD in a related field (Education, Communication, Psychology, etc.). Research & Methodological Training: The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will participate in a structured mentorship program to master mixed-methods research tailored to the veterinary healthcare and educational environment. Responsibilities include: Quantitative research methodologies, including survey design, statistical analysis of educational outcomes (such as competency-based assessments), and data-driven evaluation of communication interventions Qualitative research methods, including thematic analysis of reflective practice, conducting and coding focus groups and semi-structured interviews, and utilizing ethnographic or observational approaches Scholarly output through writing and submitting one first-author manuscript per year to a peer-reviewed journal (e.g., Journal of Veterinary Medical Education ) Teaching, Facilitation, and Curriculum: The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will be integrated into the DVM curriculum to ground ongoing research initiatives in active educational practice related to professionalism and communication training. Responsibilities Include: Communication Lab Facilitation - Leading small-group sessions using simulated clients (SCs) and providing real-time, constructive feedback to DVM students on clinical communication Guest Lecturing - Developing and delivering didactic content on topics such as conflict management, breaking bad news, or veterinary professional ethics Curriculum Development - Collaborating with faculty to refine and enhance learning modules and assessments across the professionalism curriculum

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar- Intestinal Microenvironment-Stem Cell Interactions
description: The McKinney-Aguirre Lab uses in translational large animal models to study epithelial recovery following clinically-relevant epithelial injury – with a special interest in the role of the microenvironment driving intestinal regeneration. The Lab is housed in the College of Veterinary Medicine and is part of Center for Gastrointestinal Biology and Disease. Duties and Responsibilities: The postdoctoral research fellow will participate in the management, processing, and analysis of studies employing a novel ex vivo intestinal perfusion models of intestinal injury. The fellow will also optimize new assays for evaluating intestinal response to injury and recovery including the application of ELISAs and advanced sequencing. This postdoctoral research fellow will interact regularly with scientists from various research backgrounds including experimental biologists. The successful candidate will be initiative-taking and enjoy working in a collaborative research environment. The postdoctoral research fellow will complete experiments, author primary research articles, and attend scientific meetings to present research progress.

title: Feline Health Center Veterinary Technician
description: The position is for an individual that is either a NC Registered Veterinary Technician (RVT) or is eligible for the NC RVT exam. The position interacts with internal specialty services and their respective staff, clinicians and students to provide coordination and veterinary care for feline patients. Duties include but are not limited to: Support the I-131 (hyperthyroidism treatment) program Provide excellent patient care by applying full knowledge of anatomy, physiology, disease processes, pharmacology, specialized equipment usage, and specialized drug administration for feline patients. Demonstrate and encourage the use of feline-friendly low-stress handling techniques. Work directly with clients, rDVM, and hospital personnel to facilitate communication and anticipate, integrate and coordinate services that optimize both internal and external satisfaction and overall patient care. Participate in client check in, patient admitting, updates, scheduling, and questions. Perform various technical procedures including; anesthesia support and monitoring, Intravenous catheter placement, venipuncture, IV injections, drug administration (IV, Oral, Subcutaneous), inpatient hospitalization care, and various routine diagnostic testing. Participate in supervising, coaching, teaching, orienting and evaluating in the principals of feline friendly practices for veterinary students and house officers. Support in-house training of staff to comply with feline friendly practices Provide support for feline-related clinical studies conducted at the College of Veterinary Medicine by adhering to research protocols, obtaining client consent, collecting and processing patient samples, and collecting clinical trial data. Record a variety of data relating to patient care, diagnostic testing and treatments, and client communications. Provide quick and accurate information regarding each patient, acting as the liaison between client and veterinarian. Enter data into electronic medical records in a proficient manner. The position also provides programmatic assistance for the Feline Health Center: Organize, coordinate, and develop initiatives to meet program needs and enhance the success of the Feline Health Center and constituents Emphasize cooperation with administration to ensure appropriate and effective flow of patients and program initiatives Assist with reviewing, updating, and preparing communications, marketing, and program databases. Ensure accuracy of data and compliance with program standards. Evaluate, research and assist with procurement of feline clinical supplies and equipment Assist with symposium, community outreach and educational events Pursue ongoing continuing education to support career growth and maintenance of licensure Partner with North Carolina Veterinary Medical Foundation for philanthropic development, including help with stewardship and cultivation of existing and potential donors to the Feline Health Center.

title: Facilities Maintenance Technician - HVAC Mechanic
description: The Facilities Maintenance Technician – HVAC Mechanic plays a critical role in maintaining the comfort, reliability, and efficiency of campus facilities. In this position, you will support the operation, maintenance, and repair of a wide range of building systems, including HVAC equipment, boilers, piping systems, and supporting electrical and mechanical components within an assigned maintenance zone. This role is ideal for a skilled technician who enjoys hands-on troubleshooting, solving complex mechanical issues, and working across multiple building systems . You will help ensure that heating, cooling, steam, and hot water systems operate safely and efficiently while supporting the daily operations of campus facilities. Working as part of a collaborative maintenance team, you will interact with coworkers, supervisors, and campus partners to diagnose issues, complete repairs, and perform preventative maintenance that helps prevent system failures and disruptions. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining safe, reliable environments that support teaching, research, and campus life. If you are a skilled HVAC technician who enjoys problem-solving, working with varied building systems, and making a meaningful impact on facility operations , we encourage you to apply. Apply today to join our team and help maintain the systems that keep our campus running smoothly. Key responsibilities and duties included, but not limited to: Perform maintenance, repair, and installation of HVAC systems, including air conditioning, refrigeration equipment, and ventilation systems. Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot steam and hot water boilers and associated auxiliary equipment. Diagnose and repair mechanical equipment, including pumps, fan turbines, condensate receivers, steam lines, pressure-reducing stations, and expansion joints. Inspect, maintain, and repair piping systems, insulation, strainers, valves, and other components used in steam and hot water distribution systems. Conduct preventive maintenance on refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment in accordance with manufacturer recommendations. Troubleshoot and repair pneumatic and electronic control systems, including temperature controls, regulators, humidity controllers, sensors, and control valves. Analyze faults and malfunctions in secondary electrical systems up to 600 VAC and implement corrective actions. Maintain and repair electrical components, including conduit wiring, electrical panels, breakers, switchgear, magnetic starters, motors, disconnects, switches, and receptacles. Diagnose and resolve control system faults affecting HVAC and related building systems. Perform minor plumbing and piping installations to support HVAC and building mechanical systems. Maintain and repair equipment used in steam generation and distribution, including air compressors and water softeners. Develop solutions for both routine and occasionally complex maintenance issues across HVAC, electrical, and plumbing systems. Coordinate with coworkers, supervisors, and other departments to ensure repairs and maintenance tasks are completed efficiently and safely. Communicate with campus customers and stakeholders to minimize disruptions and maintain building operations. Identify when specialized expertise or additional assistance is required and coordinate with appropriate personnel. Document maintenance activities and service requests to ensure accurate records and effective work order management. Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Assistant Professor - Plant Pathology
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor to advance its undergraduate educational mission in plant pathology while developing a complementary research program. This is a 9-month faculty position that has split responsibilities of 60% teaching and 40% research. The role provides leadership in delivering and evolving the undergraduate plant pathology curriculum, integrating active learning, case-based instruction, emerging technologies, and innovative approaches to prepare students for careers and continued study in the discipline. The role includes approximately two to three courses annually, spanning foundational plant pathology instruction, team-taught and specialized courses, and the development of undergraduate and distance education offerings. In this role, you will help shape how plant pathology is taught, experienced, and applied across the curriculum while building a research program that complements the department’s strengths. Your scholarship may engage areas such as plant disease diagnostics and management, fungal biology, soilborne pathogens, plant disease ecology, plant–soil–microbe systems, or epidemiology. You will have opportunities to develop innovative teaching and research programs, create meaningful experiential learning experiences, and foster collaboration across disciplines while engaging students in discovery and inquiry. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Teaching and Mentoring: Deliver and modernize core undergraduate plant pathology curriculum, including PP 315 (Principles of Plant Pathology) and its laboratory component, through innovative approaches such as active learning, case studies, emerging technologies, and distance education. Contribute to graduate, team-taught, and specialized courses while helping shape curriculum innovation and assessment across the program. Create meaningful opportunities for students to connect classroom learning with research, discovery, and other experiential learning. Mentor undergraduate researchers, graduate students, and postdoctoral scholars in their academic and professional development. Research and Discovery: Build and sustain an active, externally visible research program that complements departmental strengths and advances knowledge in plant pathology. Develop collaborative research that engages students and connects teaching, discovery, and emerging areas such as soilborne pathogens, fungal biology, and plant–soil–microbe interactions. Pursue scholarly work, external support, and partnerships that expand the reach and impact of your research. Contribute to a culture of inquiry and discovery across the department and broader scientific community. Department Service and Professional Engagement: Contribute to department, college, and university priorities through service, faculty governance, and academic leadership. Foster interdisciplinary collaborations and professional partnerships that strengthen teaching, research, and engagement. Engage with the broader scientific community through professional leadership, manuscript and grant review, and scholarly activities. Support outreach and initiatives that enhance the visibility and impact of the department and university while fostering a collegial and productive academic environment. If you are an innovative educator, collaborative researcher, and engaged academic who is passionate about advancing plant pathology education and discovery, we encourage you to apply.

Our research programs cover a varied spectrum including astrophysics, general relativity, condensed matter theory and experiment, computational physics, biophysics, nanoscale science, physics education, experimental nuclear physics, particle and nuclear theory, experimental optics, and experimental atomic and molecular physics. The department enrolls approximately 120 graduate students and 140 undergrad physics majors. The department size is approximately 57 faculty members. While working in this department, you will be expected to foster a supportive and welcoming environment. NC State promotes an integrated approach to problem solving that transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. NC State’s land grant mission of teaching, research and service is dedicated to the service of North Carolina and its people. Applicants are encouraged to review the institution’s mission, vision and strategic plan, and consider how their background, interest and experience would enable them to support the university.

Essential Job Duties: The Burclaff Lab focuses on understanding how metabolism and cellular energetics are regulated within intestinal stem cells, and how this dynamic regulation supports homeostasis, identity maintenance, fate decisions, cell cycle regulation, and tissue plasticity following injury or disease. We utilize a mix of animal models and cutting-edge, genetically modified, primary human intestinal stem cell cultures to advance our understanding of the mammalian intestine. The Research Associate will advance research operations, understand project rationales, and execute experiments to test scientific hypotheses across mouse models, cell lines, and primary cell cultures. In this role, you will also assist with laboratory management, including inventory tracking, equipment oversight, and day-to-day operational organization. Core Duties and Technical Responsibilities: Primary Cell Culture Management: Establish, propagate, and maintain mammalian primary cell cultures and established cell lines using aseptic techniques to support research projects. Molecular & Biochemical Assays: Perform routine and advanced molecular biology and biochemical assays, including DNA / RNA /protein extraction, PCR , RT-qPCR, gel electrophoresis, tissue sectioning, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry staining, and live image analysis. Animal Model Care & In Vivo Research: Oversee mouse colony operations—including handling, breeding, weaning, genotyping, and tissue collection—and execute experimental procedures in accordance with institutional guidelines. Laboratory Operations & Instrumentation: Maintain, calibrate, and troubleshoot laboratory equipment, manage inventory and data logs, and ensure strict compliance with safety protocols and standard operating procedures. If you are a collaborative scientist who enjoys hands-on research, solving problems, and keeping complex laboratory operations running smoothly, we encourage you to apply.
Other Responsibilities: Additional duties include organizing and maintaining research data, drafting or editing documents, contributing to publications, grant applications, and presentations.
Minimum Education and Experience: Relevant post-Baccalaureate degree, or relevant Bachelor’s degree plus 3 or more years of independent research experience. May require terminal degree and licensure. All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
Other Required Qualifications: Experience in mammalian primary cell culture (establishment and maintenance) Experience in molecular biology and biochemistry techniques ( PCR ; RT-qPCR; gel electrophoresis, DNA , RNA , and protein extraction; immunofluorescence; immunohistochemistry) Experience in mouse colony management (animal handling, breeding, weaning, genotyping, etc) and in vivo experimentation
Preferred Qualifications: Prior research experience. Ability to work with animals. Strong computer skills and ability to use highly specialized laboratory equipment with troubleshooting abilities.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Abolhasani Research Group in the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering at North Carolina State University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scholar in microreaction engineering and automated flow chemistry as part of the NSF-funded SPEED Programmable Cloud Laboratory. The successful candidate will develop automated continuous-flow and microfluidic experimental platforms for accelerated chemical and materials discovery. Research will combine microreaction engineering, multiphase transport, automated reaction screening, in-line/online analytical characterization, and closed-loop optimization. Applications may include homogeneous catalysis, photocatalysis, nanoparticle and semiconductor materials synthesis, and other solution-phase chemical and materials systems relevant to SPEED. Highly motivated candidates with experience in flow chemistry, microfluidics, reaction engineering, transport phenomena, catalysis, or automated chemical experimentation are encouraged to apply. Duties and Responsibilities include: Design and develop automated continuous-flow and microfluidic reactor platforms. Develop flow systems for homogeneous, gas-liquid, liquid-liquid, photochemical, and/or materials synthesis applications. Integrate pumps, valves, mass-flow controllers, temperature/pressure control, and other process equipment. Integrate flow reactors with in-line and online analytical characterization tools such as HPLC, GC, MS, UV-Vis, fluorescence, Raman, or IR spectroscopy. Develop automated reaction-screening and optimization workflows. Investigate mixing, mass transfer, heat transfer, residence-time distributions, kinetics, and other fundamental transport and reaction phenomena. Interface flow platforms with SPEED automation, data-management, and AI/ML infrastructure. Conduct high-throughput and closed-loop experimental campaigns. Analyze experimental results and develop mechanistic and data-driven understanding of chemical systems. Collaborate with chemists, materials scientists, automation engineers, and AI/ML researchers. Prepare scientific manuscripts, presentations, technical documentation, and project reports.

title: Operations Manager
description: As the Operations Manager, you will connect SPEED’s scientific mission with its day-to-day operations by coordinating facility access, staffing, scheduling, safety, equipment readiness, procurement, and user support. SPEED will serve researchers from universities, national laboratories, government agencies, and industry, and your leadership will help establish the facility as a dependable, accessible, and professionally managed research resource. You will also help shape the operational foundation of a growing national research resource. SPEED will serve researchers from universities, national laboratories, government agencies, and industry, and you will play a key role in establishing SPEED as a dependable, accessible, and professionally managed facility. Through thoughtful coordination, responsive support, and effective operational leadership, you will help create an environment where researchers can focus on advancing their work through remote autonomous experimentation. List of Primary Responsibilities Facility & User Operations Lead daily facility operations, including laboratory readiness, platform availability, staffing coverage, access, scheduling, and user support. Develop and maintain operational procedures for user onboarding, experiment submission, training, platform access, technical assistance, and project closeout. Coordinate laboratory capacity and schedules across internal researchers, academic users, government collaborators, and industry partners. Monitor facility utilization, experiment throughput, turnaround times, incidents, and user needs to identify and resolve operational issues. People & Resource Management Lead and support technical and operational personnel, including establishing priorities, schedules, performance expectations, training, and cross-coverage for critical facility functions. Manage operational budgets, purchasing, inventory, service contracts, equipment needs, and vendor relationships in coordination with university partners. Maintain operational records and monitor staffing, resource needs, project milestones, and facility deliverables. Safety, Compliance & Risk Management Lead facility-wide safety and risk management activities, including hazard assessments, emergency procedures, incident response, inspections, training, and business-continuity planning. Coordinate with Environmental Health and Safety, information technology, research administration, facilities, and other university partners to support applicable safety, compliance, cybersecurity, and research requirements. Investigate operational incidents and recurring failures and implement corrective and preventive actions. Stakeholder Communication & Continuous Improvement Serve as the primary operational contact for SPEED leadership, users, university administrators, vendors, and external partners. Communicate facility capabilities, access requirements, schedules, limitations, risks, and operational updates to technical and nontechnical audiences. Use operational data and user feedback to improve procedures, training, services, facility reliability, and user support. Contribute to strategic planning for facility growth, new platform deployment, service expansion, workshops, demonstrations, sponsor visits, and long-term sustainability. If you are an analytical and collaborative leader who enjoys bringing people, technology, and complex operations together, we invite you to apply. This is an opportunity to help build and manage a cutting-edge research facility while supporting researchers, technical teams, and partners from across the university and beyond.

title: Temporary Financial Operations Specialist
description: The Temporary Financial Operations Specialist provides accounting and financial operations support within the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) Business Services unit. Business Services is transitioning to a cross-functional service model in which employees develop proficiency across multiple financial operations functions. Employees will support Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Travel, and Procurement Card (PCard) operations and may be assigned primary responsibilities based on operational needs. Work assignments may shift across functional areas to support workload balancing, team coverage, and continuity of business operations. Primary Responsibilities: Process and support Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Travel, and Procurement Card (PCard) transactions, as assigned. Process, review, reconcile, and analyze financial transactions for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with university policies and procedures. Apply accounting principles and established business processes to transactions across multiple funding sources. Review financial activity for appropriate documentation, classification, and compliance with applicable university, state, federal, and sponsor requirements. Research and resolve transaction discrepancies while maintaining accurate financial records and supporting documentation. Assist with financial monitoring, reconciliation, reporting activities, and audit support. Utilize university financial systems, including PeopleSoft, ServiceNow, and reporting tools, to process, review, and monitor financial activity. Provide customer service and guidance to departments regarding financial processes, documentation requirements, and transaction status. Collaborate with campus partners to resolve financial issues and support efficient business operations. Identify opportunities to improve processes, strengthen internal controls, and enhance operational effectiveness. Participate in cross-training and provide backup coverage across Business Services functions as operational needs require. Perform other duties as assigned

title: Director of Recruiting, Enrollment Management, and Educational Partnerships
description: The Director of Recruiting, Enrollment Management and Educational Partnerships provides strategic leadership for recruitment, enrollment management, and educational partnerships within the Office of Academic Affairs in the NC State College of Engineering . This position plays a key role in shaping the college’s enrollment strategy, expanding pathways to engineering degrees, strengthening institutional partnerships, and advancing opportunities for student success. The Director serves as a senior leader and primary liaison for recruitment and enrollment initiatives, working closely with university partners, academic units, educational institutions, donors, and other stakeholders to achieve enrollment goals and strengthen the College of Engineering’s position as a premier destination for engineering education. What you will do: Lead recruitment and enrollment strategy , establishing priorities and initiatives that support enrollment goals and long-term growth. Lead recruitment and admissions efforts , partnering with the Office of Admissions on standards, enrollment targets, and recruitment strategies while promoting the college’s academic programs, research, facilities, and student achievements. Oversee engineering pathway programs and educational partnerships , including 2+2 Regional, 3+2 dual-degree, community college, and other strategic pathways to NC State engineering degrees. Lead and develop direct reports , setting clear priorities and ensuring activities align with university, college, and departmental policies. Manage recruitment and partnership budgets , strategically allocating resources to support programs and initiatives while maintaining sound financial practices. Champion the College of Engineering’s strengths , maintaining a strong understanding of its academic programs, research, facilities, and faculty and student achievements. Partner with the Engineering Foundation to expand scholarship support , cultivating donor relationships, increasing scholarship revenue, and developing effective award processes. Oversee incoming undergraduate scholarships , collaborating with university scholarship programs to maximize opportunities for engineering students. Partner on recruitment marketing and strategic planning , developing materials and initiatives that advance college and university enrollment goals. Support the Office of Academic Affairs and college leadership through relevant committees, initiatives, and other responsibilities as assigned. In this role, you will lead with vision, collaboration, and innovation , building strong relationships across the university and with external partners. You will bring a proven record of effective leadership , the ability to inspire and engage students and colleagues , and excellent written and oral communication skills. Success in this position requires sound judgment, discretion, and integrity , along with the interpersonal skills and political acumen to build effective bridges, foster collaboration, and advance shared goals.

title: Client Support Specialist
description: The Client Support Specialist serves as the primary point of contact for all client-related inquiries within the Veterinary Hospital Business Office. This role ensures high-quality customer service by managing multi-channel communications, addressing client concerns, and processing financial transactions with accuracy and professionalism. Additionally, this role serves as a key liaison between clients and hospital staff to resolve complex issues, while providing operational support to maintain seamless business office coverage. Key Responsibilities Manage incoming phone calls and the business office email inbox, serving as the first line of response for client inquiries, questions, and concerns. Accurately process client payments, handle refunds, and manage daily transaction updates in accordance with hospital financial policies. Communicate and collaborate effectively with other hospital staff to investigate and resolve client billing or service issues. Administer and manage the client satisfaction survey program to gather feedback and support hospital service improvements. Perform routine Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable tasks as needed to assist with business office coverage. Operational Support (as needed) Accounts Receivable: Ensure hospital invoices are paid according to University guidelines; process employee reimbursements and supplemental pay; manage staff and student pagers and cell phones; and reconcile financial transactions (processing JVs and IDTs). Accounts Payable: Manage, audit, resolve, and deliver the daily hospital deposit and revenue recap; manage bad debt, past-due accounts, and aged credits; handle communications and reconciliations with Collections and the Attorney General; and execute other duties including but not limited to posting payments, issuing refunds, credit card and Care Credit troubleshooting. Key Qualifications Ability to maintain a high volume of professional, empathetic, and clear verbal and written communication with clients and staff for extended periods. Capacity for frequent, repetitive motions associated with digital payment processing, data entry, email management, and utilizing hospital information systems. Ability to efficiently switch between customer service, conflict resolution, and detailed financial tasks in a fast-paced office environment. If you are a customer-focused professional who enjoys helping others, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and takes pride in delivering accurate, responsive service, we encourage you to apply. If you excel at building positive relationships, communicating with empathy and professionalism, and balancing customer service with detailed financial and administrative responsibilities, we'd love to have you join our Veterinary Hospital Business Office team.

title: Assistant Engineer
description: NC State Athletics is a leader in video and broadcast production, supporting high-profile live events and innovative media experiences across its athletic venues. We are seeking a Broadcast Engineering professional to join our team and help ensure the reliable operation and delivery of complex productions across the department. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, this position plays a hands-on role in maintaining broadcast and A/V systems, supporting ESPN/ACC Network events, preparing production equipment, and helping bring multiple productions together on tight timelines. The ideal candidate is technically capable, highly organized, self-directed, and comfortable working in a fast-paced live production environment where priorities can change quickly. Key Responsibilities Assist the Director of Engineering with the maintenance, troubleshooting, configuration, and technical operation of broadcast facilities, A/V systems, video boards, and digital signage throughout athletic venues. Provide engineering support for ESPN/ACC Network event broadcasts hosted or supported by NC State facilities. Plan and coordinate equipment allocation and deployment for multiple productions. Set up, test, and prepare production equipment, often supporting multiple events within tight turnaround windows. Perform basic maintenance, configuration, and troubleshooting of broadcast and production equipment. Train and mentor student operators in equipment operation, safe handling practices, professional production techniques, and production etiquette. Apply knowledge of live broadcast programming concepts, production principles, methodologies, and technical practices to support successful events. Supervise student staff as needed, including scheduling, load-ins and strikes, coaching and directing, intern management, and oversight of engineering projects. Ability to lift up to 30 pounds frequently and up to 60 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations. This role requires someone who can take initiative, work independently, and stay focused in a fast-moving production environment while collaborating effectively within a team. The successful candidate will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, responding with urgency when situations demand it, and working through complex technical challenges with appropriate support from colleagues. If you enjoy live sports, broadcast technology, and the challenge of making complex productions work seamlessly behind the scenes, this is an opportunity to make a direct impact on the fan and broadcast experience at NC State Athletics.

title: Alumni Coordinator
description: The Alumni Coordinator serves as a key relationship-builder and ambassador for the College of Education by developing, strengthening, and sustaining meaningful connections with alumni, students, faculty, staff, donors, and community partners. This position is responsible for advancing alumni engagement initiatives that foster lifelong relationships with the college and promote a strong sense of community, pride, and philanthropic support. Through strategic outreach, impactful programming, stewardship activities, communications, and events, the Alumni Coordinator plays an essential role in enhancing alumni participation, volunteerism, mentorship opportunities, and advancement efforts in support of the college’s mission and long-term strategic priorities. This position works collaboratively across the college to cultivate a vibrant alumni network that supports student success, professional development, career exploration, community engagement, and institutional advancement. This role requires a highly relational, organized, and proactive professional who is passionate about higher education, engagement, and building authentic relationships across populations and generations of alumni. Key Responsibilities Alumni Communications & Engagement Develop and support alumni engagement communication initiatives designed to strengthen alumni connection, participation, and affinity with the College of Education. Assist in the creation and coordination of alumni-focused content including digital newsletters, email campaigns, donor stewardship messaging, alumni spotlights, event promotions, social media collaboration, and engagement materials. Serve as a liaison and collaborative partner with university advancement and annual giving initiatives related to alumni outreach and engagement communications. Support strategic communication efforts that promote alumni networking, mentoring, volunteer engagement, continuing education opportunities, and professional development initiatives. Maintain and support accurate alumni records, contact information, engagement tracking, and participation data to strengthen outreach efforts and long-term relationship management. Analyze engagement trends and assist in identifying opportunities to increase alumni participation and connectivity across programs and initiatives. Relationship Development & Volunteer Engagement Cultivate, develop, and steward meaningful relationships with alumni across a broad range of backgrounds, professions, career stages, and geographic regions. Recruit and support alumni volunteers for mentorship programs, speaking engagements, networking initiatives, advisory opportunities, student engagement activities, and college events. Develop strategies to increase alumni involvement and strengthen connections between alumni, current students, faculty, and the broader college community. Conduct proactive outreach to alumni to preserve institutional relationships, strengthen long-term engagement, and enhance continuity of institutional knowledge and community connection. Identify and support opportunities for alumni leadership, advocacy, and volunteer participation in support of college initiatives and strategic priorities. Performs other duties as assigned in support of alumni programming, engagement events, continuing education initiatives, and the overall mission and strategic goals of the College of Education and Advancement Office. Alumni Programming, Events & Continuing Education Partner with alumni leadership groups and advisory boards to support the development and achievement of strategic alumni engagement goals and initiatives. Coordinate, plan, and facilitate alumni events and engagement activities including networking events, mentoring opportunities, reunions, continuing education initiatives, recognition programs, annual celebrations, tailgates, and special college events. Support the development of innovative programming that fosters professional growth, career connection, lifelong learning, and community engagement among alumni. Collaborate with internal and external partners to ensure successful execution of alumni engagement initiatives and programs. Assist with event logistics, communications, registration management, volunteer coordination, budgeting support, and post-event assessment activities. Other duties as assigned that support the mission, goals, and strategic priorities of the Alumni Coordinator role and the College of Education Advancement Office. Advancement & Philanthropic Engagement Support Partner with advancement and development staff to strengthen alumni engagement as it relates to philanthropy, donor cultivation, volunteerism, and institutional support. Support donor stewardship initiatives by assisting with gratitude communications, alumni recognition efforts, engagement tracking, and relationship-building activities. Assist with Day of Giving and other fundraising initiatives by coordinating student philanthropy activities, increasing alumni participation, and supporting donor engagement efforts. Help cultivate a culture of philanthropy and alumni investment within the College of Education community. This position is open for current NC State Employees only, permanent or temporary.

Our work encompasses educational research, professional development, policy and program evaluation, and direct services to schools, districts, state departments of education and public- and private sector organizations. We are deeply involved in work in throughout North Carolina, leading some of the major statewide K-12 education initiatives and working closely with the Department of Public Instruction, the State Board of Education, and the majority of school districts in the State on the transition to digital teaching and learning. Since opening in 2005, the Friday Institute has developed a strong national presence, working with organizations throughout the country, and is increasingly developing international connections. Essential Job Duties: The Research Associate will report to the Executive Director of the Friday Institute and will provide direct support to coordinate across initiatives, communicate clearly with internal and external partners, and maintain shared visibility into priorities, progress, and decisions. A core function of this role is extending reach—helping to author, package, publish, and report on its work so that high-quality ideas and programming become usable artifacts, visible impact, and sustained momentum with partners and funders. The primary work centers on connecting the dots across initiatives by identifying patterns, surfacing insights, coordinating collaborators, and ensuring projects move from planning to high-quality execution. In this role, you will help turn complex ideas, research, and partner feedback into clear strategies, actionable plans, and meaningful outcomes. You will connect people and priorities across projects, bringing structure to work that spans multiple initiatives and partners. Your ability to see the big picture while managing important details will help teams make informed decisions, strengthen programs, and continuously improve. You will also help amplify the Friday Institute’s work by creating clear, compelling materials and communications that demonstrate impact, support partnerships, and build momentum for future opportunities. Key responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Program strategy and synthesis: Conduct structured inquiry (interviews, listening sessions, document review) to understand needs, constraints, and opportunities across partners and initiatives. Synthesize research, practitioner feedback, and implementation data into clear insights, recommendations, and decision points for project teams and leadership. Translate strategy into actionable workplans (milestones, dependencies, risks, resourcing) and maintain visibility across the portfolio. Identify gaps, overlaps, and opportunities for alignment across initiatives; propose pragmatic ways to streamline and strengthen the portfolio. Evidence and improvement: Define and track meaningful indicators of progress (implementation readiness, participation, adoption signals, quality measures, partner satisfaction). Support lightweight evaluation and learning cycles: collect feedback, document lessons learned, and integrate improvements into next iterations. Monitor the broader landscape (policy, research, edtech and AI developments) and flag implications for program design and partner needs. Convenings, coordination, and communications: Facilitate and/or contribute to convenings, training, and other partner-facing learning opportunities. Coordinate project meetings, working groups, governance structures, and partner communications to support timely decisions and follow-through. Prepare, maintain, and update partner-ready project materials for online and print dissemination (briefs, agendas, decision memos, implementation supports), ensuring outputs are clear, consistent, and publication-ready. Growth and resourcing: Contribute to project and grant proposals, including framing problems and possibilities of practice and aligning deliverables. Draft and coordinate funder-facing reports and updates that communicate progress, evidence, and impact with clarity and credibility Document project activity to capture outcomes, lessons learned, and next-phase recommendations. Track and support a pipeline of aligned opportunities; maintain portfolio-level visibility into funding status, commitments, and next steps. If you are a curious, collaborative, adaptable professional who enjoys connecting ideas, people, and possibilities to move meaningful work forward, we encourage you to apply.
Other Responsibilities: In addition to the core responsibilities of this role, there may be occasional opportunities to take on additional duties such as: Support day-to-day operations Coordinate project meetings, organization structures, and communications Prepare, maintain, and update project materials for online and print dissemination Up to 20% for in-state and/or out-of-state travel This offers an opportunity to build on your skills, explore new areas, and gain a deeper understanding of the department’s operations.
Minimum Education and Experience: Relevant Master’s degree in Education or Technology, or a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field plus 5 or more years of experience as a K-12 educator, technology leader, or researcher. All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
Other Required Qualifications: Demonstrated ability to gather, analyze, and synthesize research, stakeholder feedback, and implementation data to identify insights, trends, and opportunities for improvement. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex ideas for academic and practitioner audiences through written materials, presentations, and other communications.
Preferred Qualifications: PhD in instructional technology, learning sciences, STEM education, or a related field. Project management, organizational, and coordination skills sufficient to manage multiple priorities, timelines, and stakeholders while maintaining attention to detail and follow-through. Facilitation, presentation, and relationship-building skills sufficient to effectively engage diverse academic, practitioner, and partner audiences. Knowledge of digital learning and emerging technologies, including computer science and AI education, and their application to teaching, learning, implementation, or program improvement.

As part of the support process, this position provides support of hardware, applications, operating systems, and networking. This function requires an in-depth understanding of a wide variety of technologies to effectively support end-users and to provide helpful and accurate information to peers and IT colleagues across campus. As a senior member of the OIT Managed Desktop Support team, this position may participate in in-depth application support, system integration and networking activities. This work requires very strong communication skills, an ability to effectively interact with a broad range of end-users and IT professionals, as well as, an ability to use a variety of resources for diagnosing and resolving technical problems. The department provides learning opportunities within the four-year veterinary curriculum (educational information) and through continuing education for practitioners. Within the Veterinary Health Complex, faculty and staff provide care for patients, teach veterinary students, and provide advanced training for interns and residents. Essential Job Duties: The Translational Research in Pain team is seeking a Research Technician who is passionate about advancing pain management through innovative clinical and basic research. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to meaningful studies that improve pain assessment and treatment approaches in veterinary medicine while working alongside an interdisciplinary research team in a collaborative laboratory environment. Key Responsibilities: Support clinical and translational research studies focused on pain management and pain assessment. Assist with the organization and execution of clinical trials, including participant recruitment, screening, scheduling, and study coordination. Perform pain assessments and provide patient care support for clinical and laboratory research subjects. Assist with other laboratory support duties as assigned in support of the research team’s mission.

Knowledge of animal anatomy, animal handling techniques, and the ability to assist with animal dissection or tissue collection activities. Familiarity with orthopedic pain research, gait analysis software, or related research technologies. Strong organizational, analytical, and computer skills with the ability to maintain accurate records and manage research data. Ability to demonstrate initiative, communicate effectively, and work proactively in a collaborative clinical and laboratory research environment.

title: Administrative Assistant
description: Join NC State University’s Facilities Division as an Administrative Assistant on our Business Operations team and play an important role in keeping day-to-day operations organized, efficient, and connected.
