This is a great opportunity for an organized, proactive professional who enjoys supporting others, solving problems, coordinating details, and making a meaningful contribution to a team that supports the university’s facilities and operations. If you’re ready to bring your organizational skills, professionalism, and collaborative spirit to NC State’s Facilities Division, we invite you to apply today! Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Coordinate and manage complex schedules and calendars for both the department and division, ensuring seamless communication and time management Draft and prepare memorandums, create detailed spreadsheets, schedule meetings, and maintain essential records for the team Maintain and update databases and spreadsheets for special projects assigned by the Assistant Vice Chancellor, conducting in-depth research, reconciling data from multiple systems such as Interscope and other project management tools, and producing both standard and customized high-level reports and presentations Coordinate travel arrangements and process necessary separation paperwork in a timely manner Assist in the development and lead the maintenance of procedures for tracking remote work, ensuring accuracy and consistency. Serve as a resource for resolving complex, non-standard issues by coordinating with other work units, facilitating effective solutions, identifying and addressing internal issues that impact customer service and operational efficiency, and collaborating with departmental coordinators to establish standard processes and procedures to enhance overall efficiency. Interpret guidelines and policies, respond to inquiries, and provide guidance on processes, services, and operations in non-standard situations. Serve as a Facilities Division communications representative by developing and maintaining Standard Operating Procedures and delivering in-person training to departments. Maintain and update the Facilities website using WordPress , ensuring content is accurate, current, and timely, and develop and distribute communications to keep employees informed of important updates and information. Provide comprehensive technical and administrative support for Business Operations by initiating job postings, scheduling interviews, preparing hiring proposals, and processing separation paperwork to ensure a smooth recruitment process Manage supply orders and maintain the supply closet, tracking inventory using AiM and the Capital Asset Management System to ensure accuracy.

title: Equine and Farm Animal Attendant
description: The Equine and Farm Animal Attendant plays a critical role in providing exceptional daily care and husbandry support for all patients at the Equine and Farm Animal Veterinary Center. From handling varied large animal species to maintaining strict sanitary standards, this position ensures a clean, safe, and supportive healing environment for our patients and clinical team. Key Responsibilities: Patient Care & Husbandry: Provide daily feeding, watering, grooming, and handling for patient species including equine, bovine, caprine, ovine, and camelids. Safely restrain animals to assist clinical staff during treatments and examinations. Hospital Sanitation & Biosecurity: Maintain a clean and hygienic hospital environment by strictly following established protocols. Perform stall cleaning, deep cleaning, disinfection of clinical areas, and regular trash removal. Strictly adhere to all Infectious Disease and biosecurity protocols. Facility & Equipment Maintenance: Maintain indoor and outdoor hospital grounds as needed. Monitor supplies and equipment, assisting with routine maintenance and repair schedules. Operations & Operations Support: Assist with inventory control, supply ordering, and purchasing. Collaborate and maintain effective communication with hospital departments and ancillary services. Participate in an on-call schedule, including weekend and holiday rotations as required. Qualifications & Expectations Experience: Prior experience handling and caring for large animals (equine, livestock, etc.) in a veterinary, farm, or clinical setting preferred. Physical Stamina: Ability to perform physically demanding tasks (lifting, walking, bending, stall cleaning) in varying weather conditions. Skills: Strong communication skills, high attention to detail, and a team-first mindset. Availability: Flexibility to participate in evening, weekend, holiday, and on-call rotations.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Crop and Soil Sciences encompasses varied disciplines in research, extension, and teaching. The department’s mission is to develop future leaders in crop, soil, and environmental sciences, improve crop plants and products, devise effective and sustainable crop production systems, devise effective and sustainable soil management techniques in both agriculture and urban settings; and disseminate crop, soil, and environmental science knowledge for the benefit of users and producers of food, feed turf, biofuels and fiber in North Carolina, the nation and the world. The successful candidate will conduct independent and collaborative research to develop and elucidate bio-physical-chemical mechanisms that regulate soil carbon sequestration, nitrogen retention, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mitigation in agricultural systems. The primary focus will be on understanding how soil amendments derived from bioenergy production byproducts influence soil processes and ecosystem sustainability. Key responsibilities include: Collect soil samples and set up microcosm experiments. Measure soil fluxes of carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide. Conduct metagenomic DNA extraction and shotgun sequencing. Perform bioinformatics and statistical data analyses. Prepare manuscripts and present research findings in professional meetings. Work closely with team members and help train graduate students.

title: Plumber II
description: Are you an experienced plumber looking for an opportunity to work on a varied range of facilities while making a lasting impact on a major university campus? As a Plumber II , you will perform skilled installation, repair, maintenance, and modification of complex plumbing and piping systems that support classrooms, laboratories, offices, residence halls, and other critical campus facilities. This journey-level role offers the opportunity to apply advanced plumbing and pipefitting expertise while expanding your knowledge through exposure to secondary electrical and HVAC-related systems. If you take pride in solving complex problems, delivering quality workmanship, and supporting the infrastructure that keeps a campus community running, we encourage you to apply and join our team. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Install, maintain, repair, and modify plumbing and piping systems, including water, waste, steam, gas, chilled water, and compressed air systems. Service domestic, lab, and acid waste drainage systems, building sewers, and associated fixtures and equipment. Perform pipefitting tasks, including cutting, threading, assembling, testing, and installing piping, valves, supports, and fixtures. Conduct scheduled preventive maintenance on plumbing and related air, gas, water, and waste disposal systems. Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair boilers, pumps, steam systems, compressors, water softeners, and related equipment. Apply working knowledge of secondary electrical and HVAC-related systems , controls, and components. Ensure all work complies with Federal, State, OSHA, and Facilities Operations safety policies and procedures. Identify and address safety hazards and properly use required personal protective equipment. Communicate clearly with supervisors, coworkers, and campus customers regarding work assignments and timelines. Perform tasks that involve climbing ladders, accessing confined or elevated spaces, occasional lifting up to 60 lbs, and working in varied conditions, including exposure to areas with insects or small animals. All essential duties must be completed with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Automation Engineer
description: The Automation Engineer will help build the systems that make SPEED’s laboratories smarter, more data-rich, and capable of running complex experiments remotely. You’ll connect robots, scientific instruments, sensors, reactors, and safety systems to SPEED’s orchestration software—turning sophisticated laboratory procedures into reliable, reusable automated workflows. This is a hands-on engineering role with direct impact on the reliability, throughput, safety, and reproducibility of a national user facility. What You’ll Do Build and Integrate Laboratory Automation Design and implement automated workflows for synthesis, materials processing, sample preparation, testing, and characterization. Integrate robots, liquid handlers, pumps, valves, reactors, instruments, sensors, and other laboratory equipment. Translate scientific protocols into robust, executable workflows with defined operating limits and error handling. Develop reusable device drivers and equipment interfaces for SPEED’s automation platform. Commission and validate new robotic systems, workcells, and scientific instruments. Develop Control Software and Interfaces Develop and maintain Python software for device control, workflow execution, monitoring, and diagnostics. Connect laboratory equipment to SPEED’s scheduling, orchestration, data, and user-access systems. Implement reliable communications using APIs, Python libraries, TCP/IP, OPC UA, REST, serial, digital I/O, and other protocols. Establish consistent device states, commands, metadata, and error handling across varied equipment. Use version control, testing, and code review to deliver dependable automation software. Develop simulation or digital-twin capabilities to test workflows before running them on physical equipment. Improve Reliability and Performance Monitor automated systems and troubleshoot robotics, motion control, fluid handling, sensors, instruments, software, and network issues. Develop preventive maintenance, calibration, readiness checks, and recovery procedures. Analyze failures and implement improvements that increase uptime, repeatability, and ease of recovery. Work with manufacturers and vendors to resolve technical issues and support critical systems. Maintain clear documentation of configurations, dependencies, maintenance, and known failure modes. Build Safe, Usable Systems Design automation with appropriate interlocks, alarms, safe states, emergency stops, and shutdown logic. Conduct hazard and failure-mode reviews for robotic, fluidic, thermal, pressure, gas-handling, and unattended operations. Create system documentation, operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, and maintenance instructions. Train researchers, operators, students, and technical staff to use automated platforms safely and effectively. Help establish engineering standards and platform designs that enable automation to scale across SPEED and partner facilities. You’ll work at the intersection of automation, robotics, software, and scientific research , solving challenging engineering problems that enable experiments to run faster, more reliably, and at greater scale. Your work will help transform advanced laboratory capabilities into dependable platforms that scientists can use to accelerate discovery.

title: Food Services Supervisor
description: NC State Dining is seeking a dynamic, hands-on Food Service Supervisor to oversee the daily operations of a campus café or market. This is a working supervisory role where you will lead by example, driving exceptional customer service and culinary quality during peak service hours. If you are a collaborative leader dedicated to fostering a safe, high-energy environment for the Wolfpack community, we want you on our team! Key Responsibilities Daily Operations & Leadership: Oversee front- and back-of-house operations, including opening/closing procedures, cash handling, register setup, and attractive product displays. Team Management: Interview, hire, schedule, and train student and temporary staff. Mentor employees through cross-training, one-on-one coaching, and daily duty assignments. Quality & Inventory Control: Maintain brand-specific standards for food and beverage quality. Assist with vendor ordering, conduct regular inventories, and utilize the C-Board food system to manage food and labor costs. Customer Service Excellence: Maintain a strong presence to resolve customer issues on the spot, build rapport with guests, and ensure swift, friendly service. Sanitation & Safety: Uphold strict Wake County Health Department and food code rules to maintain a Grade A sanitation rating (95% or better) . Ensure all allergen best practices and sanitation logs are strictly followed.

title: TRIO Upward Bound Instructor
description: The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State. NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here ( You Belong Here ). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Upward Bound Program is an early intervention pre-college program that helps students prepare for higher education. Upward Bound brings high school students to college campuses after school, on the weekends, and during the summer to receive instruction in mathematics, laboratory sciences, composition, literature, and foreign languages. Tutoring, counseling, mentoring, cultural enrichment, and work-study programs are additional components to the Upward Bound Program. The NC State University Program serves five high schools (Vance County HS, Louisburg HS, Bunn HS, Franklinton HS, and East Wake HS). The Program has been a part of the University since 1978 and has assisted hundreds of students to enroll in college and gain a college degree. The Upward Bound Program is looking for Instructors that will be responsible for: Developing and executing lesson plans in assigned curriculum courses in the following areas: High School Mathematics High School English High School Science, including physical science and chemistry Computer Science, especially AI Providing written evaluations on each program participant

title: Assistant Professor of Linguistics
description: The Department of English at North Carolina State University invites applications for one full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Linguistics. As a faculty member, you will contribute to our undergraduate major and M.A. concentration through teaching, research, and service. The area of specialization is open; however, we are particularly interested in candidates specializing in either: corpus linguistics, with a focus on syntax, morphology, or the lexicon; or experimental sociolinguistics and/or experimental psycholinguistics. If you are passionate about advancing linguistic research, committed to excellence in teaching and mentorship, and eager to contribute to a collaborative academic community, we encourage you to apply.

title: Shipping & Receiving Assistant
description: Join our team as a Shipping and Receiving Assistant , a vital role supporting faculty, staff, and students across the Centennial Biomedical Campus. In this hands-on position, you will support daily receiving, asset tracking, mail runs, event setup, fleet care, and heavy equipment operation. You will also safely handle specialized items, including refrigerated supplies, controlled substances, anatomy specimens, and hazardous diagnostic samples. Key Responsibilities: This position plays a crucial role in supporting the sponsored activities of faculty, staff, and students within the College by performing a variety of tasks and responsibilities across different areas: Sign for and inventory all packages received daily from delivery trucks, confirming their accuracy against delivery manifests, including perishable, infectious, controlled substances, and valuable items. Conduct detailed inventories of all packages delivered to the Centennial Biomedical Campus, including various buildings and units within the college. Deliver packages to designated locations within the college campus, obtaining recipient signatures and recording delivery dates, especially for perishable items requiring refrigerated storage. Transport veterinary diagnostic samples to and from diagnostic laboratories, ensuring proper handling of infectious materials. Handle formaldehyde-preserved large and small animal cadavers for the Anatomy Lab, including transportation and use of protective equipment. Receive, document, and transport infectious disease samples for the Vector Born Laboratory to avoid public health risks. Locate and tag new purchases made by the college, documenting their details and entering them into the inventory database. Assist in documenting, tagging, and removing surplus items for disposal, adhering to safety procedures, and maintaining accurate inventory records. Assist with setting up and logistics for special events at the college, including deliveries, setup, and furniture rearrangement. Operate heavy equipment such as forklifts, pallet jacks, backhoes, dump trucks, and box trucks, ensuring proper safety training and certification. Assist with light maintenance on departmental vehicles, including fueling, cleaning, and scheduling maintenance and repairs. Assist with various moves within the college, including office and laboratory moves, and transporting heavy or delicate equipment. Provide customer service throughout the college and the College of Engineering Biomedical Engineering department, assisting customers with their needs. Demonstrate knowledge of various programs administered by Shipping and Receiving and explain them to others. Address various requests from customers across campus, ensuring policies and procedures are communicated and followed. Abilities Necessary to Perform Job Duties: Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations, on a frequent basis.

title: Transportation Supervisor

In this role, you will be the backbone of our event execution, ensuring that all catering equipment, beverages, and supplies are delivered safely, efficiently, and on schedule. Staff Scheduling: Utilize specialized departmental software to create, distribute, and monitor employee schedules. Clear Communication: Foster a collaborative team environment and maintain professional communication with multiple levels of University employees, peers, and customers. Logistics, Driving & Event Execution Delivery Operations: Develop, distribute, and monitor the daily delivery and transportation schedules. Behind the Wheel: Drive various delivery trucks and vehicles to execute catering and dining deliveries safely. Event Support: Load and unload cargo at each location; actively assist with event setup and breakdown. Fast-Paced Adaptability: Thrive and maintain professionalism under pressure in a high-energy, fast-moving environment. Fleet Management & Safety Fleet Care: Ensure a well-maintained, clean, and safe fleet of catering and dining vehicles. Training & Records: Establish and maintain a driver training program and a comprehensive fleet service record-keeping system. Preventative Maintenance: Oversee routine inspections, fueling, and preventative maintenance schedules in strict accordance with the NCSU Motor Pool guidelines. Inventory & Supply Control Inventory Management: Oversee inventory control, receipt, storage, and issuance of a wide variety of catering supplies, materials, and equipment. Physical Stamina: Ability to handle physical demands including bending, twisting, pulling, pushing, and standing for extended periods. We offer a collaborative, team-oriented workspace where your leadership directly impacts the success of major University events. If you are ready to drive your career forward, apply today!

title: Landscape Construction Project Manager
description: Do you have a passion for landscape construction and enjoy turning plans into well-executed projects? NC State University is seeking a Landscape Construction Project Manager to help shape and improve the campus landscape through thoughtful planning, strong project management, and a commitment to quality. In this role, you will manage landscape construction projects from planning and design through construction and final closeout. You’ll collaborate with University project managers, designers, consultants, contractors, and Facilities leadership to keep projects on schedule, within budget, and aligned with university standards. Your expertise in landscape construction, horticulture, hardscaping, irrigation, and stormwater systems will help ensure projects are built to last and successfully transition into ongoing campus maintenance. This is an opportunity to see your work become part of the NC State campus while working with a collaborative team dedicated to creating safe, functional, beautiful, and sustainable outdoor spaces. If you’re ready to bring your landscape construction expertise to projects that have a lasting impact on the NC State campus, we encourage you to apply! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Manage landscape construction projects from planning and design through construction and final closeout, monitoring scope, schedules, budgets, milestones, and overall project progress . Use AiM, shared documentation, and team collaboration tools to track project information and maintain accurate project records. Identify and resolve project challenges and operational roadblocks while adapting project scope to meet university priorities. Develop, review, and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to promote consistent and efficient project delivery. Manage project documentation, including contracts, competitive bids, product warranties, project records, and final closeout materials. Serve as the primary point of contact for project-related communication and provide timely, clear updates to stakeholders and leadership. Collaborate with University Project and Design Managers, designers, consultants, contractors, and internal Facilities teams throughout planning, design, and construction. Provide concise project status, milestone, and issue updates during weekly leadership meetings. Build strong working relationships with Grounds Leadership, Landscape Construction Services, Waste Reduction and Recycling, Grounds Planning, and other campus partners. Participate in design reviews and evaluate project plans to ensure alignment with university standards and industry best practices. Apply knowledge of landscape construction, plant and tree identification, hardscape construction, commercial irrigation systems, and stormwater control measures (SCMs) . Conduct project site inspections to verify construction meets approved designs, specifications, quality standards, and campus expectations. Identify construction issues and coordinate solutions with project partners to maintain quality and project objectives. Lead project closeout activities, including final inspections and walk-throughs, verification and filing of as-built drawings, and transition of completed projects to the Grounds Maintenance team.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: This position will support an ongoing project with the NCDOT to evaluate road ripples and the position may generally involve supporting other short duration experimental mechanical evaluations of asphalt concrete mixtures. The position will also provide some laboratory and project management support. The main duties and responsibilities include: Conduct and synthesize literature and agency-practice reviews related to road ripples, including potential formation mechanisms, diagnostic methods, contributing factors, and pavement-performance implications. Coordinate and participate in field and forensic evaluations of North Carolina pavements exhibiting road ripples, including site selection, records and data compilation, field testing, sample collection, laboratory evaluation, and comparative analysis. Plan, conduct, and analyze laboratory and modeling studies to evaluate residual moisture in asphalt mixtures and the potential short- and long-term effects of road ripples on pavement performance. Draft quarterly reports and monthly reports to support the aforementioned research project and/or similar project. May be asked to participate in other research projects related to aforementioned topic as projects are awarded. Coordinate laboratory management activities in support of the asphalt mixture analysis group tasks. This may include coordinating graduate students for cleaning, ensuring PPE is appropriately worn, ensuring supplies are ordered, and coordinating on calibrations.

title: Research Technician-Burclaff Lab
description:
Posting Number: PG195176SP
Internal Recruitment: No
Working Title: Research Technician-Burclaff Lab
Anticipated Hiring Range: $36,000-$40,000
Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 9:00 – 5:00 pm (with some flexibility) plus occasional evenings and weekends
Job Location: Raleigh, NC
Department: Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences
About the Department: North Carolina State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine (NC State CVM ) is a dynamic community whose members are dedicated to preparing veterinarians, veterinarian scientists, and biomedical scientists while advancing animal and human health from the cellular level through entire ecosystems. The Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences at the NC State CVM trains veterinarians, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows in research-based careers focused on discovering new information about animal and human health and disease and using those findings to enhance animal and human health and wellbeing.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare benefits, Wellness & Recreation Membership , and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community. Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part-Time or Full-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.
Essential Job Duties: The Burclaff Lab is interested in better understanding how metabolism and cellular energetics are regulated within intestinal stem cells and how dynamic regulation underlies the intestine’s ability to maintain itself at homeostasis and following injuries or disease. Our major focus is on the stem cell compartment, studying how the intestinal stem cells maintain their identity, undergo fate decisions, regulate cell cycle, and the dynamic plasticity that occurs within crypt populations following injury. We use a mix of animal and human models, including cutting-edge genetically modified primary human intestinal stem cell cultures, to advance our understanding of the mammalian intestine. Position Overview We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented team member to support research operations, assisting with experiments, and assist with lab management. This role combines hands-on scientific research with core lab oversight in a collaborative environment. Key Responsibilities & Qualifications Research & Lab Work: Execute experiments using animal models (mouse line maintenance/tissue collection), cell lines, and primary cultures. Perform molecular biology techniques ( RNA /protein work, staining, tissue sectioning, live-image analysis). Lab Management: Oversee day-to-day operations, manage equipment and inventory, and coordinate multiple concurrent projects. Data & Documentation: Maintain accurate records, manage scientific data, and contribute to publications, grant applications, and presentations. Technical & Problem-Solving Skills: Prior research experience required. Proficient in standard lab equipment, troubleshooting, computers, and data management tools. Work Ethic & Soft Skills: Self-motivated, highly organized, and able to work independently while fostering a collaborative, supportive team environment.
Other Responsibilities: In addition to the core responsibilities of this role, there may be occasional opportunities to take on additional duties. This offers an opportunity to build on your skills, explore new areas, and gain a deeper understanding of the department’s operations.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Experience working in a research lab Experience in mammalian primary cell culture (establishment and maintenance) Experience in molecular biology and biochemistry techniques ( PCR ; RT-qPCR; gel electrophoresis, DNA , RNA , and protein extraction; immunofluorescence; immunohistochemistry) Experience in mouse colony management (animal handling, breeding, weaning, genotyping, etc) and in vivo experimentation
Required License or Certification: N/A

title: UTS - Temporary Proctor at NC State
description: The primary purpose of this role includes but is not limited to: The Center is currently seeking a part-time employee to serve as a proctor for NC State academic exams. Proctors are responsible for ensuring exam integrity and providing superior customer service in a friendly, technology-enhanced environment. Individuals will be expected to be flexible both in hours and day-to-day operations.

title: CLAWS Lithography Engineer
description: We are seeking a highly-skilled lithography engineer to join our team and contribute to the ownership for NNF’s suite of lithography capabilities. The ideal candidate will have deep, hands-on experience in all lithographic processes; including contact lithography tools, stepper/projection lithography tools, automated wafer coat/develop stations, and e-beam/laser direct-write systems. Process Research & Development Advanced Development: Lead the design and optimization of cutting-edge photolithography processes tailored for next-generation applications, specifically targeting wide-bandgap devices for RF, power electronics, and photonics. Technical Consultation: Provide expert-level process integration support to internal and external users, translating complex device requirements into repeatable lithographic workflows. Service Excellence: Execute high-precision service work for external customers, ensuring all deliverables meet rigorous industry standards for semiconductor fabrication. Equipment Engineering & Maintenance Serve as the primary technical lead for lithography toolsets, ensuring maximum uptime and process stability through regular baseline monitoring. Maintenance & Repair: Independently perform scheduled preventative maintenance and diagnose/repair unscheduled hardware failures to minimize facility downtime. Vendor Management: Manage relationships with equipment manufacturers; coordinate complex service visits, manage service contracts, and oversee major tool overhauls. User Training & Technical Communication Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs for students and researchers, certifying users on tool operation, chemical safety, and lithographic theory. Act as the central communication hub for the lithography area, providing timely updates to management and users regarding tool status, process drifts, or facility interruptions. Facility Operations & Compliance Actively participate in facility safety audits and uphold strict cleanroom protocols to ensure a safe working environment for all personnel. Maintain meticulous records including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), maintenance logs, user databases, and training certifications. Oversee the lithography supply chain, managing the inventory of specialized chemicals, resists, and critical spare parts to ensure uninterrupted lab operations.

title: UTS - Temporary Recycling Collections Operator at NC State
description: Bulk Waste and Electronics Collections – scheduled route collections average of 180 sites per week for materials and electronics not accepted in the automated or recycling collection system. Related transport and sorting into appropriate materials bins at the Dearstyne Rolloff Site. Bulk material collections include items such as pallets, crates, discarded furniture, scrap metal, electronics, etc. Recycling and Reuse Collections – customer requested collections of reuse, recycling and unwanted building items and hauling to Dearstyne for recycling or disposal. This is on demand service for campus customers and response time is offered within 1-2 business days of the initial request. Common requests include delivery and pick up of carts for office clean outs, pick up and signature collections of confidential recycling, preparing and distributing materials for reuse in other areas or departments. Events and Projects – Field support to provide special waste/recycling/compost service for campus events and support major activities on campus such as residence hall move in and move out where additional services, monitoring and staff support are needed for collections. Repair, Maintenance, Safety – provide inspection and maintenance of containers related to the collection of waste and recycling on campus. Includes cleaning, proper labeling, delivery, distribution and placement of containers inside and outside of buildings. Inspection and maintenance of assigned trucks and equipment used daily to complete duties and assignments. Perform all work assignments and duties in compliance with established safe work practices. Follow safety and health regulations, policies and procedures. Identifies and resolves potential safety concerns or violations.

title: Research Administrator
description: Essential Job Duties As part of the College’s research administration team, The Research Administrator plays an important role in supporting faculty and ensuring the effective management of sponsored projects. The position provides financial and administrative support throughout the full award lifecycle, from proposal development and submission through award management, reporting, and closeout. By partnering with faculty and university stakeholders, this role helps ensure sponsored projects are managed effectively and in compliance with university, state, federal, and sponsor requirements. Proposal Development and Submission Prepare, compile, and submit grant and contract proposals for assigned faculty through NC State University systems, including RED, and sponsor electronic submission portals such as Grants.gov, Research.gov, and EERE Exchange. Collaborate with Principal Investigators (PIs) to develop proposal budgets, budget justifications, and other required documents in accordance with university and sponsor requirements. Create and maintain RED records for faculty and coordinate with campus offices to facilitate timely and accurate proposal submissions. Provide guidance and training to faculty within the assigned portfolio regarding NC State business processes and requirements for proposal development and submission. Review proposal documentation for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with applicable university and sponsor guidelines. Serve as a resource to faculty throughout the proposal process, identifying potential issues and coordinating resolutions with appropriate university offices. Award Management Manage an assigned portfolio of sponsored projects by monitoring financial activity, expenditures, budgets, and projections and providing Principal Investigators (PIs) with timely information to support effective project and financial decision-making. Provide financial guidance and oversight by applying accounting principles, sponsor requirements, and university policies to budgeting, forecasting, personnel expenses, cost allocations, and other fiscal activities. Partner with PIs throughout the award lifecycle by conducting regular financial reviews, discussing project spending and future plans, identifying potential issues, and recommending appropriate actions to keep projects on track. Coordinate award modifications and approvals by preparing and managing project modification requests, including rebudgeting, no-cost extensions, changes in PI, equipment purchases, travel, pre-award costs, and other actions requiring university or sponsor approval. Manage subcontracts and subawards throughout their lifecycle, including setup, monitoring, reporting, compliance, and closeout, while coordinating with PIs, university offices, and sponsoring agencies as needed. Ensure financial and regulatory compliance by monitoring sponsored project activity, reviewing personnel and financial expenditures, supporting effort certification, and addressing issues in accordance with federal, state, university, and sponsor requirements. Coordinate sponsored project closeout by resolving outstanding financial and administrative matters, completing final reconciliations, obtaining required approvals, maintaining project records, and coordinating timely submission of final reports and documentation. Grant Reporting Provide financial reports, budget analysis, and consultation to PIs to support effective fiscal management of sponsored projects. Assist PIs and project teams with sponsor-required financial and progress reporting, ensuring reports are accurate, complete, and submitted by established deadlines. Monitor and manage cost-share commitments and reporting, including maintaining appropriate supporting documentation and ensuring expenditures are accurately tracked and reported. Reconcile project financial activity and provide supporting documentation for sponsor and university reporting requirements. Respond to questions from faculty and project stakeholders regarding project financial status, reporting requirements, and allowable expenditures. Maintain accurate and complete financial records and documentation to support reporting, audits, and compliance requirements. If you are a detail-oriented professional who enjoys working with faculty, managing complex projects, and using financial expertise to support research, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Environmental Services Technician I - 40324
description: Are you looking for a fulfilling career where you can make a tangible difference in creating a clean and welcoming environment? We are seeking a passionate and detail-oriented Environmental Services Technician to join our exceptional Environmental Services team at NC State’s Facilities Division . In this vital role, you will help maintain over 10 million square feet of campus space, ensuring a safe and inviting atmosphere for students, staff, and visitors. With the support of a dynamic team of over 320 professionals, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and take pride in your work while contributing to our vibrant campus community. Join us and be a part of a team that takes pride in delivering exceptional service to one of the most prestigious campuses in the region. Apply today and help us keep NC State shining bright! Working Hours: 8:30 am - 5:00 pm, Monday – Friday Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Clean and sanitize designated areas using standard cleaning assignments to maintain a safe and hygienic environment Report any discrepancies, damages, or maintenance needs within buildings and promptly respond to emergencies and inclement weather Operate housekeeping equipment such as vacuums, mops, and scrubbers to complete tasks like dusting, disinfecting, and replenishing supplies Periodically strip and refinish floors, shampoo and extract carpets, and perform pressure washing of entrances, exterior walls, and windows Remove and manage recycling from centralized indoor recycling sites Assist with window washing and other seasonal cleaning tasks as needed Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs. Perform lifting duties up to 30 pounds frequently and 60 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations, and perform physical tasks such as grasping, pushing, and pulling cleaning equipment; reaching overhead; bending, squatting, climbing, and maintaining balance.

title: COSS Support Specialist, Gaston County
description: The County Support Specialist is a member of the staff of the North Carolina Cooperative Extension Service (NCCES). The full-time County Support Specialist’s primary responsibility is to provide specialized office support for staff and volunteers, program marketing assistance, and some administrative support duties for Extension program areas. The position duties reflect a relatively high degree of independence and accountability. Requires fluent computer and marketing skills, excellent customer service, and basic accounting skills.

title: Assistant Vice Chancellor, Campus Planning and University Architect
description: The Assistant Vice Chancellor, Campus Planning and University Architect , provides leadership for planning and strategic investment within the Facilities Division. This position leads university-wide planning initiatives that guide the long-term development, stewardship, and strategic investment of NC State’s physical environment, aligned with the university’s mission and strategic plan and serves as or supervises the university architect. The position is responsible for the development, implementation, and ongoing stewardship of the university’s Physical Master Plan , which serves as the framework for campus growth, land use, infrastructure investment, sustainability, and design decision-making across NC State’s campuses and research properties, including the Raleigh campus precincts, Lake Wheeler Field Laboratory, and Reedy Creek Field Laboratory. Reporting to senior Facilities Division leadership, the Assistant Vice Chancellor, Campus Planning and University Architect provides leadership for campus planning, infrastructure planning, facilities information systems, and sustainability initiatives. The position collaborates extensively with university leadership, the UNC System, local and regional governments, faculty, staff, students, and community stakeholders to ensure the university’s physical environment supports teaching, research, outreach, student success, and operational excellence. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Strategic Campus Planning Lead the development, implementation, and periodic updates of the university’s Physical Master Plan and Campus Development Process, including the 6-Year Capital Plan and capital budget development. Ensure campus planning and capital development initiatives align with the university’s strategic priorities, long-range vision, and design principles. Chair the Campus Design Review Panel and provide architectural leadership for campus design standards, aesthetics, development guidelines, wayfinding, and signage systems. Collaborate with Design and Construction to guide capital project planning, programming, scope development, and design review. Lead site planning, landscape planning, space programming, architectural studies, and environmental planning efforts, including the Urban Forest Management Plan and stewardship of Lake Raleigh Woods. Coordinate university engagement with municipal, regional, and community planning initiatives. Present planning recommendations and master plan updates to university leadership, the Board of Trustees, and the Buildings and Property Committee. Infrastructure Planning Lead long-range infrastructure planning, capital renewal strategies, and lifecycle management of university facilities, utilities, and major building systems. Direct the assessment, prioritization, and development of data-driven capital renewal plans, investment strategies, dashboards, and reporting tools that support institutional decision-making. Coordinate Facilities Division Capital Needs Requests and support development of biennial and long-range capital plans. Ensure infrastructure investments support institutional growth, operational reliability, risk mitigation, financial stewardship, and the strategic use of utility and asset information systems. Facilities Information Systems and Space Management Oversee campus GIS programs, mapping systems, and maintenance of the official University Campus Map. Manage building information, floor plans, room inventories, and space data systems to ensure accurate records, reporting, and strategic planning. Direct management of Facilities’ physical and digital plan room, including project documentation, as-built drawings, O&M manuals, specifications, real estate records, and hazardous materials reports. Provide analytics, reporting, and business intelligence to support space utilization, capital planning, utilities management, research administration, and university operations. Maintain building records, digital archives, and campus addressing standards. Sustainability Leadership Provide leadership for the Sustainability Office and implementation of the university’s Sustainability Strategic Plan. Advance sustainability initiatives that promote student engagement, applied learning, climate action, resource stewardship, and environmentally responsible operations. Integrate sustainability, energy efficiency, and environmental stewardship into campus planning, design, construction, renovation, and operational practices. Champion partnerships and solutions that improve building performance, reduce lifecycle costs, and support institutional sustainability goals. Governance and Committee Leadership Chair the Campus Planning Subcommittee, Space Working Group, and Campus Design Review Panel. Advise and support the Campus Development Committee on capital planning, land use, design, and space allocation decisions. Support the Board of Trustees Buildings and Property Committee on matters related to the Physical Master Plan and campus development. Serve on university committees and advisory groups related to sustainability, environmental stewardship, stormwater management, GIS, public art, and urban forestry. Support the NC State Sustainability Council and serve as an ex officio member of capital project building committees.

title: Journey Utilities Plant Operator - Nightshift
description: Behind every class, laboratory, residence hall, and campus event is a team making sure NC State has the reliable utilities it needs to operate. As a Utility Plant Operator , you’ll play a critical role in keeping the university running by operating and monitoring the central utility systems that provide electricity, steam, hot water, and chilled water across campus. This is an opportunity to work with a variety of utility equipment and gain valuable experience in a central utility environment. You’ll work alongside experienced utility professionals to monitor plant operations, troubleshoot equipment, perform inspections, and help maintain safe, efficient, and reliable service. If you're dependable, safety-minded, mechanically inclined, and interested in learning how large-scale utility systems work, we want to hear from you. Please apply today! Working Hours: 12 hr shift, 3-4 days a week, 6:00 PM - 6:00 AM. Hours may adjust to meet the needs of the organization. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Assist in the control and monitoring of steam boilers, chillers, cogeneration equipment, and auxiliary systems to ensure continuous utility services. Maintain safe and efficient operations of steam, hot water, and chilled water production systems. Conduct real-time monitoring, make necessary adjustments, and ensure compliance with emissions and regulatory standards. Inspect plant equipment, including fuel gas compressors, air filters, pumps, and cooling towers. Work under the guidance of a shift supervisor to optimize plant performance and address operational challenges. Support the operation of the Cates and Centennial Cogeneration Facilities to produce electricity and steam for the campus. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform a wide range of physically demanding tasks in varied outdoor environments, ensuring safe handling practices and maintaining productivity in varying weather and terrain conditions. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Agriculture Marketing & Content Creator Internship
description: Capture,edit, prepare and upload agricultural educational content from small grains and Official Variety Trial programs to multi-media platforms. These may include NC State University web portals, social media accounts associated with the program including but not limited to facebook, X and Instagram. Content creation will be both short and long form. Short form to include images with written captions or short video clips with closed captioning. Long form will include 2 to 5 minute video content describing an agricultural concept with closed captioning. Development of written and visual program marketing materials will also be required, along with attendance at grower meetings and larger industry events to deliver those materials to stakeholders.

title: Landscape Maintenance Technician
description: Do you enjoy working outdoors and taking pride in creating beautiful, healthy landscapes? Join NC State University’s Landscape Maintenance and Operations team as a Landscape Maintenance Technician and help shape the campus environment that students, faculty, staff, and visitors experience every day. In this hands-on role, you’ll provide professional landscape care across NC State’s campus, using your knowledge of horticulture, turf management, and landscape maintenance to keep our grounds safe, attractive, and sustainable. You’ll work as part of a dedicated team that takes pride in maintaining one of the university’s most visible and important assets, its campus landscape. If you’re dependable, enjoy hands-on work, and want to see the results of your work make a difference every day, we invite you to apply and join the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Perform routine landscape maintenance, including mowing, edging, trimming, blowing, mulching, leaf collection, and general debris removal. Install and maintain plant materials including annuals, perennials, trees, shrubs, bulbs, and sod. Apply herbicides, pesticides, and insecticides safely and in accordance with all regulatory and product guidelines. Prune shrubs, trees, and ornamental plants to promote plant health, structure, and seasonal bloom. Monitor turf and plant health, identify pests, diseases, and soil deficiencies, and report concerns promptly. Operate and perform basic maintenance on landscape equipment such as trimmers, mowers, chainsaws, blowers, and utility vehicles. Assist with turf care through soil testing, seeding, fertilization, irrigation support, and sod installation. Collaborate with the irrigation team by monitoring system performance and assisting with repairs when needed. Maintain clean, organized, and safe worksites, vehicles, and storage areas. Respond to customer and field concerns professionally, escalating issues to Field Leads or Zone Managers when appropriate. Complete daily work logs, timesheets, and records with accuracy and attention to detail. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform physically demanding outdoor tasks safely in various weather and terrain conditions. Ability to verbally communicate effectively with supervisors and the general public and understand verbal and written instructions and other communications regarding work assignments and other matters.

title: Associate Director of Autonomous Science
description: The Associate Director of Autonomous Science will contribute to advancement of the scientific and engineering vision for SPEED’s autonomous laboratories, helping transform how experiments are designed, executed, analyzed, and optimized. This is a highly collaborative leadership role at the intersection of science, robotics, artificial intelligence, and advanced laboratory automation. The Associate Director will coordinate the translation of complex scientific questions into closed-loop autonomous experiments that combine AI-driven planning, robotic experimentation, multimodal characterization, data analysis, and scientific reasoning. Working with SPEED scientists, engineers, researchers, and external users, the position will shape new capabilities, guide high-impact research programs, and ensure that autonomous experiments deliver rigorous, reproducible, and scientifically meaningful results. Primary Responsibilities: Autonomous Science and Engineering Leadership Lead design and operation of end-to-end autonomous experimentation workflows across SPEED’s robotic laboratories. Translate scientific goals into closed-loop systems spanning experimental design, robotic execution, measurement, analysis, interpretation, and AI-guided experiment selection. Define requirements for integrating synthesis, processing, characterization, optimization, and autonomous decision-making. Advance Bayesian optimization, active learning, machine learning, scientific models, genetic algorithms, and AI agents in physical laboratory systems. Establish standards for controls, validation, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility, metadata, and experimental provenance. Evaluate AI-generated recommendations for scientific validity, feasibility, safety, and alignment with research objectives. Drive improvements in SPEED’s reliability, throughput, autonomy, and scientific capabilities. Scientific Program and User Engagement Serve as scientific leader and primary point of contact for researchers using SPEED’s autonomous experimentation capabilities. Translate user questions into defined experimental objectives, strategies, and success criteria. Assess project feasibility and develop experimental plans, autonomous campaigns, analysis strategies, and validation approaches. Partner with researchers and engineers to execute projects, interpret results, and resolve scientific and technical challenges. Lead reviews of experimental results, AI recommendations, uncertainty, emerging hypotheses, and next steps. Develop sustained research partnerships with academic, government, national laboratory, and industry organizations. Expansion of SPEED Scientific Capabilities Lead development and integration of new autonomous laboratory capabilities, methods, and application areas. Identify opportunities to expand SPEED across chemistry, materials science, catalysis, molecular discovery, formulation, process development, and related fields. Define requirements for robotic platforms, analytical systems, sensors, AI tools, and integrated workflows. Guide new capabilities from concept and prototyping through commissioning, validation, and deployment. Establish benchmarks to evaluate performance, reproducibility, and transferability. Evaluate emerging technologies in laboratory robotics, scientific AI, multimodal characterization, digital twins, agentic systems, and autonomous decision-making. Develop strategies to transfer methods, models, and experimental knowledge across SPEED platforms and partner laboratories. Contribute to strategic planning, equipment investments, partnerships, proposals, publications, and initiatives advancing SPEED’s scientific mission. Research Team Leadership and Technical Coordination Provide scientific direction and mentorship to researchers, platform scientists, and engineering personnel. description: In this role, you will play a central role in advancing the Biotechnology (BIT) Program and supporting the students, faculty, and partners who make it successful. You will serve as the program expert and a trusted advisor to students, helping them navigate their academic programs, connect with opportunities, and achieve their educational and professional goals. You will work closely with BIT leadership, faculty, university offices, students, and external sponsors to coordinate courses, monitor student progress, lead communications and events, and support program reporting. You will also lead data analysis and reporting for externally funded training programs, including NSF REU and NIH T32 grants, helping demonstrate program impact and support continuous improvement. This position offers an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful program activities, build relationships across the university and beyond, and directly shape the student experience and continued growth of a dynamic biotechnology education and training program. This role focuses specifically on BIT program operations and does not oversee ISI-wide education or partnership initiatives. Communications, Outreach & Events Lead BIT communications, website content, marketing, and outreach to showcase program opportunities. Coordinate seminars, workshops, recruitment activities, visitors, and other program events. Coordinate meetings, schedules, presentations, reports, and other activities that support effective program operations. Take ownership of day-to-day program needs, solve problems, and help advance the BIT program's goals and student experience. This is a visible, multifaceted position that combines student advising, academic program management, data and reporting, communications, and event coordination . The role is well suited to a proactive, organized professional who enjoys managing varied responsibilities, solving problems independently, and serving as a trusted resource to students, faculty, leadership, and university partners. Success in this role requires strong communication and organizational skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high level of service and accuracy.

title: Sponsored Research Administrator
description: The College of Engineering is looking to hire multiple Sponsored Research Administrators (SRA) within the newly established college-managed operating model, responsible for orchestrating both pre-award and post-award lifecycles for an assigned departmental faculty portfolio. While the incumbent is physically co-located within a department to provide high-touch, localized customer service, the position is an integral part of the centralized College ORA team. The primary purpose of this role is to apply advanced accounting principles, federal/state regulations, and university guidelines to ensure the fiscal and administrative integrity of all sponsored projects. Operating under this modernized model, the incumbent must balance localized portfolio execution with central compliance directives, actively participating in college-wide resource-sharing and standardized service-level agreements (SLAs). Detailed Description of Core Responsibilities Pre-Award Portfolio Management & Proposal Development Localized Faculty Consultation: Partner directly with PIs in the embedded unit to develop accurate, compliant proposal budgets and detailed justifications from initial concept through final submission. Standardized Regulatory Screening: Analyze complex agency Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOAs) to ensure strict alignment with F&A rules, cost-sharing restrictions, budget caps, and direct cost allowability, reducing front-end submission errors. Institutional System Management: Fully execute and route records within institutional software suites, including RED Proposal Development, ensuring data integrity is validated at the departmental level before final central routing. Electronic Research Administration (eRA): Build, format, and package proposal submissions within varied sponsor portals (Research.gov, GRANTS.gov, eRA Commons, ASSIST), acting as the localized technical expert for the department's faculty. Post-Award Financial Management, Forecasting & Closeout Award Onboarding & Budget Translation: Review select incoming award notices alongside the PI to establish accurate internal ledger setups, ensuring F&A is calculated correctly based on MTDC or TDC parameters. Compliance Monitoring & Risk Mitigation: Perform continuous financial analysis of active grant ledgers. Monitor expenditures for accuracy, allowability, and strict compliance with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), Uniform Guidance, state rules, and university policies. Projections & Planning Models: Build multi-year spending projections and variance analysis models for faculty to optimize fund utilization, prevent over-expenditures, and manage labor distributions/personnel charges. Reconciliations & Cost-Share Tracking: Audit human resource expenditures, travel vouchers, and procurement charges against grant terms. Track, document, and report mandatory or voluntary committed cost-sharing obligations. Lifecycle Closeouts: Execute comprehensive closeouts for expiring grant segments. Prepare and process Project Modification Requests (PMRs) for budget modifications, no-cost extensions, or residual balance distributions, ensuring audit-ready documentation is permanently archived. Model Alignment, Cross-Coverage & Leadership Matrixed Team Collaboration: Actively participate in the broader College ORA network to ensure alignment with university-wide research administration standards. Navigate the dual priorities of central College compliance policy and local departmental workflow. Cross-College Workload Balancing: Participate in the new model's agile resource framework, willingly stepping in to provide temporary pre- or post-award coverage for other COE departments during peak submission cycles or staff absences to maintain college-wide continuity. Faculty Onboarding & Training: Develop and deliver targeted resources, onboarding guides, or info-sessions for new faculty and departmental business officers regarding centralized ORA standard operating procedures and financial management tools.

title: Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Administration
description: The Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Administration (AVC-RA) serves as the university's senior executive leader for sponsored programs and institutional research administration, providing strategic oversight of enterprise-wide pre-award services, sponsored project administration, research contracts, research administration systems, and research administration data governance. Reporting directly to the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation, the AVC leads a high-performing leadership team that includes the Director of Institutional Research Systems & Reporting, the Director of Research Administration & Campus Liaison, and additional OSP directors. Working collaboratively with university leadership, colleges, research centers, faculty, federal sponsors, and administrative partners, the AVC ensures a coordinated, compliant, and service-oriented research administration enterprise that advances NC State's research mission while strengthening institutional stewardship and operational excellence. As the AVC RA, you will shape the future of research administration at one of the nation's leading public research universities. Your leadership will influence how investigators secure external funding, how research operations evolve to meet an increasingly complex regulatory environment, and how institutional systems, data, and policies support innovation at scale. Success in this position comes from balancing strategic vision with collaborative leadership—building trusted partnerships across the university, championing continuous improvement, and fostering an environment where faculty and research administrators have the resources, guidance, and infrastructure needed to expand NC State's research impact. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Strategic Leadership & Research Administration: Provide strategic leadership for the university's sponsored programs enterprise, aligning research administration priorities with institutional goals and the evolving external funding landscape. Advise the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation and university leadership on research administration strategy, sponsored programs, regulatory compliance, institutional risk, and operational effectiveness. Lead the development and implementation of university-wide policies, governance, and business practices that strengthen research administration and support faculty success. Foster a culture of collaboration, service excellence, continuous improvement, and accountability across the Office of Sponsored Programs and the broader research community. Enterprise Oversight & Risk Management: Provide executive oversight of institutional pre-award operations, research agreements, and sponsored programs administration to ensure consistent, compliant, and customer-focused service delivery. Safeguard the university's legal, financial, and operational interests through effective risk management, contract oversight, and compliance with federal, state, and sponsor requirements. Lead the university's response to significant regulatory changes, audits, investigations, and other matters impacting the research enterprise. Research Systems, Data & Operational Excellence: Provide executive sponsorship for research administration systems, institutional data governance, and modernization initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness and decision-making. Champion technology, process improvement, and analytics strategies that strengthen research administration services and support institutional growth. Ensure research administration infrastructure evolves to meet the changing needs of faculty, sponsors, and the university. University & External Engagement: Build trusted partnerships with university leadership, faculty, colleges, and research administrators to advance the institution's research mission. Represent NC State in relationships with federal agencies, industry, nonprofit organizations, and national research administration associations. Serve as the university's senior institutional representative for complex sponsor negotiations, strategic collaborations, and matters requiring executive-level consultation. If you are a collaborative and strategic leader who is passionate about advancing research, building strong institutional partnerships, and shaping the future of research administration, we encourage you to apply.

title: Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Commercialization
description: The Associate Vice Chancellor for Research Commercialization (AVC‑RC) provides executive leadership for NC State’s commercialization enterprise, spanning intellectual property management, licensing, startup formation, venture development, and investment programs. The AVC sets university‑wide commercialization strategy, ensures compliance with federal and institutional requirements, and leads programs that accelerate the translation of research into societal and economic impact. As the AVC-RC, you will have the opportunity to expand NC State’s innovation ecosystem by connecting researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, and industry partners to accelerate the journey from discovery to impact. You will lead initiatives such as the Wolfpack Investor Network (WIN), commercialization funding programs, and the NSF I-Corps Mid-Atlantic Hub, while representing NC State within regional and national innovation communities. Through your vision, partnership-building, and strategic leadership, you will help position NC State’s research enterprise for greater economic and societal impact while advancing a culture of innovation across the university. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Strategic Leadership for Research Commercialization: Establishes and advances NC State’s research commercialization strategy, aligning innovation priorities with institutional research goals, economic development initiatives, and national R1 expectations. Sets enterprise-level priorities, performance measures, and service standards that strengthen commercialization outcomes across the university. Advises the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation on commercialization policy, innovation strategy, and external engagement. Intellectual Property, Licensing & Commercialization Governance: Provides executive oversight for intellectual property strategy, ensuring effective management, protection, and commercialization of university-developed innovations. Establishes policies, frameworks, and practices that support licensing, agreements, compliance, and responsible stewardship of intellectual assets. Provides university-wide leadership and guidance on intellectual property and commercialization matters. Venture Development & Innovation Funding: Leads NC State’s venture development ecosystem, expanding pathways for research discoveries to advance through startup formation, market validation, and investment opportunities. Provides strategic oversight for the Wolfpack Investor Network (WIN), commercialization funding programs, and NSF I-Corps Mid-Atlantic Hub activities. Cultivates relationships with investors, entrepreneurs, accelerators, and industry partners to strengthen commercialization opportunities. Innovation Ecosystem & Executive Leadership: Builds strategic partnerships with industry, investors, and innovation organizations to expand research impact and strengthen NC State’s role within regional and national innovation ecosystems. Provides leadership for a multidisciplinary commercialization team, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Ensures effective governance, operational excellence, and high-quality services that advance the university’s commercialization mission. This is an opportunity for an accomplished commercialization leader to shape strategy, influence innovation at scale, and build connections that move groundbreaking research from discovery to impact. If you are ready to lead with vision and purpose, we invite you to apply.

title: Assistant Director, Member Services and Student Employment
description: NC State University is seeking an energetic, innovative, and student-centered leader to serve as the Assistant Director of Member Services and Student Employment. We are looking for a collaborative, proven leader who thrives in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment and is passionate about student success. The ideal candidate will empower both student and professional staff to cultivate world-class wellness and recreation programs, services, and facilities that enrich the student experience inside and outside the classroom. The Assistant Director provides strategic leadership and management for Wellness and Recreation member services, point-of-sale (POS) and facility access software, and the department-wide student employment program. Additionally, the candidate will identify and develop alternative revenue streams while adding value to the student experience through special events and programming. Specific responsibilities include: Staff Supervision and Human Resource Management Direct Supervision: Provide strategic leadership, supervision, and performance management for the Coordinator of Member Services and the Student Employment Specialist. Indirect Supervision: Indirectly oversee approximately 120 student staff, ensuring the team delivers the highest level of customer service to students and members. Department-Wide Student Employment: Manage the comprehensive student employment program (recruitment, hiring, onboarding, orientation, and training) for a department that employs approximately 650 student staff annually. Process Optimization: Evaluate current HR workflows to identify efficiencies, develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and maintain comprehensive training materials for the department. Payroll & Timekeeping: Oversee complex department-wide timekeeping and payroll processes to ensure data integrity and strict deadline compliance. Student Recognition: Spearhead comprehensive student staff appreciation initiatives, including Student Employee Appreciation Week and university Wellness Days; plan, produce, and host the annual end-of-year awards ceremony for over 250 attendees to celebrate student staff achievements. Membership Growth and Marketing Membership Management: Drive the strategic growth, forecasting, and optimization of Wellness and Recreation Member Services, directly overseeing annual membership and auxiliary revenues exceeding $900k. Growth & Retention: Design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive recruitment and retention strategies; establish continuous sales pipelines for alumni, faculty, staff, and external community segments. Community Engagement: Build strong relationships with Centennial Campus affiliates and organize special events to boost member satisfaction. Marketing & Promotions: Develop high-impact marketing materials, targeted digital promotions, programmatic tours, and data-backed incentives to maximize conversion rates for prospective members. Revenue Generation and Partnerships Auxiliary Revenue Streams: Identify and cultivate alternate revenue streams, including the conceptualization and execution of specialized member events, paid programming, and creative retail or facility rentals. Corporate Partnerships: Assist with the design and execution of strategic marketing partnership/sponsorship programs; collaborate with external partners to maximize marketing packages and fundraising opportunities. Financial Oversight: Manage the specific and direct fiscal budgets for Member Services, the student staff training program, and the student professional development fund. Strategic Leadership and Systems Administration Leadership: Provide leadership and direction for Wellness and Recreation member services, point of sale and facility access software and student employment program by implementing goals, expectations and processes for programs and revenues. Systems Administration: Provide strategic direction for the maintenance, upkeep, configuration, communication, and design of InnoSoft Fusion (the department’s POS and facility access software) and FusionGO (the department’s mobile application for program registration and facility access). Compliance: Ensure all operations adhere to University, State, and Federal regulations, as well as specific departmental or governing body requirements. Committee Leadership: Lead the Wellness and Recreation student training and development work team, as well as the Fusion department work team. Data-Driven Evaluation: Serve on the Wellness and Recreation assessment work team; design satisfaction surveys, evaluate program efforts, and develop data-driven recommendations to implement new programs. title: Budget Analyst
department: 200101 - Dean's Office - Poole College Of Management
description: The Budget Analyst provides professional budget and financial support to the Poole College Office of Business Services (OBS). Reporting to the Finance Officer, the position assists academic and administrative units with budget development, financial monitoring, and reporting to support effective fiscal management. As, the Budget Analyst you will analyze financial data, prepares budget reports, monitors expenditures, and advises departments on budgetary options and the financial implications of operational decisions. Additionally, you will work collaboratively with college leadership, department administrators, and central university offices to ensure compliance with university policies and funding requirements while supporting responsible stewardship of financial resources. Primary Responsibilities include but aren't limited to: Budget Development and Financial Monitoring Assist in the preparation and maintenance of annual operating, personnel, and departmental budgets. Monitor departmental budgets throughout the fiscal year and identify variances between budgeted and actual expenditures. Review expenditures to ensure compliance with university policies, funding restrictions, and budgetary provisions. Assist departments in evaluating available funding and understanding the budgetary impact of proposed expenditures. Support year-end budget reconciliation and fiscal close activities. Monitor salary funding, labor redistributions, and position funding to ensure accurate financial reporting. Financial Analysis and Reporting Compile financial data and prepare recurring and ad hoc budget and financial reports for college leadership and departmental administrators. Analyze budget activity and financial trends to support operational decision-making. Maintain financial records and reconcile budget information using university financial systems. Assist with financial reporting for operating, trust, grant, and other funding sources as assigned. Provide supporting documentation and analysis for budget requests and financial reviews. Budget Consultation and Customer Service Advise department administrators and staff regarding budget availability, funding options, and budgetary implications of financial transactions. Respond to budget and financial inquiries from faculty, staff, and administrators. Interpret university financial policies and procedures related to budget administration. Build collaborative relationships with academic and administrative units to support effective financial management. Provide guidance on budget processes and financial reporting requirements. Systems, Processes, and Continuous Improvement Assist in developing and maintaining budget tracking tools, spreadsheets, and standard financial reports. Identify opportunities to improve budget processes and reporting efficiency. Support implementation of process improvements and updates to financial systems. Maintain accurate financial documentation and records. If you are a detail-oriented financial professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights, solving problems, and partnering with others to support sound financial decisions, we invite you to apply.
