title: Postdoctoral Appointee of Anatomy, Cell Biology & Physiology
description: The laboratory of Dr. Carol Witczak in the Department of Anatomy, Cell Biology & Physiology at the Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM) is searching for a postdoctoral appointee to join our research team. The Witczak lab has broad interests in the mechanisms regulating skeletal muscle metabolism under physiological, pathological, and pharmacological conditions, such as exercise, type 2 diabetes, and weight loss drug therapies. The Witczak laboratory uses state-of-the-art technologies, novel pharmacological/chemical reagents, and tissue-specific mutant mouse models to investigate the underlying mechanisms controlling muscle growth and metabolic flux. The projects are multidisciplinary with excellent opportunities for advanced training and scientific development. Current projects funded by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) include: 1) determining the role of glucose in the regulation of muscle hypertrophic growth; 2) identifying the glucose transporter(s) activated by resistance training in muscle; and 3) examining the connections between glucometabolic flux and the muscle transcriptome. For more information see: https://medicine.iu.edu/faculty-labs/witczak Successful candidates will have recently completed PhD training, possess a strong background in type 2 diabetes, metabolism, and/or skeletal muscle physiology, have extensive experience working with mouse models, and have a strong publication record. The selected candidate will join a dynamic, collaborative, and fast-paced research environment, working closely with Dr. Witczak and other members of the laboratory while also contributing independently to ongoing and new research projects. Responsibilities include developing and implementing novel research methods, conducting in vitro and in vivo experiments, planning and managing research projects, interpreting data, preparing presentations and peer-reviewed publications, assisting with laboratory management, training personnel, and contributing to grant applications. The Principal Investigator is committed to supporting the candidate's scientific and professional development by fostering grant submissions, providing opportunities to attend and present at scientific conferences, and encouraging exploration of new research directions and collaborations. Salary and benefits are provided in accordance with National Institutes of Health (NIH) guidelines. The Department of Anatomy, Cell Biology & Physiology has the dedicated mission of improving human health. It houses cutting-edge biomedical research programs focused on a variety of diseases/disorders, including osteoporosis, muscular dystrophy, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, etc. The department has a long history of synthesizing different subdisciplines of the life sciences—including cell and molecular biology, genetics, biophysics and physiology, anatomical structure, histology, neuroscience, and imaging—to solve complex health problems from a basic science perspective. This integration of diverse disciplines provides a rich scientific environment for biomedical researchers. More information about the Department is available at: https://medicine.iu.edu/anatomy-cell-biology-physiology The Indiana Center for Musculoskeletal Health (ICMH) has the mission to discover and develop new treatments, cures, preventative strategies, diagnostic tools and technologies to address the increasing burden of bone, muscle and cartilage disorders. The ICMH is an integrated research facility and consists of core facilities directed towards the study of muscle-bone interactions. The facilities include full-service histology, microscopy (fluorescent, confocal, and electron), tissue culture, animal surgery and imaging rooms, providing a rich scientific environment for basic science and translational research of the musculoskeletal system. More information about the ICMH is available at: https://medicine.iu.edu/research-centers/musculoskeletal The Center for Diabetes and Metabolic Diseases at the IU School of Medicine (CDMD) has the mission to foster knowledge, support training, and promote basic and translational research in diabetes and related metabolic disorders. The CDMD is an integrated research facility and highly collaborative environment that promotes learning and encourages interaction amongst investigators and trainees. More information about the CDMD is available at: https://medicine.iu.edu/research-centers/diabetes The Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM) is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. It is growing economically thanks to a strong corporate base anchored by the life sciences. Indiana is home to one of the largest concentrations of health sciences companies in the nation. Residents of this dynamic city, and surrounding suburbs, enjoy leading educational systems and top-ranked universities, paired with a diverse population. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Quantum Materials and Quantum Optics
description: Working under the direction of Dr. Iqbal Utama, the postdoctoral fellow will lead experimental research focused on low-dimensional, molecular, and hybrid organic–inorganic materials for applications in quantum sensing, quantum photonics, and related quantum technologies. The successful candidate will design, fabricate, and characterize quantum materials and nanoscale devices, contribute to scientific publications and research proposals, and mentor graduate and undergraduate students in a collaborative research environment. This is an outstanding opportunity for early-career researchers to advance an independent research program, build a strong publication record, and contribute to cutting-edge developments in quantum science and technology within a highly interdisciplinary and well-supported academic setting. Specific Duties: Conduct experimental research on low-dimensional, molecular, and hybrid organic–inorganic materials for quantum sensing, quantum photonics, and related quantum technologies. Design, fabricate, and characterize quantum-material and nanoscale devices using techniques that may include materials synthesis and processing, nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, magnetometry, and optically-detected magnetic resonance. Develop experimental protocols and assist with the setup, operation, maintenance, and documentation of laboratory instruments. Analyze and interpret experimental data and maintain complete, organized records of experiments, procedures, and results. Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present research findings at scientific meetings. Contribute to the preparation of research proposals, technical reports, and collaborative projects. Mentor graduate and undergraduate students and provide training in relevant laboratory methods. Contribute to a safe, collegial, collaborative, and intellectually engaged laboratory environment. Anticipated start date: December 1, 2026, or a mutually agreed date thereafter. Anticipated end date: November 30, 2027, based on a December 1, 2026 start date. Appointment term: The initial appointment will be for 12 months. The appointment may be renewed annually, subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funding.

title: Research Associate – Public Health Specialist
description: Prevention Insights at the Indiana University School of Public Health-Bloomington invites applications for a Research Associate – Public Health Specialist. This position will begin on or around August 31, 2026. Applications received by August 14, 2026 will receive full consideration and will continue to be accepted until the position is filled. This is a one-year position that is subject to annual renewal. The work structure will be hybrid, including a combination of remote work, on-site work at Prevention Insights, and occasional in-state travel for meetings, trainings, or site visits. About Us : Prevention Insights is a center in the Indiana University School of Public Health-Bloomington that has been in operation for nearly 40 years. The center is located in Bloomington, Indiana and currently employs 26 full-time staff and faculty members. Prevention Insights is funded almost entirely through grants and contracts from federal, state, and other extramural organizations. The center provides a range of public health services that includes technical assistance, coaching, and consultation to non-profits and community-based partnerships implementing substance abuse prevention or related health and wellness initiatives at the community level. We also provide training in other evidence-based models and approaches (e.g., Screening, Brief Intervention, Referral to Treatment [SBIRT], Motivational Interviewing [MI], mental health) and provide services that include in evaluation, survey design and administration, customized application and web development, grant writing, translational research, and regulatory compliance, among other topics. Prevention Insights works with single state agencies, technology transfer centers, prevention networks, hospitals, companies, and organizations across the country. Responsibilities: This role’s primary responsibility will be to provide technical assistance (including consultation and coaching) as well as skill-building education via synchronous and asynchronous trainings, webinars, and resource development to communities that have received state funding from the Indiana Division of Mental Health and Addiction, which may include onsite visits as well as utilizing various technologies including email, telephone, zoom, websites, and other online modalities. The candidate will work as part of a technical assistance team but will ultimately be directly responsible for supporting multiple communities as the primary point of contact for technical assistance. Typically, this technical assistance will take the following forms: · Offering technical assistance in prevention process for all competencies across the 10 essential public health services and the Strategic Prevention Framework, including assessment and qualitative and quantitative data utilization, organizational and community-level capacity development, comprehensive strategic planning and program selection, use of evidence-based models with assurance of fidelity and population saturation, prevention infrastructure and coalition development, and evaluation framework application and utilization. · Offering training, work sessions, meetings, consultations, phone calls and webinars to allow for resource sharing, coaching, fiscal compliance, report requirements, and capacity building. · Providing feedback on data assessments, reviewing reports, and giving guidance for community planning and implementation. · Creating webinars, resource documents, worksheets, and tailored tools to support the milestones and benchmarks associated with implementation of the Strategic Prevention Framework with fidelity. · Occasionally offering one-on-one coaching, group instruction, facilitated planning, or resource sharing. Because Prevention Insights is a grant- and contract-funded organization, employees often operate in multiple work areas at once. While technical assistance will be the primary work area, the candidate will likely be asked to participate in other projects on an ad hoc basis to contribute to center growth. This work may include, but is not limited to: · Assisting with other technical assistance, evaluation, or training projects. · Contributing to grant writing. · Leading or contributing to smaller independent projects. · Participation in taskforces to accomplish specific goals (e.g., working with an external advisory board). People who thrive when provided with a large degree of independence and an expectation for high-quality work will likely enjoy this position.

title: Assistant Research Professor of Pediatrics
description: The Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research conducts basic science and translational research within the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine. The Wells Center houses more than 300 faculty investigators, staff, and trainees seeking answers to the most pressing questions related to childhood illness. With the collaboration between scientists and physicians, the center aims to increase knowledge of causes and mechanisms of serious pediatric diseases. Our goal is to develop innovative approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of sick children in Indiana and beyond. The laboratory of Dr. Emily K. Sims at the Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research is seeking a highly motivated Scientist with expertise in molecular biology techniques and type 1 diabetes. The successful candidate will contribute to an NIH-funded research project focused on interferon alpha impacts on islet extracellular vesicles. Responsibilities: Design, conduct, and analyze experiments related to extracellular vesicles in in vitro islet models, human islets, and human blood samples. Perform animal studies, including handling, treatment, and tissue collection. Collaborate with other researchers to advance the project’s scientific goals. Maintain accurate experimental records and prepare data for presentations, publications, and grant reports. Contribute to a productive and collegial laboratory environment. IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Biochemistry, Molecular Biology & Pharmacology
description: The Department of Biochemistry, Molecular Biology and Pharmacology (BMBP) at the Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position. Competitive applicants will build a research program that investigates fundamental mechanisms of human health and disease, complements existing programs in BMBP and at the IU Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center, the Stark Neurosciences Research Institute, or the Center for Diabetes and Metabolic Diseases, and is competitive for external funding. Candidates are also expected to contribute to graduate and professional education at IUSM. Applicants must hold a PhD (or equivalent) in biochemistry, pharmacology, molecular biology, or a closely related field. To apply, submit a CV, a cover letter (2 pages max), a research statement outlining future plans (3 pages max), and contact information for at least three references. title: University Archivist
description: IU Indianapolis University Library seeks a University Archivist to join the Ruth Lilly Special Collections and Archives, part of Distinctive Collections. The University Archivist reports to the Director of Distinctive Collections and works collaboratively with library colleagues, faculty, and Indiana University partners to collect and provide access to university records. The position advances institutional priorities related to student and faculty research as well as community engagement and collaboration. This position will work with records of all types, including born-digital records such as websites, emails, and digital files, as well as audio-visual material. The University Archivist will support the full lifecycle of university records, which includes liaising with staff and faculty units about records management policies and the value of institutional records before transfer to the archives, as well as providing education and reference to researchers using these records of permanent value. Responsibilities Actively collect university records deemed of permanent value, including born digital materials and university websites Supervise and perform University Archives collection management activities: accessioning, processing, preservation, and creation of finding aids, including training and supervising student workers to assist in this work Provide reference services for University Archives, assisting virtual and in-person researchers (faculty, students, staff, and other researchers) in using university records Liaise with campus offices on the interpretation and implementation of records retention schedules Manage web archiving of university websites, including appraising URLs and setting appropriate capture schedules Promote interest in the history of IUI/IUPUI and the historic neighborhoods predating the campus, through reference, instruction, and outreach efforts Collaborate with Ruth Lilly Special Collections & Archives department members to improve service, provide access to collections, develop policies and procedures, and move department initiatives forward Secondary responsibilities Participate in development of records management policies in partnership with other campus archivists and the University Records Manager Serve as a member of the Digital Collections Advisory Group, which is charged with setting priorities, establishing best practices for digital collections creation, and evaluating potential digital collections projects Participate in University Library planning and decision-making activities Participate in University Library and campus faculty organizations Represent the library in local, state, and national library venues as appropriate. Participate in library and university initiatives that advance campus and community engagement with distinctive collections Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of University Library.

title: Religious Collections Cataloging Librarian
description: Indiana University Bloomington Libraries’ Lilly Library seeks a collaborative, enthusiastic, and innovative librarian to serve as the inaugural Religious Collections Cataloging Librarian. Funded by a dedicated endowment , the cataloger will work closely with the Head, Cataloging & Description, and the Curator of Religious Collections to describe and make available Lilly Library materials relating to religion and spirituality in all formats. The Lilly Library is Indiana University’s principal rare books, manuscripts, and special collections library. The library’s actively used and dynamically growing collections encompass manuscripts, printed books, and devotional objects spanning a wide chronological and geographical span. Core strengths include European medieval and Renaissance religious manuscripts, early printed Bibles in many languages, hymnological resources, and rare works produced in the Spanish, Portuguese, and Dutch colonial worlds. The collections also feature significant materials from Asian and Islamic religious traditions. Active collecting areas include pilgrimage, religious materials created for and by children, and religious narratives related to disability. The majority of these collections are in English, Latin, Italian, French, German, and Spanish, with other languages represented in smaller numbers. The successful candidate will work in a collaborative environment with colleagues within the Lilly Library and the IU Libraries system. This is a tenure-track position with requirements for ongoing professional development and service. Responsibilities Reporting to the Head, Cataloging & Description, the Religious Collections Cataloging Librarian will: Serve as the primary cataloger for all Lilly Library materials relating to religion and spirituality in all formats. Organize and lead special projects relating to intellectual and physical control of Lilly Library materials relating to religion and spirituality. Collaborate with the Curator of Religious Collections on interpreting and increasing awareness of the Lilly Library’s collections relating to religion and spirituality. Participate in departmental conversations and contribute to internal policy development and documentation. Keep abreast of national developments in cataloging standards and best practices as they emerge and develop. Engage in service and professional development activities that enrich the librarian’s practice and contribute meaningfully to the profession.

title: Assistant, Associate or Full Professor of Music (Double Bass); Tenure of Tenure-track position
description: The Jacobs School of Music seeks candidates for a position in the Department of Strings in Double Bass. The successful candidate will have an extensive and successful background as a performer and teacher at the highest national and/or international level, will be able to work effectively with faculty colleagues, and will be able to inspire students in a professionally-oriented educational environment. Participation in departmental meetings, recruitment activities and auditions, doctoral committees, and recital hearing committees, along with other department activities, such as faculty recitals and outreach activities, master classes, service on Jacobs School of Music committees, and other similar activities is expected.

description: The Jacobs School of Music seeks candidates for a position in the Percussion Department in general/orchestral percussion/timpani. Studio instruction for undergraduate and graduate percussion students as well as chamber music coaching. Orchestral repertoire class (percussion/timpani) may also be a component of this job. title: Postdoctoral Fellow - RPBS Lab
description: The RPBS Lab invites applications for Postdoctoral Researcher positions. Postdocs will lead independent research projects at the interface of focused ultrasound, synthetic biology, and cancer immunotherapy while mentoring graduate and undergraduate students. This is an excellent opportunity for early-career scientists looking to develop a strong publication record and build an independent research trajectory within a highly collaborative and well-resourced environment. Research Areas Sonogenetics — engineering ultrasound-responsive genetic circuits for non-invasive cellular control Mechanotransduction — investigating how mechanical forces from focused ultrasound alter immune cell function and tumor microenvironments Acoustic tool development — designing next-generation transducers, wearable ultrasound devices, and integrated imaging-therapy platforms Translational immunotherapy — combining ultrasound priming with CAR T and other cellular therapies for solid tumors What We Offer Competitive NIH-scale salary with full benefits through Indiana University Dedicated mentorship toward career development, grant writing, and faculty applications Access to shared core facilities (imaging, flow cytometry, animal resources) within the Luddy School and IU Bloomington Travel funding for conference presentations A collaborative, interdisciplinary research culture

title: Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA) / Borns Jewish Studies Program, Indiana University Bloomington - Visiting Fellow in Antisemitism Studies
description: Title: Visiting Fellow in Antisemitism Studies Appointment Status: Non-Tenure Track Department/Program: Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA) / Borns Jewish Studies Program, Indiana University Bloomington Location: Bloomington, Indiana Term: One-year appointment with the possibility of renewal for a second year Salary & Support: $57,000 plus health benefits Position Summary: The Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA) in the Borns Jewish Studies Program at Indiana University Bloomington invites applications for a Visiting Fellow in Antisemitism Studies. ISCA is one of the leading research institutes dedicated to the scholarly study of contemporary antisemitism, and this fellowship offers an exceptional opportunity to pursue original research in the field while contributing to the intellectual life of the institute and the broader program. The fellowship is open to scholars working in any discipline and using any methodological approach, including but not limited to historical, sociological, computational, psychological, legal, literary, or educational perspectives on antisemitism. We particularly welcome candidates whose work addresses contemporary manifestations of antisemitism in Europe, North America, the Middle East, or online environments, and whose research complements and enriches ISCA’s existing portfolio of projects. Position is expected to begin January 1, 2027, for a one-year term, with the possibility of renewal for a second year. For more information about ISCA and its current research, please visit: https://isca.indiana.edu Core Responsibilities: Research Pursue an independent, original research agenda in antisemitism studies, resulting in publications, conference presentations, or other scholarly outputs. Participate actively in ISCA seminars, colloquia, research workshops, and collaborative discussions. Contribute to ISCA’s public-facing activities, including events, reports, and media engagement as appropriate. Collaborate with ISCA faculty and research staff on ongoing and emerging projects. Teaching Teach one course per semester on antisemitism or a closely related topic, at the undergraduate or graduate level, in coordination with the Borns Jewish Studies Program. Community and Program Engagement Participate in the intellectual community of the Borns Jewish Studies Program through lectures, workshops, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Contribute to grant writing and funding applications in support of ISCA’s research mission as appropriate. Mentor graduate and undergraduate students engaged in antisemitism-related research where relevant. Qualifications: Required: PhD in a relevant field. The PhD must be completed by the start of the appointment. Demonstrated research focus on antisemitism. Strong record of scholarly publication or a clear publication trajectory based on dissertation or postdoctoral work. Ability to work collegially in an interdisciplinary research environment. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Preferred: Regional or thematic expertise in contemporary antisemitism (e.g., Europe, North America, online/digital environments, the Middle East, campus contexts). Experience with or interest in public-facing scholarship, policy engagement, or applied research. Proficiency in languages relevant to the study of antisemitism Prior teaching experience at the university level. Applications Materials: To apply, please submit the following through Indiana University's PeopleAdmin system at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34103 A cover letter describing your research agenda, scholarly background, and why you are interested in this fellowship, including your available start date. A current curriculum vitae. A writing sample (article, dissertation chapter, or equivalent, up to 40 pages). A brief teaching statement (1–2 pages), including a proposed course on antisemitism. Contact information for three references. For questions about the position, contact Gunther Jikeli ( gjikeli@iu.edu ). Timing: Review of applications will begin September 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.

title: Director, Center for Intellectual Property Research and Professor of Law
department: IU Bloomington Maurer School of Law
description: The Indiana University Maurer School of Law is seeking an outstanding lateral candidate to join our faculty as a tenured professor of law and to serve in the role of Director of the Center for Intellectual Property Research. Founded in 2009, the Center oversees the law school’s intellectual property curriculum and programming, its co-curricular activities, its scholarly research in intellectual property and related areas, and its outreach to the practicing bar. The law school’s curriculum includes numerous upper-level courses in intellectual property law and adjacent areas such as information policy, health law, AI and the law, and other aspects of law and technology, which are taught by both full-time and adjunct members of the law school’s faculty. The Law School seeks a Director who will oversee the Center’s scholarly mission, coordinating scholarly symposia, visits of distinguished speakers, and similar activities. The Director also oversees the law school’s intellectual property pro bono activities, including, in conjunction with the Intellectual Property Clinic director, the management of the Intellectual Property Clinic and the PatentConnect pro bono patent hub program, pursuant to a partnership agreement with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. The Director works closely with the law school’s Career Services Office to coordinate career-related presentations as well as the Office of Admissions to coordinate programming for prospective law students who may have an interest in intellectual property law, particularly prospective students who are enrolled in science or engineering degree programs. The Director has supervisory responsibility for staff personnel of the Center.

description: The Business Economics and Public Policy Department at the Kelley School of Business, Indiana University, Bloomington, invites applications for open rank tenure-track/tenured faculty positions to begin Fall 2027.

title: Non-Tenure Track Clinical Faculty Position in Environmental Sustainability
description: The O’Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs (O’Neill) at Indiana University, Bloomington seeks a sustainability professional with deep experience in environmental sustainability (including environmental sustainability intermingled with social and/or economic sustainability) to join our faculty as a full-time, non-tenure track, clinical assistant professor or for exceptionally qualified candidates, clinical associate professor. The clinical faculty track requires teaching as well as public or professional service that can include applied research and providing professional/technical expertise to public, professional, and nonprofit organizations (e.g., as a consultant). We seek someone who can teach courses in environmental sustainability and related topics and maintain active engagement with the professional field of sustainability. Clinical faculty may advance to higher rank and long-term contracts on the basis of excellence in teaching or service. Teaching may include traditional classroom instruction, experiential and active learning, and project-based courses and practica that may include collaborations with external partners. The successful candidate will leverage their professional expertise to provide students with applied, interdisciplinary learning experiences that prepare them to address real-world sustainability challenges and will mentor students as rising professionals. They will also provide leadership on initiatives that strengthen the School’s visibility, impact and connections to practice in sustainability. The long-term teaching load for Clinical faculty is typically 6 courses per year, possibly with lighter starting loads and reductions to balance heavy service loads when those arise. Clinical faculty are not eligible for tenure but will be considered for promotion and/or long-term contracts no later than the sixth year of appointment. Salary and rank are commensurate with qualifications and experience. The expected start date is August 1, 2027. O’Neill-Bloomington contains a vibrant student and faculty community and is the largest school of public affairs and public policy in the United States, with over 4,000 students, and for five years has ranked in one of the top two spots of the U.S. News & World Report rankings for graduate public affairs schools in the country. Six of O’Neill’s specialty programs are ranked in the top five listings nationally; O’Neill is also tied for the top-ranked public administration program according to the 2020 Academic Ranking of World Universities. The school attracts very high performing faculty and students and provides a collegial workplace environment. Indiana University is a major research University founded in 1820 and currently enrolls over 38,000 undergraduates and 10,000 graduate and professional students on the Bloomington campus. Additional information about the school and Indiana University can be found at https://oneill.indiana.edu/ . Bloomington is a welcoming community located in the beautiful, wooded hills of southern Indiana approximately 1 hour from Indianapolis and 4 hours from Chicago, with abundant cultural and recreational opportunities, low housing costs, and excellent schools. Additional information about the city of Bloomington can be found at https://www.visitbloomington.com/ . To ensure consideration, application materials must be received by November 1, 2026. However, the search may continue until the position is filled. Please submit via the online system https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34089 , the following materials: 1) a letter of application; 2) a current vita that includes a history of academic and professional experience; 3) a statement of teaching philosophy including approaches to course design and classroom instruction; 4) evidence of successful teaching, training, and/or related professional experience (including online/distance-learning instructional experience, if applicable) and 5) contact information for three references. For more information, please contact the search committee chair: Dr. Vicky Meretsky ( meretsky@iu.edu ).

title: Open Rank Clinical positions, Kelley School of Business (Operations and Decision Technologies, Information Systems)
department: IU Bloomington Operations and Decision Technologies
description: The Operations and Decision Technologies (ODT) Department of the Kelley School of Business at Indiana University – Bloomington invites applications for an open-rank, non-tenure-track clinical faculty position in Information Systems (IS) beginning in Fall 2027. Clinical faculty play a critical role in the dept and School’s success. We offer opportunities to advance through the ranks, and clinical faculty are eligible for leadership roles within the School and the University.

title: Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA) / Borns Jewish Studies Program - Leslie J. Raffel Chair in Antisemitism Studies (Research Professor)
description: Title: Leslie J. Raffel Chair in Antisemitism Studies (Research Professor) Appointment Status Non-Tenure Track (Research Professor), Open Rank – Senior Preferred Department Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA) Robert A. and Sandra S. Borns Jewish Studies Program Indiana University Bloomington Location Bloomington, Indiana Position Summary The Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA), housed within the Robert A. and Sandra S. Borns Jewish Studies Program at Indiana University Bloomington, invites applications for the Leslie J. Raffel Chair in Antisemitism Studies. The appointment will be at the rank of Research Professor (open rank, with preference for associate or full professor). It is expected to begin January 1, 2027, for a term of up to five years, subject to review, with potential consideration for renewal. The Raffel Chair represents a significant investment in advancing Indiana University’s global leadership in the interdisciplinary study of antisemitism. We seek a widely recognized scholar, in any academic discipline, whose work addresses the most urgent contemporary forms of antisemitism. The occupant of the Chair is expected to be fully conversant with the long history of anti-Jewish hostility while maintaining a primary focus on the most consequential present-day expressions of hostility directed against Jews, Judaism, and the State of Israel. The Chair will provide intellectual leadership at the highest level—strengthening research initiatives, convening scholars across disciplines, expanding strategic partnerships, and pursuing external funding to advance major projects. This is a full-time research appointment. Basic Qualifications • Ph.D. or equivalent terminal degree in a relevant field • An established record of significant scholarly achievement focused on antisemitism • Demonstrated expertise in contemporary manifestations of antisemitism • Evidence of sustained research productivity Preferred Qualifications • Senior scholarly standing • Record of successful external grant funding • Demonstrated capacity for intellectual leadership and interdisciplinary collaboration • Experience mentoring graduate students and advanced undergraduate students. Scholars from the humanities, social sciences, law, media studies, political science, psychology, sociology, history, religious studies, and related fields are encouraged to apply. Application Instructions Interested candidates should submit: • Cover letter • Curriculum vitae • Research statement • Names and addresses of three references Applications received by September 15, 2026 will receive full consideration, but the search will remain open until the position is filled. Applications must be submitted electronically at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/33982 For questions about the position, please contact: Alvin H. Rosenfeld, Director, Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism at rosenfel@iu.edu .

title: Chair, Department of Endodontics
department: IU Indianapolis Department of Endodontics – School of Dentistry
description: Indiana University School of Dentistry (IUSD) invites applications for Chair, Department of Endodontics. This full-time 12-month appointment type on either a clinical or tenure-track (Preferably TT) appointment at the rank of associate professor or full professor, based upon credentials and qualifications. The anticipated start date of January 1, 2027, or sooner. For candidates seeking appointment on the tenure track, application materials must include evidence of sustained scholarly activity consistent with School and University expectations. The successful candidate should have academic leadership experience, a national reputation for excellence in the discipline of Endodontics, documented success in leading strategic initiatives and a strong record of scholarship and research. The Department of Endodontics is responsible for the endodontics education of pre-doctoral dental students and graduate students in our Endodontics residency program. The Department Chair provides leadership for the vision, strategic direction, and long-term growth of the Department of Endodontics in alignment with the mission and priorities of the School of Dentistry. The Chair is responsible for overseeing departmental operations, faculty and staff supervision, curriculum management, and fiscal stewardship. This role includes mentoring and evaluating faculty; providing input on promotion, tenure, reappointment, and merit processes; and ensuring high-quality didactic and clinical education within the full scope of Endodontics. The Chair reports to the Dean. The Chair works collaboratively with other members of the Dean’s cabinet, including department chairs, and associate deans, as well as the Office of Clinical Affairs team to support effective clinical education, patient care, and faculty development. Responsibilities include managing departmental curriculum and academic workload assignments, aligning teaching responsibilities with clinical operations, ensuring compliance with CODA accreditation standards and institutional policies, and supporting faculty scholarship and professional growth. The Chair communicates regularly with the Dean, participates in school leadership and committee meetings, and serves as a key liaison between departmental faculty and School administration. There is an expectation that the Chair will play a teaching role as part of their duties and responsibilities; providing clinical and classroom teaching and supervision. There are opportunities for the Chair to supervise and mentor residents in research related to their postdoctoral program and assist in the preparation of postdoctoral dental students for specialty board examinations. Faculty members are expected to foster transformative learning that is informed by interdisciplinary and translational research, scholarship, and creative expression. Our Commitment As the state’s premier urban research institution, Indiana University is committed to being a welcoming campus community. As a member of that community, the IU School of Dentistry seeks candidates whose teaching, service, scholarship, research and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning, working, and patient care environments. This commitment is core to our mission through our school-owned clinics and educational programs in Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, Indiana. IUSD offers a dynamic learning environment for faculty, in which teaching, research, clinical care, and community service are core to our mission through our School-owned clinics and educational programs in Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, Indiana. Our main facility includes a state-of-the-art 45,000–square-foot James J. Fritts DDS Clinical Care Center on the IU-Indianapolis campus, adjacent to local hospitals and part of an urban academic health center.

title: Assistant/Associate/Professor of Clinical Pathology & Laboratory Medicine
description: The Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at the Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM), in partnership with IU Health Medical Group (IUHMG), is seeking to recruit an anatomic pathologist with strong diagnostic skills in surgical pathology and cytopathology at our IU Health Ball Memorial Hospital in Muncie, Indiana. Additional specific subspecialty areas are welcome. The pathology footprint at Ball Memorial currently includes two full-time anatomic pathologists (this position will expand to three full-time pathologists), a pathologists’ assistant, and one cytologist. This recruitment is part of a strategic expansion driven by continued growth across the Indiana University Health (IU Health) system. IU Health is committed to expanding access to high-quality, patient-centered care, with growing opportunities at our Ball Memorial Hospital in Muncie, Indiana. Ball offers a comprehensive range of services, including emergency, surgical, and specialty care, bringing advanced healthcare closer to home for individuals and families in the region. IU Health Ball is part of the 17-hospital IU Health Laboratory System, served by approximately 70 anatomic pathologists. Although based in Muncie, the pathologists at Ball have access to the expertise of the subspecialized pathologists operating out of the department’s IU Health Central Pathology Laboratory in Indianapolis. Being a part of the expansive IU Health Laboratory system affords the ideal candidate the ability to practice in a community environment with the support of the enriched environment created by an academic pathology practice. Responsibilities: Provide diagnoses of benign and malignant conditions, including tumor grading and staging. Interpret intraoperative consultations (e.g., frozen sections). Correlate histopathologic findings with clinical, radiologic, and laboratory data. Prepare and sign out pathology reports in a timely and accurate manner. Participate in multidisciplinary tumor boards and clinical case discussions. Ensure quality assurance and compliance with laboratory standards (e.g., CAP, CLIA). Interpret cytologic specimens, including Pap smears, fine needle aspirations (FNA), and body fluids. Provide diagnostic consultations to clinicians and participate in multidisciplinary case reviews. Perform and supervise FNAs, including rapid on-site evaluations (ROSE). Provide on-call coverage and conference support with department faculty members. Minimum Qualifications: A Doctorate or terminal degree (MD, DO, or equivalent) is required. Board certification by the American Board of Pathology in Anatomic Pathology or Anatomic and Clinical Pathology. Completion of a Surgical Pathology Fellowship or equivalent experience. Eligibility for medical licensure in the state of Indiana. Cytopathology experience. Preferred Qualifications: Completion of a Cytopathology fellowship or equivalent experience, along with board certification in Cytopathology. Benefit Information: Strong base salary that is not RVU-based. IUSM and IUHMG is committed to providing inclusive benefits for eligible employees and their families. to learn more, click here: IU - https://hr.iu.edu/benefits IUHMG - https://team.myiuhealth.org/benefits About the IUSM: IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Clinical Pediatrics
description: The Division of Pediatric Infectious Disease in the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking to add a clinical track faculty physician to provide patient care at Riley Hospital for Children and serve as a clinical educator for our school of medicine students and trainees. A majority of the clinical time will be spent as an inpatient attendee, split between general and immunocompromised ID, approximately 10-14 weeks, and staffing up to one half-day clinic per week. Additionally, this role will provide support for urgent outpatient phone consults for 6-8 weeks and the remainder of clinical service will be dedicated to antimicrobial stewardship. The Department of Pediatrics at IUSM/Riley Hospital for Children is a 398-member faculty that is consistently within the top 10 pediatric departments in NIH funded research in the United States and has 19 Fellowship programs. There is a new large pediatric clinical research center, a new pediatric outpatient center dedicated to general pediatrics and neurodevelopment related divisions in pediatrics, genetics, and psychiatry. There are also State-of-the-art laboratories in a dedicated pediatric research building, a clinical research center, a well-functioning biobank, six T32 fellow training grants and one K12s that support research in the Department. Our nationally recognized Division of Children’s Health Research is available for collaboration and as a resource for combined fellowships with the pediatric hospitalist program. The Department also has research relationships with the Regenstrief Institute in Health Informatics. Pediatric Radiology and Pediatric Neuroradiology are strong research partners. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. title: Roger E. Covey Professorship in Silk Road Studies (Open Rank, Tenure Track)
description: The Department of Central Eurasian Studies in the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies at Indiana University Bloomington seeks to make a tenure-track or tenured hire (open rank) to fill the Roger E. Covey Professorship in Silk Road Studies. The successful candidate will contribute to the Department’s mission in the study of Central Eurasia and play a leading role in advancing Silk Road Studies across the Hamilton Lugar School and beyond. Applicants should have an established or emerging record of innovative research on the overland and/or maritime Silk Roads (2nd century BCE through 15th century CE) and their relevance to the contemporary world. We welcome applications from scholars whose research advances understanding of one or more aspects of the histories, societies, religions, languages, politics, diplomacy, material worlds, and interconnections of the overland and/or maritime Silk Roads. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in one or more major languages necessary to conduct original research in their area of specialization, including the use of primary sources. Proficiency in one or more languages taught in or closely affiliated with the Department is also highly desirable. Additionally, applicants should demonstrate excellence in teaching in Silk Road-related Studies, and a commitment to public engagement and program development of Silk Road Studies within the Department as well as within the Hamilton Lugar School. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to teach classes appealing to a broad range of students at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Teaching will be conducted in English. Review of applications will begin immediately, with all applications received by September 30, 2026 being guaranteed full consideration. The appointment begins August 1, 2027. Required Application Materials: Application materials must include a cover letter, curriculum vitae/resume, career statement describing research, service, teaching experiences and contact information of three academic referees, samples of published, in-press, and forthcoming research works, and previous teaching materials and course evaluations. Applicant referees will receive an email link to submit their letters of reference directly to the search committee through the PeopleAdmin interface. Application materials may be submitted via the PeopleAdmin applicant portal at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34008

title: Postdoctoral Fellow - – Health Equity, Health Disparities, and Community-Engaged Research
description: The Indiana University School of Nursing seeks a highly motivated Postdoctoral Fellow to join the Center for Enhancing Quality of Life in Chronic Illness (CEQL). The fellow will work under the mentorship of Dr. Amy Knopf, an established nurse scientist whose research focuses on health equity, health disparities, social determinants of health, bioethics, and clinical trial access. This fellowship is designed to support the development of an early-career nurse scientist pursuing an independent program of research focused on health equity, health disparities, ethics, and/or population health. The fellow will engage in ongoing research projects while receiving individualized mentorship in research design, data analysis, scientific writing, grantsmanship, community engagement, and academic career development. The Center for Enhancing Quality of Life in Chronic Illness (CEQL) is dedicated to advancing research that improves the quality of life of individuals living with chronic illness. CEQL fosters interdisciplinary collaboration, mentorship, and innovation to address complex health challenges through rigorous scientific inquiry, implementation science, and community engagement. The fellowship provides an opportunity to collaborate with interdisciplinary researchers, community organizations, health systems, and policy partners across Indiana University and beyond while contributing to innovative research that addresses health disparities and promotes equitable health outcomes. Research Focus Areas • Health equity and health disparities • Social determinants of health • Community-engaged and participatory research • Ethics • Clinical trial access, enrollment, and retention • Policy Primary Responsibilities of the Fellow • Develop an individualized career development plan leading toward research independence and external funding. • Conduct independent and collaborative research activities. • Work with faculty mentor on ongoing projects, including: study design, implementation, data collection, and analysis. • Prepare manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed journals. • Present research at IU School of Nursing Research Forums and at regional and national professional conferences.

title: Director, Center for Constitutional Democracy and Professor of Law
department: IU Bloomington Maurer School of Law
description: The Indiana University Maurer School of Law is seeking an outstanding lateral candidate to join our faculty as a tenured professor of law and to serve in the role of Director of the Center for Constitutional Democracy. Founded in 2005, the Center has developed an impactful record of scholarship, teaching, international engagement, and practical assistance focused on constitutional democracy and the rule of law. Its work has included partnerships with scholars, lawyers, judges, public officials, and reformers confronting democratic transition, constitutional reform, institutional fragility, and threats to constitutional government. The Law School seeks a director who will build on this distinguished first chapter and help the Center envision the most important tools to understand and support democratic constitutional orders domestically and abroad in the years ahead. We welcome candidates whose interests connect constitutional democracy with fields such as law and political economy; comparative constitutionalism and democratic resilience; or technology, information systems, and democratic governance. These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive. The Center’s mission extends beyond any single domestic legal issue and calls for a director able to engage constitutional democracy across institutions, disciplines, and national boundaries. The director will oversee the Center’s programs and operations; work with affiliated faculty and students; develop conferences, lectures, and scholarly and applied projects; represent the Center to academic, professional, governmental, philanthropic, and international audiences; open professional opportunities for students, and teach courses related to its mission.

title: Open Rank Professor of Accounting
description: The School of Business at Indiana University Southeast invites applications for an open-rank, tenure-track Professor of Accounting. Start date is August 2027, though an earlier start date may be considered. Rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The school anticipates multiple hires as part of a strategic investment in the continued growth of its accounting program within an AACSB-accredited School of Business. We seek a collaborative, academically engaged faculty member who is excited to contribute to a rapidly growing accounting program serving the Kentuckiana region. Successful candidates will demonstrate a commitment to high-quality teaching, an active scholarly agenda, and an interest in engaging with the regional business and professional community. Responsibilities Successful candidates will: · Teach undergraduate and graduate accounting courses · Maintain an active scholarly agenda consistent with AACSB standards for faculty qualification · Contribute to the continued growth and development of the accounting program Required Qualifications · Earned Ph.D. in Accounting or DBA from an accredited institution by date of appointment (ABD candidates nearing completion may be considered) · Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching and student engagement · Evidence of an active research agenda or ongoing scholarly engagement · Strong communication and interpersonal skills · Commitment to collegiality, collaboration, and community engagement Preferred Qualifications · CPA credential and/or professional accounting experience · Evidence of continued scholarly productivity and potential for publication in peer-reviewed journals · Interest or experience in program growth, curriculum development, and external partnership-building · Evidence of effective engagement with students, employers, and/or professional organizations · Ability to teach in multiple areas such as taxation, auditing, financial accounting, managerial accounting, or accounting information systems Candidates from all areas of accounting specialization are encouraged to apply. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. About the School of Business The School of Business at Indiana University Southeast is AACSB accredited and committed to excellence in teaching, scholarship, professional engagement, and workforce development. The school values faculty scholarship, professional engagement, and student-centered teaching within a collaborative and collegial environment. Faculty benefit from meaningful opportunities to engage with students, contribute to a growing program, and maintain active scholarly agendas while working within a supportive academic community. About IU Southeast and the Kentuckiana Region Indiana University Southeast is a residential regional comprehensive university of approximately 4,000 students located in New Albany, Indiana, just minutes from downtown Louisville, Kentucky. As part of the nine-campus Indiana University system, IU Southeast combines the resources and reputation of a major public university with the accessibility and community focus of a regional campus. The Kentuckiana region offers an exceptional quality of life, combining the affordability and accessibility of Southern Indiana communities with the cultural, recreational, and professional opportunities of the greater Louisville metropolitan area. description: PAUL H. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Medical and Molecular Genetics
description: Postdoctoral Fellow in Neuropsychiatric Genetics The Lai Laboratory in the Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at the Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking highly motivated postdoctoral fellows to join our growing research team. About the Lab Our mission is to uncover the genetic and molecular basis of complex diseases and translate these discoveries into precision medicine. We develop computational and statistical methods while integrating human genetics, single-cell and multi-omics, large-scale biobank resources, and experimental disease models to identify disease mechanisms, discover therapeutic targets, and improve disease prediction, prevention, and treatment. Our research focuses primarily on substance use disorders and neurodegenerative diseases, where we combine genomic discovery with functional validation and clinical investigation to develop clinically actionable polygenic scores, identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets, and advance genetically informed drug repurposing. Our laboratory is supported by multiple NIH grants and internal funding and offers an outstanding collaborative environment with investigators across Indiana University and leading national and international research institutions. We are committed to helping postdoctoral fellows establish independent research programs through strong mentorship, high-impact publications, grant writing, and career development. We especially welcome applicants with backgrounds in psychiatry, neuroscience, or neurobiology who are eager to develop expertise in statistical genetics and computational genomics. Our lab provides a collaborative environment with strong mentorship in quantitative methods, enabling fellows to integrate experimental and computational approaches to study complex brain disorders. Responsibilities The successful candidate will have the opportunity to: Conduct innovative genetic and translational research in substance use disorders or neurodegenerative diseases. Analyze large-scale genomic, single-cell, multi-omics, and biobank datasets. Design research studies, analyze and interpret data, and prepare manuscripts for publication. Present research at national and international conferences and organize scientific symposia. Contribute to fellowship and NIH grant applications. Lead independent research projects while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. Establish new scientific collaborations within and outside Indiana University. Training and Career Development Our goal is to prepare postdoctoral fellows for successful independent research careers. Fellows receive close mentorship and support from the PI, lab mates, and an interdisciplinary network of collaborators in genetics, neuroscience, psychiatry, computational biology and bioinformatics, statistics, and clinical research. Training emphasizes: · Developing an independent research program · Publishing high-impact manuscripts · Scientific communication and leadership · Fellowship and NIH grant writing · Building a long-term academic career This position is particularly well suited for candidates pursuing independent academic careers in psychiatric genetics, neurogenetics, or precision medicine. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. title: Assistant Professor Tenure-Track, Prosthodontics
department: IU Indianapolis Department of Prosthodontics – School of Dentistry
description: The Prosthodontics department in the Indiana University School of Dentistry is seeking qualified applicants for our tenure-track faculty position. This will be a 12-month appointment at the rank of assistant professor at 1.0 FTE. The anticipated start date is negotiable, with a preferred start of September 1, 2026, or as soon thereafter as possible. TEACHING AND LEADERSHIP THAT IMPROVES LIVES Our new faculty member will come with proven expertise in all aspects of prosthodontics, ready to build upon the school’s and campus’s tradition of excellence, advancing scholarship, education, clinical service, and community engagement. Proven expertise in digital methodologies and workflows in prosthodontics, including how those are implemented in didactic, preclinical, and clinical instruction as well as scholarly activity. Additionally, our new faculty member will have a record of creating an environment that promotes collegiality, collaboration, and inclusion among members of various education, research, and service communities. Consistent with our school’s core values, this candidate will demonstrate commitment to serve as a role model and advocate for the ideals of professionalism and high ethical standards in a health science educational setting. Engagement in university service at the department, school, and university levels, including participation in departmental and school governance is expected. You will make a difference weekly by providing preclinical, clinical, and didactic instruction to predoctoral dental students, participating in competency assessments, applying and shaping a comprehensive and robust predoctoral curriculum using state-of-the-art and emerging technologies. Teaching responsibilities may also include course directorship(s). In fulfilling those deliverables, a focus on developing collaboration within and beyond the dental school, and a sustained record of scholarship activities is expected. Our department’s research enterprise naturally includes the fields of education, clinical patient care, dental materials, and implantology. Albeit in a limited capacity, you also might have opportunities to participate in the postdoctoral prosthodontic curriculum in the Advanced Education Program in Prosthodontics. Faculty practice and other revenue-generating opportunities will be considered for eligible candidates. The department is committed to professional growth for each of its team members through professional development. IUSD offers a dynamic learning environment for faculty, in which teaching, research, clinical care, and community service are core to our mission, through clinical programs in Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, Indiana. Our main facility includes a state-of-the-art 45,000–square-foot James J. Fritts DDS Clinical Care Center on the IU Indianapolis campus, adjacent to local hospitals and part of an urban academic health center. Over 12,000 alumni of IUSD are pursuing careers throughout the US and around the world. This commitment is core to our mission through our school-owned clinics and educational programs in Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, Indiana.

title: Tenure-Track Assistant/Associate Professor of Digital Art
department: IU Bloomington Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design
description: The Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design at Indiana University Bloomington invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position with the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor in Digital Art, to begin August 1, 2027. The Digital Art area is seeking an innovative artist, scholar, and educator who integrates advanced technical expertise with creative innovation to foster and support new ideas and forms of exploration. The responsibilities of the position align with expectations for tenure and include maintaining a robust record of scholarly and creative achievement, teaching digital art at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students. Service and administrative responsibilities include committee participation, support and coordination of graduate assistants and area faculty, and contribution to the leadership of the Digital Art area. The candidate should demonstrate strong potential for scholarly and creative achievement and the ability to develop a program of research and creative practice recognized nationally and internationally. The candidate should demonstrate expertise in one or more areas of digital art, including, but not limited to, creative coding; computational, algorithmic and generative art; artifi cial intelligence and machine learning; human-computer interaction; interactive media; game art and animation; virtual, mixed, and augmented reality; computational storytelling; fi lm, video, and audiovisual media; data visualization; digital fabrication; physical computing; wearable technologies; creative technologies, and related emerging practices. Because digital art is a rapidly evolving discipline, the candidate should also demonstrate the capacity to engage critically and creatively with emerging technologies, evolving forms of expression, and changing modes of human experience. Preference will be given to candidates who demonstrate disciplinary excellence, effective teaching experience, and meaningful contributions to the fi eld. We seek a collaborative colleague who can provide leadership, take initiative, and work effectively in a team-based environment. title: Postdoctoral Fellow
description: Postdoctoral Position in Theoretical Nuclear/Hadronic Physics at Indiana University The Nuclear Theory Group in the Department of Physics at Indiana University Bloomington (IU) invites applications for a postdoctoral research position under the supervision of Dr. Sebastian Dawid. The appointment will initially be for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year subject to satisfactory performance and the availability of funding. The start date is flexible and may be arranged by mutual agreement. The position is intended for a researcher interested in developing new theoretical and computational approaches to the strong interaction. Possible directions include the extraction and interpretation of hadronic observables in few-body and multichannel scattering, applications of effective field theories to nuclear and hadronic systems, and formal developments in scattering theory or lattice field theory. The successful candidate will also be encouraged to pursue independent research directions and to collaborate across the IU Nuclear Theory Group. The IU Nuclear Theory Group consists of four faculty members, several postdoctoral researchers, and graduate students. Current research areas include: hadronic amplitude analysis and scattering theory, heavy-ion collisions and the properties of hot QCD matter, hadronic probes of beyond-the-Standard-Model physics, and formal developments in lattice QCD. IU Physics Department also maintains strong ties to leading hadronic and nuclear physics experiments. A Ph.D. in theoretical high-energy or nuclear physics is required by the time of appointment. Research experience in one or more relevant areas, including lattice QCD, effective field theory, and hadronic/nuclear scattering, is preferred. Applications, including a CV, a statement of research interests and plans, and three letters of reference, should be submitted through the application portal located at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/30550 Review of applications will begin on November 15th, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. For questions about the position, please contact Dr. Sebastian Dawid (sdawid@iu.edu) or the IU Physics Department (812-855-1247). title: Postdoctoral Fellow, Physics (Nuclear / Precision Measurement)
department: IU Bloomington Cntr For Explor of En & Matter
description: The IU experimental nuclear physics group has an active program addressing fundamental questions in nuclear physics, particle physics, and astrophysics/cosmology. Group members are leaders in a wide range of experiments, including: investigations of the flavor and spin structure of the nucleon (STAR at RHIC, Belle II at KEK); studies of parity and time reversal violation between nucleons (NIST, SNS, LANSCE, JPARC, JLAB, FRM), measurements of neutrino properties (Fermilab, SNS, SURF, LNGS), neutron decay and neutron interferometry (NIST, LANSCE, SNS, ISIS, ILL), and searches for possible exotic spin-dependent interactions. The group is part of the Center for Exploration of Energy and Matter (CEEM) at IU, which also includes research in theoretical nuclear physics, condensed matter, and radiation effects studies. Group members include professional staff in electronics, mechanical engineering, cryogenic design, and machinists, as well as graduate and undergraduate students. Local facilities include a low-energy neutron source (LENS) available for neutron detector development and testing, high-bay facilities for large-scale fabrication, professional and student machine shops, a polarized 3He lab, a dilution refrigerator, and a vibration isolated lab for weak force measurement. The laboratory possesses infrastructure on a scale which enables us to make major hardware contributions to experiments. Opportunities are available on all major research projects. title: Chief Dental Officer
description: The Indiana University School of Dentistry (IUSD) seeks an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as Chief Dental Officer (CDO). Reporting directly to the Dean and serving as a member of the School's executive leadership and cabinet, the CDO provides strategic leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight for all clinical operations of the School of Dentistry, including predoctoral (DDS), graduate specialty clinics, faculty practices, and hospital-based clinical programs. The CDO is accountable for advancing the School’s clinical mission in patient care, education, quality, safety, compliance, and financial sustainability, while ensuring full alignment with academic priorities, accreditation standards, and the health system environment. The Chief Dental Officer manages the business of our clinical enterprise. This new leader joins the IU School of Dentistry at a pivotal moment for the clinical enterprise. Over the next 5 years there will be implementation of a new PACS and a new patient information system, new Special Care Clinic for adults with disabilities and a new facility to house the OMFS residency program. All of these will rely on collaboration internally and with external partners. Position Summary This role serves as the School’s senior clinical executive, leading the integration of clinical education, patient care delivery, and faculty practice across diverse settings, and representing the School internally and externally on matters related to clinical strategy and performance. The successful candidate will have a strong background in running a multidisciplinary medical/dental operation of $20-$50M in annual revenue as a business, with a primary focus on quality patient care, clinic workflows, and strategic initiatives to increase/maximize revenue. Relevant previous experience includes CEO/COO of a large group practice with multiple locations/service lines or a dental service organization (DSO). Direct reports include the assistant dean of clinical education, the assistant dean of clinical operations, the associate dean and director of dental informatics and digital health, the director of clinical operations , director of Clinical staff, the Director of Clinical Revenue Cycle (dotted line) and the chief infection prevention officer. Key partners include the Chief Fiscal Officer, the Director of Facilities and Auxiliary Services, the Compliance and Privacy Officer, the Associate Dean for Education and Academic Affairs, the Associate Dean for Hospital Affairs, and the chairs of the academic departments who lead clinical faculty who work and teach in the IUSD clinics. Scope of Responsibilities The Chief Dental Officer has enterprise-wide responsibility for: All School of Dentistry clinical operations, including: Predoctoral (DDS) comprehensive care and specialty clinics Graduate and postgraduate specialty clinics Faculty practice operations Hospital-based dental and oral and maxillofacial surgery programs Community-based and extramural clinical education sites Clinical faculty and staff practice environments Clinical quality, safety, compliance, and risk management Clinical financial performance, access, utilization, and growth Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership Provide visionary leadership for the clinical mission of the School of Dentistry, ensuring integration of patient care excellence with educational outcomes and faculty engagement. Develop and execute a comprehensive clinical strateg y aligned with the School’s strategic plan, accreditation requirements, and institutional priorities for education, research, and service. Lead long-range planning for clinical programs, facilities, technologies, and workforce needs. Clinical Operations Oversight Direct and coordinate all clinical enterprises across DDS, graduate, faculty, and hospital-based settings. Ensure efficient, effective, and standardized clinical operations while allowing appropriate differentiation among programs. Oversee clinic scheduling, space utilization, staffing models, and clinical workflows to optimize educational value and patient access. Quality, Safety, and Compliance Establish and maintain a robust clinical quality and patient safety framework across all clinics. Ensure compliance with all regulatory, accreditation, infection control, billing, documentation, and risk management requirements. Promote continuous quality improvement and evidence-based clinical practice. Financial and Performance Stewardship In collaboration with the Chief Fiscal Officer, provide executive oversight of clinical financial performance, including revenue cycle integrity, cost management, and productivity. Partner with finance, operations, and department leadership to ensure sustainable clinical margins that support the School’s academic mission. Use data analytics and performance dashboards to monitor access, productivity, outcomes, and patient experience. Academic and Educational Integration Ensure that clinical operations support high-quality clinical education for DDS, allied dental, and graduate programs. Collaborate closely with Academic Affairs, department chairs, and program directors to align clinical experiences with curricular and competency requirements. Support innovation in clinical education, including digital dentistry, interprofessional care, and emerging care models. Faculty and Staff Leadership In collaboration with the Chair of Comprehensive Care and Allied programs, lead, mentor, and evaluate clinical leaders, including assistant deans, clinic directors, and faculty leaders. Foster a culture of professionalism, accountability, collaboration, and inclusion within clinical environments. Partner with Associate Dean for Faculty Affairs on recruitment, development, evaluation, and succession planning for clinical faculty leadership. External and Institutional Engagement Advance strategic partnerships that enhance clinical education, patient care, and institutional reputation. Represent the School nationally in forums related to academic dentistry, clinical education, and health system integration. Our Commitment As the state’s premier urban research institution, Indiana University is committed to having for all a welcoming campus community that informs academic excellence. We seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to heterogenous, robust, and collaborative learning, working, and patient care environments for all of our students, employees, and patients. IUSD offers a dynamic learning environment for faculty, in which teaching, research, clinical care, and community service are core to our mission through our School-owned clinics and educational programs in Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, Indiana. Our main facility includes a state-of-the-art 45,000–square-foot James J. Fritts DDS Clinical Care Center on the IU-Indianapolis campus, adjacent to local hospitals and part of an urban academic health center. title: Postdoctoral Fellow
description: An NIH funded postdoctoral position is available immediately in the laboratory of Dr. Laura Snell at the Indiana University School of Medicine in Indianapolis, Indiana. The laboratory studies the mechanisms by which chronic viral infections suppress antiviral immunity and drive T cell exhaustion to facilitate viral persistence. We also have a major interest in how chronic viral infections suppress secondary immune responses to enhance the susceptibility to and severity of multiple co-infections and cancers. We have previously demonstrated that chronic viral infection decreases the activation of antigen presenting cells (APCs), resulting in the skewing of newly primed T cell responses for decreased immunity to virus and secondary tumors (see Snell et al. Immunity 2018, Snell et al. Cell Reports 2016). This position focuses on determining the mechanisms by which chronic viral infections drive APC dysfunction / exhaustion, and will use cutting edge technologies to define how these cells become transcriptionally and metabolically reshaped across time. This understanding will have important implications not only for immunity to chronic viruses, but also for subsequent immune responses to co-infections and tumors. The candidate will work with Dr. Snell and her team in a dynamic and collaborative lab environment in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology at Indiana University School of Medicine. In addition to conducting research, the candidate will also be expected to prepare manuscripts, fellowship applications, present findings at internal and external meetings, and help train new grad students / lab members. Salary is commensurate with NIH rates based on experience IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty.
